[2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final")→

The **2008 UEFA Champions League final** was a [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match that took place on 21 May 2008 at the [Luzhniki Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzhniki_Stadium "Luzhniki Stadium") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia, to determine the winner of the [2007–08 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League"). It was contested by [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."), making it an all-English final for the first time in the history of the competition; it was only the third time that two clubs from the same country had contested the final, after [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2000 UEFA Champions League final") and [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final"). It was the first European Cup final played in Russia, and hence the easternmost final in the tournament's history. It also marked the 100th anniversary of Manchester United's [first league triumph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907%E2%80%9308_Football_League "1907–08 Football League"), the 50th anniversary of the [Munich air disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_air_disaster "Munich air disaster"), and the 40th anniversary of United's first European Cup triumph in [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_European_Cup_final "1968 European Cup final"). It was Manchester United's third European Cup final after 1968 and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final"), while it was Chelsea's first.

Manchester United won the match 6–5 on [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"), following a 1–1 draw after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)"). [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") opened the scoring for Manchester United in the 26th minute with a header from a cross by [Wes Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brown "Wes Brown"), but [Frank Lampard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lampard "Frank Lampard") equalised shortly before half-time. The second half and most of extra time passed without incident until Chelsea's [Didier Drogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Drogba "Didier Drogba") was sent off for slapping [Nemanja Vidić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemanja_Vidi%C4%87 "Nemanja Vidić") four minutes from the end. In the penalty shoot-out, Ronaldo missed Manchester United's third kick, giving [John Terry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Terry "John Terry") the chance to win the title for Chelsea, only for his shot to hit the post when he slipped as he was about to kick the ball. [Edwin van der Sar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_van_der_Sar "Edwin van der Sar") then saved [Nicolas Anelka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Anelka "Nicolas Anelka")'s effort from Chelsea's seventh kick to secure Manchester United's third European Cup title.

More than 67,000 people watched the game in the stadium, along with more than 17.5 million television viewers in the United Kingdom and Ireland. In addition to prize money received from earlier in the competition, Manchester United received [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")7 million for winning the final, while Chelsea received €4 million. As winners, Manchester United went on to play in the [2008 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Super_Cup "2008 UEFA Super Cup"), losing 2–1 to [2007–08 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Cup "2007–08 UEFA Cup") winners [Zenit Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg"), and the [2008 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2008 FIFA Club World Cup"), which they won after beating [2008 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Copa_Libertadores "2008 Copa Libertadores") winners [LDU Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LDU_Quito "LDU Quito") 1–0 in the final.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Manchester United and Chelsea had played each other 150 times prior to the Champions League final, including 18 meetings in domestic cup competitions (the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup"), the [Football League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_Cup "EFL Cup") and the [FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Community_Shield "FA Community Shield")). Due to various historical restrictions regarding the number of teams from the same country entering European competitions, they had never met in Europe before. Manchester United held the upper hand in the teams' previous meetings, winning 65 times to Chelsea's 41, with 44 draws. Their cup record was equally good, winning 10 of their 18 meetings, with 4 draws and 4 Chelsea wins. However, honours were even in cup finals, with Manchester United having won the [1994 FA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FA_Cup_final "1994 FA Cup final") 4–0, while Chelsea won the [2007 FA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_FA_Cup_final "2007 FA Cup final") 1–0, the last cup game between the two sides.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5) Manchester United responded to defeat in the 2007 FA Cup Final by beating Chelsea in the [2007 FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_FA_Community_Shield "2007 FA Community Shield") the following August, winning 3–0 on [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") after a 1–1 draw in normal time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-background-6) They went on to claim their 17th league title at the end of the [2007–08 Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League "2007–08 Premier League") season, finishing two points ahead of Chelsea. Both teams went into the final game of the season level on points, but United were ahead of Chelsea because of their superior goal difference, meaning United's 2–0 win against [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on the final day made Chelsea's late draw with [Bolton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolton_Wanderers_F.C. "Bolton Wanderers F.C.") irrelevant.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-8) In the two sides' league meetings that season, United won 2–0 at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") in [Avram Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avram_Grant "Avram Grant")'s first game in charge of Chelsea on 23 September 2007, while Chelsea won 2–1 at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") in the return game on 26 April 2008.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-background-6)

Because of the aforementioned restrictions on entry to UEFA competitions, Manchester United had only met English opposition in Europe twice before,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-10) while Chelsea had far more experience against English opposition, having played 12 matches against compatriot clubs, winning five, drawing five and losing just two.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-12) There had been two previous Champions League finals between teams from the same country: in [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2000 UEFA Champions League final"), when [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") beat fellow Spanish side [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") 3–0 at the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France"); and in [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final"), when Italian sides [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") and [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") played out a 0–0 draw at Old Trafford before Milan won 3–2 on penalties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-13)

Both sides had a connection to the early history of European football; Chelsea were invited to take part in the inaugural European Cup in [1955–56](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955%E2%80%9356_European_Cup "1955–56 European Cup") as champions of England, only to be denied entry by [The Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_League "The Football League"), allowing Manchester United to become the first English entrants in the competition the following season.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14) In February 1958, eight Manchester United players were killed in the [Munich air disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_air_disaster "Munich air disaster"), when the aeroplane carrying their team back from a match in Belgrade crashed while attempting to take off from a refuelling stop in Munich.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-15) Manager [Matt Busby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Busby "Matt Busby") was seriously injured in the crash and almost died as a result, but he rebuilt the team, and in May 1968, Manchester United became the first English winners of the European Cup, beating [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") 4–1 in the [1968 European Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_European_Cup_final "1968 European Cup final").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-16) Chelsea won their first European trophy three years later, when they beat Real Madrid 2–1 in the [1971 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1971 European Cup Winners' Cup final") replay after a 1–1 draw in the first match.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17) Both Chelsea and Manchester United won that same competition during the 1990s – first Manchester United beat [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") 2–1 in the [1991 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1991 European Cup Winners' Cup final")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) (followed by victory over [Red Star Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade "Red Star Belgrade") in the [1991 Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_European_Super_Cup "1991 European Super Cup")),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) and then Chelsea beat [VfB Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VfB_Stuttgart "VfB Stuttgart") in the [1998 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1998 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final")[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20) (followed by victory over Real Madrid in the [1998 Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Super_Cup "1998 UEFA Super Cup"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21) their most recent European success at the time). Manchester United then won their second European Cup the following year, beating [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") in the [1999 Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-22)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Venue")]

[![Image 8: Two large red obelisks supporting a metal gantry. People with umbrellas are passing underneath the gantry.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/2008_0521_Moscow_04.jpg/250px-2008_0521_Moscow_04.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_0521_Moscow_04.jpg)

The entrance to the UEFA Champions Festival in Red Square, Moscow

The [Luzhniki Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzhniki_Stadium "Luzhniki Stadium") in Moscow was selected as the venue for the match at a meeting of the UEFA Executive Committee in [Ljubljana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ljubljana "Ljubljana"), Slovenia, on 4 October 2006. The committee – who decided the venue for the [2009 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final") and the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Cup_final "2008 UEFA Cup final") and [2009 UEFA Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final "2009 UEFA Cup final") at the same meeting – based their decision on a number of factors, including stadium capacity, safety and security facilities, and accessibility.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-moscow_chosen-23) The other venues in contention were the [Estadio Olímpico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_de_La_Cartuja "Estadio de La Cartuja") in Seville, the [Olympiastadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") in Berlin, [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in London, and the [Stadio Olimpico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Olimpico "Stadio Olimpico") in Rome,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-24) which was chosen to host the 2009 final.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-moscow_chosen-23)

This was the easternmost final in the history of the European Cup/UEFA Champions League. It was the first time the competition's showpiece match had been played in Russia, although the Luzhniki Stadium had previously played host to the [1999 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Cup_final "1999 UEFA Cup final"), in which Italian club [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") beat French side [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") 3–0.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25) Because of the difference in time zones, the match kicked off at 22:45 [Moscow Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Time "Moscow Time"), making it the first Champions League final to start on one day and finish in the next.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26)

Originally known as the Grand Arena of the Central Lenin Stadium, the venue opened in 1956 as a new national stadium for the [Soviet Union national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_national_football_team "Soviet Union national football team"). In 1973, it served as the principal venue for the [seventh Summer Universiade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Summer_Universiade "1973 Summer Universiade"), before going on to perform the same function at the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics"). By this point, the stadium's capacity was 103,000; however, renovations in the mid-1990s reduced the capacity to just under 85,000. The stadium was given five-star status by UEFA in 1998, before hosting the UEFA Cup final the following year. To help the stadium cope with cold Russian winters, the grass pitch was replaced by an artificial [FieldTurf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FieldTurf "FieldTurf") surface in 2002.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-27) Although UEFA allowed matches in earlier rounds and [European Championship qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_qualifying "UEFA European Championship qualifying") to be played on the synthetic surface, they mandated that the Champions League final should be played on natural grass. The FieldTurf was removed after Russia's [UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_qualifying "UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying") match against England on 17 October, but the first grass pitch laid was deemed to be too bumpy. Another pitch was laid less than three weeks before the final at a cost of [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")160,000, using turf shipped in from Slovakia, but groundsman Matt Frost said, "I'm totally disappointed with the whole project and what we are presenting for the final."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) UEFA's director of communications, William Gaillard, said the pitch might not look as good as they had hoped to television audiences, but was confident that it would be fine to play on.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29)

### Manchester United

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Manchester United")]

[![Image 37: A wide shot of a football match with Manchester United in red in possession against Lyon in black.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Manutdvslyon.jpg/250px-Manutdvslyon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manutdvslyon.jpg)

Manchester United beat Lyon 1–0 in the second leg of their first knockout round tie at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford").

Manchester United were drawn in Group F along with [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma"), [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP") and [Dynamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-group_draw-30) United won their first five group games; they first travelled to Lisbon, where [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo")'s header secured a 1–0 win against his old club, Sporting. Next was another 1–0 win at home to Roma,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) followed by back-to-back four-goal victories over Dynamo Kyiv (4–2 in Ukraine and 4–0 at Old Trafford).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) United secured top spot in the group with a 2–1 win at home to Sporting in their fifth game.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34) They travelled to Roma for the final group game, in which both teams were already guaranteed to progress; it finished as a 1–1 draw, with [Gerard Piqué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Piqu%C3%A9 "Gerard Piqué") scoring his second goal for the club before [Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mancini_(Brazilian_footballer) "Mancini (Brazilian footballer)")'s equaliser.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) United finished with 16 points, the most of all the group winners.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36)

In the first knockout round, United were drawn against [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_Lyonnais "Olympique Lyonnais"). They drew the away leg 1–1, thanks to a late equaliser from [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-37) before winning the second leg 1–0 – Ronaldo scoring the only goal – to ensure a 2–1 aggregate victory and a place in the quarter-finals,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-38) where they were again drawn against Roma.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39)

The quarter-final matches represented the fifth and sixth times these two clubs had met in Europe in just over 12 months; they had met at the same stage of the previous season's competition and then again in the group stage this season.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-40) United went to Rome and secured a 2–0 win with a first-half header from Ronaldo and a second-half goal tapped in by [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-41) United went on to secure the tie in the second leg with a 1–0 win,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42) their record 11th consecutive home Champions League win.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43)

The semi-final pitted United against Barcelona; the teams had not met since the group stage of the [1998–99 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_UEFA_Champions_League "1998–99 UEFA Champions League"), the last time United won it.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44) The teams also had identical records going into the semi-final, each having won eight and drawn two of their 10 games, scoring 18 goals and conceding just five. The first leg at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") saw United spend most of the game defending, while Barcelona tried to pass the ball around them. United were awarded a penalty in the first minute, but Ronaldo sent the ball wide, hitting the stanchion behind the goal. That was as close as either team got to a goal in the first leg and it ended 0–0.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The second leg at Old Trafford was played at a higher tempo, and United won 1–0 thanks to a goal from [Paul Scholes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Scholes "Paul Scholes") after 14 minutes.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46) This result extended United's consecutive home win record in the Champions League to 12 and ensured that they reached the final unbeaten.

In reaching the final, United won nine and drew three of their 12 matches, dwarfing their record of four wins and six draws in the 10 games they took to reach the final in 1999 (when teams advanced from the group stage directly into the quarter-finals).[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-final_pk_p3-47) United scored 19 goals en route to the final,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-final_pk_p3-47) Ronaldo scoring seven of them, more than any other player.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

### Chelsea

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Chelsea")]

[![Image 38: The Chelsea (blue) and Liverpool (red) teams line up side-by-side in front of banners bearing their club crests and the Champions League final logo. In the background, a flag bearing the Champions League logo is waved over the centre circle, while the main stand is further back, full of spectators. In the foreground, Chelsea fans wave blue flags bearing their club crest.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Chelsea_v_Liverpool_-_The_Lineout.jpg/250px-Chelsea_v_Liverpool_-_The_Lineout.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chelsea_v_Liverpool_-_The_Lineout.jpg)

The Chelsea and Liverpool teams line up ahead of the second leg of their semi-final at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea won 3–2 after extra time (4–3 on aggregate) to qualify for the final.

In the group stage, Chelsea were drawn into Group B, along with [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04") of Germany, [Rosenborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosenborg_BK "Rosenborg BK") of Norway and Spanish club Valencia.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-group_draw-30) Chelsea's first match in the group was against Rosenborg at Stamford Bridge, where they were held to a 1–1 draw.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-49) Two days later, manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") left Chelsea by mutual consent,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-50) and was replaced by their director of football, former [Israel national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_national_football_team "Israel national football team") coach Avram Grant.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-51) Chelsea's second match was against Valencia, whom they beat 2–1, leaving Chelsea with four points from their two matches.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-52) They then faced Schalke in their next two matches; the first was played at Stamford Bridge, with Chelsea winning 2–0,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-53) while the return match in [Gelsenkirchen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelsenkirchen "Gelsenkirchen") ended in a 0–0 draw.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-54) Chelsea's final two matches in their group resulted in a 4–0 victory away to Rosenborg[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55) and a goalless draw at home to Valencia.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56) Chelsea progressed as group winners with 12 points from six games.

Chelsea faced Greek side [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") in the first knockout round. The first leg in Athens ended in a 0–0 draw,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57) but a 3–0 win in the second leg, with goals from [Michael Ballack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ballack "Michael Ballack"), [Frank Lampard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lampard "Frank Lampard") and [Salomon Kalou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salomon_Kalou "Salomon Kalou"), saw Chelsea through to the quarter-finals.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58) There, they were drawn against [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") of Turkey. The first leg was held at the [Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9E%C3%BCkr%C3%BC_Saraco%C4%9Flu_Stadium "Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium") in Istanbul, and ended in a 2–1 defeat, as [Deivid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deivid "Deivid") made up for an early own goal by scoring the winner nine minutes from time after [Colin Kazim-Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Kazim-Richards "Colin Kazim-Richards")' equaliser.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-59) Chelsea won the second leg at Stamford Bridge 2–0, with goals from Ballack and Lampard, to claim a 3–2 aggregate victory over the Turkish side.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-60)

Chelsea faced fellow English club [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in the semi-finals. This was the fourth year in succession that these teams had met in the Champions League, following semi-final meetings in 2004–05 and 2006–07, and two group stage matches in 2005–06.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) The first leg at [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield") was a 1–1 draw, in which Chelsea got a 95th-minute equaliser through a [John Arne Riise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Arne_Riise "John Arne Riise") own goal after [Dirk Kuyt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Kuyt "Dirk Kuyt") had put Liverpool 1–0 up just before half-time.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-62) Chelsea won the second leg 3–2 after extra time, with two goals from [Didier Drogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Drogba "Didier Drogba") and one from Lampard sending the Blues through to the first Champions League final in their history.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-63)

## Pre-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Pre-match")]

### Identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Identity")]

As part of the marketing for each Champions League final since 1997, UEFA commissions a unique design concept inspired by the cultural and historical heritage of the host city. The 2008 final's design was announced on 31 October 2007 in a ceremony at the Luzhniki Stadium, attended by the ambassador for the final, former Russian goalkeeper [Rinat Dasayev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinat_Dasayev "Rinat Dasayev").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) The design was based on a colour scheme of deep red and gold, inspired by the predominant colours of Red Square, the Kremlin and the gold domes of Moscow's cathedrals,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finale-65) and featured images of the Moscow skyline, as well as the UEFA Champions League logo and trophy rendered in a Russian artistic style, with text in a font similar to [Cyrillic script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrillic_script "Cyrillic script").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)

### Ticketing and supporters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Ticketing and supporters")]

[![Image 39: A ticket with a barcode strip on the right. The ticket is white on top half and red on the bottom, separated by images of the Moscow skyline in gold. In the top left corner is the seat information and the top right has the UEFA Champions League logo and the words "Final Moscow 2008".](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Man_utd_%281%29_v_CHELSEA_%281%29_-_C_L_Final_Moscow_ticket.jpg/250px-Man_utd_%281%29_v_CHELSEA_%281%29_-_C_L_Final_Moscow_ticket.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Man_utd_(1)_v_CHELSEA_(1)_-_C_L_Final_Moscow_ticket.jpg)

A ticket from the 2008 UEFA Champions League final

Although the Luzhniki Stadium had a usual capacity of almost 85,000 spectators, that was reduced to 69,500 for the final. Of those tickets, approximately 21,000 were reserved for each finalist club, with a further 10,500 available for purchase by the general public via the UEFA website. Recipients of those tickets were determined by a random ballot following an online application process that ran from 28 February to 19 March 2008. Tickets were available in three categories, priced at [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")80, €140 and €200 depending on their location in the stadium.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-67) UEFA received around 125,000 applications for tickets from the general public over the course of the three-week application process.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-68)

The clubs were able to distribute their tickets however they wished; Manchester United chose to make their allocation available to all Executive Seat Holders and any Season Ticket Holders who had successfully applied for a ticket to at least one of the club's five away Champions League matches between the group stage and the quarter-finals,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-69) while Chelsea opened up applications to all club members and season ticket holders.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-70)

Manchester United chief executive [David Gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Gill_(executive) "David Gill (executive)") expressed disappointment that his club had only been allocated 21,000 tickets for their supporters, claiming that they could have potentially sold up to 100,000.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-71) While Manchester United managed to sell out their entire allocation, UEFA's William Gaillard indicated that Chelsea still had "up to a couple of thousand" tickets unsold the day before the game, despite claims by Chelsea's chief operations officer, Ron Gourlay, to the contrary.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-72)

One of the major concerns for English fans attending the final was the acquisition of [visas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_(document) "Visa (document)") for entry into Russia. However, after a period of negotiations between representatives of Russia, the United Kingdom, UEFA and the two clubs, it was agreed that fans with tickets for the match would not require a visa, provided they were also able to produce a passport with at least six months before expiry and a completed immigration card on entry into Russia.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-73) The visa-free period was initially supposed to run for 72 hours between 19 May and 23 May,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-74) but this was later extended to an eight-day period lasting from 17 to 25 May.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-75) Because of the difficulty and expense of acquiring a ticket and visa, fans who had not already got tickets were advised against travelling to Moscow by Gaillard, who also warned fans about Russia's strict laws regarding the consumption of alcohol.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-76)

Although the two clubs claimed to have sold most of the 42,000 tickets allocated to them, only about 25,000 fans were said to have travelled to Moscow from the United Kingdom, with about 110 charter flights arriving ahead of the game. According to the head of the Russian national tourist office, Mikhail Ignatiev, many fans were put off by the cost of travel and accommodation. Additionally, most of Moscow's hotels were full on the night of the game. As some fans looked to offload tickets to the match, _[The Moscow Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Moscow\_Times "The Moscow Times")_ reported that the black-market price dropped from a high of €2,000 (£1,600) to around €500 (£400), while Russian TV channel [Sport-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport-1_(Russia) "Sport-1 (Russia)") was reporting prices as low as £300 for tickets belonging to fans who had failed to make the trip to Moscow.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-77) Among the celebrities who did not travel were Chelsea supporter and chairman of the [London Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Organising_Committee_of_the_Olympic_and_Paralympic_Games "London Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games") (LOCOG) [Sebastian Coe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Coe "Sebastian Coe"), who had to attend meetings ahead of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), and Manchester United fan and [Simply Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simply_Red "Simply Red") lead singer [Mick Hucknall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Hucknall "Mick Hucknall"), who was due to perform at the [BMW PGA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_PGA_Championship "BMW PGA Championship") at [Wentworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wentworth_Club "Wentworth Club").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-78)

### Related events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Related events")]

As has also taken place for every Champions League final since 1997, a ceremonial handover of the UEFA Champions League trophy was held in the host city; the 2008 ceremony was at the GUM Centre in Moscow's Red Square on 3 April 2008. On behalf of 2007 champions Milan, their technical operations director and former player [Leonardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Ara%C3%BAjo "Leonardo Araújo"), and club director Umberto Gandini presented the trophy to UEFA president [Michel Platini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Platini "Michel Platini"), who passed it on to the [Mayor of Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Moscow "Mayor of Moscow"), [Yury Luzhkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yury_Luzhkov "Yury Luzhkov"), for it to be displayed in five cities around the country – [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), [Yekaterinburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yekaterinburg "Yekaterinburg"), [Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar "Krasnodar"), [Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg") and [Samara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samara,_Russia "Samara, Russia") – before returning to Moscow ahead of the final. Also in attendance at the ceremony were final ambassador Rinat Dasayev and [Russian Football Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union "Russian Football Union") president [Vitaly Mutko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitaly_Mutko "Vitaly Mutko").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-79)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-80)

### Match ball

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Match ball")]

[![Image 40: A football in a perspex cabinet. The ball is predominantly white, patterned with stars in red with gold detailing. In the foreground is a black football boot with red and white trim.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_ball_%28UEFA_Champions_Festival%29.JPG/250px-2008_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_ball_%28UEFA_Champions_Festival%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_ball_(UEFA_Champions_Festival).JPG)

A ball from the 2008 UEFA Champions League final on display at the 2011 UEFA Champions Festival in [Hyde Park, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London "Hyde Park, London")

The match ball for the final was the Adidas Finale Moscow, the eighth in the [Adidas Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas_Finale "Adidas Finale") range. The ball's design was based around the "starball" pattern, inspired by the UEFA Champions League logo; the stars are dark red with gold detailing, tying in with the overall design concept for the final.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finale-65) Technically, the ball is based on the [Adidas Europass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas_Teamgeist#Europass "Adidas Teamgeist"), which was used at [UEFA Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") later that summer; it has the same 14-panel configuration as the [Adidas Teamgeist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas_Teamgeist "Adidas Teamgeist"), but with the proprietary surface texture developed for the Europass. The ball was unveiled at a ceremony in Moscow's [Manezhnaya Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manezhnaya_Square,_Moscow "Manezhnaya Square, Moscow"), attended by UEFA General Secretary [David Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Taylor_(executive) "David Taylor (executive)"), former [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") player and coach [Franz Beckenbauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Beckenbauer "Franz Beckenbauer"), final ambassador Rinat Dasayev and Russian Football Union president Vitaly Mutko.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finale-65)

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Officials")]

[![Image 41: The upper body of a middle-aged white man with brown hair. He is wearing a light-coloured shirt with light blue pinstripes over a white T-shirt with a dark jacket on top. His right hand is inside his jacket and his left hand is holding a piece of paper.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/%C4%BDubo%C5%A1_Miche%C4%BE.JPG/250px-%C4%BDubo%C5%A1_Miche%C4%BE.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%C4%BDubo%C5%A1_Miche%C4%BE.JPG)

Ľuboš Micheľ refereed the final.

The referee for the final was 40-year-old Slovak referee [Ľuboš Micheľ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C4%BDubo%C5%A1_Miche%C4%BE "Ľuboš Micheľ"), the first Slovak to take charge of a European Cup final. His team was completed by fellow Slovak [assistant referees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_referee_(association_football) "Assistant referee (association football)") Roman Slyško and Martin Balko, and [fourth official](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_referee_(association_football)#Fourth_official "Assistant referee (association football)")[Vladimír Hriňák](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_Hri%C5%88%C3%A1k "Vladimír Hriňák").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-referee-81) Having presided over the [2003 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Cup_final "2003 UEFA Cup final"), Micheľ was the second man to referee the finals of both the Champions League and UEFA Cup since the latter changed to a single-legged affair in 1998; the other was [Pierluigi Collina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierluigi_Collina "Pierluigi Collina"), who had been the referee in Manchester United's last Champions League final appearance in 1999.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-82) Micheľ began refereeing in 1987 at the age of 19, and took charge of his first top-flight game in 1993. That same year, he was promoted to the FIFA list of international referees, and in November 1993, he refereed his first international match – a [UEFA Under-21 Championship qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_European_Under-21_Championship_qualification "1994 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification") between [San Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Marino_national_under-21_football_team "San Marino national under-21 football team") and [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_under-21_football_team "England national under-21 football team").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-referee-81)

Micheľ's first UEFA Champions League matches came in the 1998–99 season, including Manchester United's 5–0 win over [Brøndby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Br%C3%B8ndby_IF "Brøndby IF") in the group stage.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-WorldReferee-83) Up to the 2008 final, he had refereed 55 Champions League matches (including qualifying), notably the second leg of the semi-final between Chelsea and Liverpool in [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"), in which Liverpool's [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)") scored a controversial goal that Micheľ chose to allow.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-84) He was also selected to referee at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics"), the [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup") and [2006 FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), and the [European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004 "UEFA Euro 2004") and 2008.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-WorldReferee-83)

[Sir Alex Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson") guaranteed a place in the starting line-up for Paul Scholes, after the midfielder had missed the [1999 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final") through suspension.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-85)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-86) Ferguson made one change from the team that had beaten Wigan Athletic to secure the league title 10 days earlier, with [Owen Hargreaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Hargreaves "Owen Hargreaves") starting on the right side of midfield in a [4–4–2 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%932 "Formation (association football)") in place of [Park Ji-sung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Ji-sung "Park Ji-sung"), who did not even make the substitutes bench despite starting both legs of the semi-final.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-87) Cristiano Ronaldo started on the midfield, where he was pitted against makeshift Chelsea right-back [Michael Essien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Essien "Michael Essien").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-88) This went against the prediction of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s [David Pleat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Pleat "David Pleat"), who thought a duel between Ronaldo and Chelsea left-back [Ashley Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Cole "Ashley Cole") would be key to the final.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-89) Ferguson hoped his substitutes might have a big impact on the match, just as [Teddy Sheringham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Sheringham "Teddy Sheringham") and [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær") did in 1999, when the pair came off the bench to help Manchester United come from behind and beat Bayern Munich.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-90) A week before the game, [Ryan Giggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Giggs "Ryan Giggs") was philosophical about his chances of being included in the starting line-up;[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-91) he was eventually named as one of seven allowed substitutes.

The day before the match, Chelsea manager Avram Grant predicted that the game would throw up few tactical surprises due to the two teams' knowledge of each other from the domestic league.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-92) Like Ferguson, Grant made only one change to the team that started Chelsea's final league game against Bolton 10 days earlier; centre-back [Ricardo Carvalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Carvalho "Ricardo Carvalho") overcame a recurring back injury to start in place of [Alex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_(footballer,_born_June_1982) "Alex (footballer, born June 1982)").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-93) Captain [John Terry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Terry "John Terry") (dislocated elbow) and striker Didier Drogba (knee) also recovered from injuries suffered against Bolton to start the match.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-94)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-95)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-96)[Florent Malouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florent_Malouda "Florent Malouda") retained his place on the left wing ahead of Salomon Kalou, while Michael Essien continued at right-back, rather than in his preferred midfield position, ahead of [Paulo Ferreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Ferreira "Paulo Ferreira") – who did not even make the bench despite starting both legs of the semi-final – and [Juliano Belletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliano_Belletti "Juliano Belletti"). Ashley Cole also started despite hurting his right ankle in training the day before the game under a heavy challenge from [Claude Makélélé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Mak%C3%A9l%C3%A9l%C3%A9 "Claude Makélélé"); Cole's replacement would have likely been [Wayne Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Bridge "Wayne Bridge"), but he recovered sufficiently that Bridge was not even included in the matchday squad as cover.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-97)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Match")]

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 43: A team in blue shakes hands with a team in red. In the foreground are people wearing red shirts and gold shorts assisting with the presentation of the game.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/2008_Champions_League_final_handshakes.jpg/250px-2008_Champions_League_final_handshakes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_Champions_League_final_handshakes.jpg)

Manchester United and Chelsea players shake hands ahead of the match.

After a fairly cagey first 21 minutes, the first major incident of the game occurred when Scholes and Makélélé clashed in mid-air, resulting in both players being booked and Scholes having to leave the field for treatment to a bloody nose.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) The first goal of the game came five minutes later, when an interchange of passes between Scholes and [Wes Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brown "Wes Brown") after a throw-in on the right flank gave Brown time to pick out a cross for Ronaldo, who directed his header past [Petr Čech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_%C4%8Cech "Petr Čech");[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) it was the first time United had scored in the first half of a European final, and the first time Chelsea had gone behind in their three final appearances.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-100) Chelsea almost equalised in the 33rd minute when Frank Lampard's cross was headed back into the goal area by Drogba. United's [Rio Ferdinand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Ferdinand "Rio Ferdinand"), under pressure from Michael Ballack, was forced to head the ball towards his own goal and [Edwin van der Sar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_van_der_Sar "Edwin van der Sar") pulled off a one-handed save to deny Chelsea a goal.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) United spent the rest of the first half pressing for a second goal, and had two good opportunities to extend their lead, but were denied by a double-save from Čech. Wayne Rooney delivered a long ball into the path of Ronaldo and the United goalscorer placed his cross on the head of the diving Carlos Tevez, only for Čech to deny him.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) Chelsea's failure to clear the loose ball gave [Michael Carrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Carrick "Michael Carrick") the chance to extend his side's lead, but Čech was again equal to the task with another save.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99)

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/2008_0521_Moscow_43.jpg/250px-2008_0521_Moscow_43.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_0521_Moscow_43.jpg)

Manchester United in possession

Chelsea survived the pressure, as Tevez failed to connect with a low cross from Rooney,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) and equalised in the final minute of the first half. The goal followed a long-range shot by Michael Essien, which deflected first off [Nemanja Vidić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemanja_Vidi%C4%87 "Nemanja Vidić") and then Ferdinand. The ball's change in direction caused Van der Sar to lose his footing, leaving Lampard, who had made a run from deep, with a simple finish.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) In celebration, Lampard looked up and pointed to the sky with both hands in memory of his mother, Pat, who had died a month earlier.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98) At the end of the first half, Sir Alex Ferguson confronted referee Micheľ, "jabbing out an angry finger and spitting out a few choice words".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-101)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second half")]

[![Image 45](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/2008_Champions_League_final_second_half.jpg/250px-2008_Champions_League_final_second_half.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_Champions_League_final_second_half.jpg)

Manchester United go on the attack.

Lampard's equaliser at the end of the first half led to a transformed Chelsea in the second, and they kept United on the back foot for long periods.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98) Nevertheless, the Red Devils managed to contain most of Chelsea's attacks. Chelsea had a few opportunities to take the lead, with Essien breaking free of United's defence in the 54th minute, only for his left-footed shot to curl well over the goal.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-102) Chelsea's closest opportunity to take the lead came in the 77th minute when a Drogba shot struck the post from 25 yards (23 m) out.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) The Ivorian striker came very close to turning [Joe Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cole "Joe Cole")'s low cross home for the winner four minutes from time, but fired wide. Ryan Giggs was then introduced in place of Scholes, making a record 759th appearance for Manchester United.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)

#### Extra time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Extra time")]

The game moved into extra time, and both teams had chances to score a vital second goal; first, Lampard hit the underside of the bar with a left-footed shot after the ball was played in to him with a disguised pass from Ballack, then Giggs stabbed the ball left-footed towards goal instead of sweeping it with his weaker right foot, only to see it headed off the line by Terry.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bbc_report-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian_report-99) Late in the second half of extra time, the ball was put out of play so players could be treated for cramp. In returning the ball to Chelsea, Tevez put it out for another throw-in deep in Chelsea's half then signalled to his teammates to put pressure on the restart. Terry and Ballack reacted angrily to this and were joined by several of their teammates, while Manchester United's players rushed in to protect Tevez. Ultimately, most of the 22 players were involved in the fracas. Amid the melée, assistant referee Martin Balko saw Drogba slap Nemanja Vidić and reported the incident to referee Micheľ.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-hytner-103) After showing a yellow card to Ballack, Micheľ showed a red card to Drogba for violent conduct, making him only the second player in history to be sent off in a European Cup final after [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") goalkeeper [Jens Lehmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Lehmann "Jens Lehmann") in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2006 UEFA Champions League final").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-104) In preparation for the penalty shoot-out, both clubs made last-minute substitutions; Manchester United brought on [Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_(footballer,_born_1988) "Anderson (footballer, born 1988)") in place of Brown, while Chelsea took off Makélélé in favour of Belletti.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-105)

#### Penalty shoot-out

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Penalty shoot-out")]

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/2008_Champions_League_final_penalties_preparation.jpg/250px-2008_Champions_League_final_penalties_preparation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_Champions_League_final_penalties_preparation.jpg)

The players prepare for the penalty shoot-out.

As the match went to penalties, Rio Ferdinand won the coin toss for Manchester United, and opted for his side to go first in the shoot-out, which would be taken at the end housing the Manchester United fans. Tevez stepped up first and sent Čech the wrong way. Ballack was next up, shooting powerfully past Van der Sar. Carrick buried his spot-kick, as did Belletti with his first touch of the game. The first miss of the shoot-out came from Ronaldo, who characteristically stuttered in his run-up in an attempt to put Čech off, but the goalkeeper dived to his right to save.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-106)

Lampard then put Chelsea 3–2 ahead, but Hargreaves levelled things up with a shot into the top corner. Ashley Cole was the next up, and Van der Sar got a strong hand to the ball but could not keep it out. [Nani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nani_(footballer) "Nani (footballer)") then knew he had to score to keep United in it, and he did, leaving it up to Terry to win the cup for Chelsea; however, he lost his footing when planting his standing foot by the ball,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-107) and, even though Van der Sar was sent the wrong way, his mis-hit effort struck the outside of the right post and went wide.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-108)

With the first penalty of sudden death, Anderson – like Belletti – scored with his first kick of the game. Kalou then sent Van der Sar the wrong way to make it 5–5. Giggs was next up and he was also successful. [Nicolas Anelka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Anelka "Nicolas Anelka") was next, and before his kick, Van der Sar pointed to his left to indicate his prediction that he would kick to that side, as had the six players who took their penalties before him,[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-109) only to correctly dive to his right and make the save to secure European football's top prize for United for the third time in their history.

The **2002 UEFA Cup final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match played on 8 May 2002, between [Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") of the Netherlands and [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") of Germany at the [Feijenoord Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Feyenoord's home ground. It was the 31st [UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Cup_and_Europa_League_finals "List of UEFA Cup and Europa League finals") and it was also the first time that the final had been played at a finalist's home ground since the introduction of single-legged finals in the UEFA Cup in 1998.

Prior to this match, Feyenoord had not won a European trophy since 1974, when they beat [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") to win the [UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_UEFA_Cup_final "1974 UEFA Cup final") four years after winning the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969%E2%80%9370_European_Cup "1969–70 European Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-3) Dortmund, who had already won the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga") title, were hoping to become the second German club, as well as the fourth club overall, to [have won all three pre-1999 major European trophies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_competition_records_and_statistics#List_of_teams_to_have_won_the_three_main_European_club_competitions "UEFA club competition records and statistics") ([European Cup/Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), UEFA Cup/Europa League and the now-defunct [Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup")), having won the [1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965%E2%80%9366_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup") and the [1996–97 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_UEFA_Champions_League "1996–97 UEFA Champions League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-4)

Feyenoord won the match 3–2, marking the first European triumph for a Dutch club in seven years, after Ajax won the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1995 UEFA Champions League final").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-5) As of 2025, this was the most recent European final won by a Dutch club.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Feyenoord and Borussia Dortmund had the two highest scorers in the competition that season in Pierre van Hooijdonk, who finished top of the scoring charts with eight goals, and Márcio Amoroso, who scored five goals overall. Both players added to their tallies during this match with Van Hooijdonk scoring two goals and Amoroso scoring one goal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-topscorer-6)

The match was the last for [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") veteran [Jürgen Kohler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Kohler "Jürgen Kohler"), who was retiring after this match,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) however, the match did not go as intended as he was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejection_(sports) "Ejection (sports)") after 31 minutes. The sides had met twice before in European competition, drawing on both occasions in the [1999–2000 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_UEFA_Champions_League "1999–2000 UEFA Champions League"). Borussia Dortmund were also boosted before kick-off by the news that [Stefan Reuter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Reuter "Stefan Reuter") had passed a late fitness test on his injured back.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)
