### Borussia Dortmund

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Borussia Dortmund")]

See also: [2001–02 Borussia Dortmund season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_Borussia_Dortmund_season "2001–02 Borussia Dortmund season")

Dortmund started off their campaign in the third qualifying of the Champions League round defeating [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") 5–1 over two legs.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-9) BVB needed to win their last group game against [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") to have any chance of making it to the second group stage, but they lost 2–0 and were eliminated from Group B on goal difference, after finishing on the same points as [Boavista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boavista_F.C. "Boavista F.C.").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-11)

Dortmund were drawn against [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Copenhagen "F.C. Copenhagen") of [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") in the third round and won the first leg 1–0 away from home with [Heiko Herrlich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heiko_Herrlich "Heiko Herrlich") scoring in injury time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) The second leg produced the same result, this time, [Jan-Derek Sørensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan-Derek_S%C3%B8rensen "Jan-Derek Sørensen") scored in the 89th minute to secure Dortmund a place in the fourth round.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-13) In the fourth round, Dortmund were drawn against [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille_OSC "Lille OSC") of France, who had also joined the UEFA Cup, after finishing third in their Champions League group.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-15) Dortmund played the first leg away from home and got an away goal, after a 1–1 draw.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-16) Dortmund had opened the scoring in the 67th minute when [Ewerthon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerthon "Ewerthon") scored after a rebound, though the lead only lasted five minutes as [Salaheddine Bassir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaheddine_Bassir "Salaheddine Bassir") scored a half-volley on 72 minutes to tie the game 1–1, going into the second leg in Dortmund. In a rain-soaked second leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion"), the match finished in a 0–0 draw, meaning Borussia went through to the quarter-finals on the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-17)

Dortmund were drawn against [Slovan Liberec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Slovan_Liberec "FC Slovan Liberec") of the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic") in the quarter-finals, the first leg was drawn 0–0 draw in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"). The draw was significant because it was the first time in the competition, that Liberec had failed to win at home.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-18) Dortmund won the second leg 4–0, after goals from [Márcio Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") on 51 minutes, [Jan Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Koller "Jan Koller") on 57 minutes, [Lars Ricken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ricken "Lars Ricken") on 70 minutes, and finally Ewerthon on 89 minutes. Borussia faced stronger opponents in the semi-finals, when they were drawn with the then five times champions of Europe, [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Semi-finals-19) Nevertheless, Borussia won the first leg 4–0, after a hat-trick from Márcio Amoroso, and a goal on 63 minutes from [Jörg Heinrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B6rg_Heinrich "Jörg Heinrich").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Amoroso_puts_Dortmund_in_control-20) Milan manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") admitted he was not surprised with the result, stating that, "We knew they had quick strikers. I am more surprised by the terrible performance of our team. The problem stemmed from the wings. I had no reason to change the team because [Rui Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rui_Costa "Rui Costa") has not trained for 10 days. It will be very difficult but it is our duty to give it our best and to try and qualify."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Amoroso_puts_Dortmund_in_control-20) In the second leg, Milan won 3–1, with [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi"), and [Cosmin Contra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmin_Contra "Cosmin Contra") scoring within 18 minutes. However, Milan did not get their third goal until injury time when [Serginho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serginho_(footballer,_born_1971) "Serginho (footballer, born 1971)") scored a penalty after Inzaghi was adjudged to have been pulled back by [Christoph Metzelder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christoph_Metzelder "Christoph Metzelder"). With Milan still needing one goal to force extra time, Lars Ricken scored for Dortmund in the fourth minute of injury time to put the club into their first European final since winning the [1997 Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "1997 UEFA Champions League Final").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-21)

### Feyenoord

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Feyenoord")]

See also: [2001–02 Feyenoord season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_Feyenoord_season "2001–02 Feyenoord season")

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg/250px-De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg)

De Kuip Stadium venue of the 2002 UEFA Cup Final

Feyenoord went straight to the first group stage of the Champions League after finishing second in the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") but were eliminated after only winning one game, and finishing six points behind [Sparta Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Sparta_Prague "AC Sparta Prague"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-22) and were consequently drawn against [SC Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Freiburg "SC Freiburg") of Germany in the third round of the UEFA Cup.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-23) Feyenoord won the first leg 1–0, after a late goal from [Shinji Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinji_Ono "Shinji Ono").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-24) The second leg was drawn 2–2, however Feyenoord came close to going out, as Freiburg took a 2–0 lead on 49 minutes with goals from [Sebastian Kehl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Kehl "Sebastian Kehl") and [Levan Kobiashvili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levan_Kobiashvili "Levan Kobiashvili"), to make the aggregate score 2–1 in Freiburg's favour. But on 57 minutes, [Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") pulled a goal back, to make it 2–2 on aggregate, which would see Feyenoord going through due to the away goal rule.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-25) Feyenoord secured their place in the fourth round when [Leonardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Santiago "Leonardo Santiago") scored in the 86th minute.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-26) Feyenoord faced [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.") of Scotland in the fourth round with the tie proving to be a close affair. The first leg ended 1–1, in [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), Feyenoord had gone ahead on 72 minutes through Shinji Ono, but Rangers equalised after [Peter Løvenkrands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_L%C3%B8venkrands "Peter Løvenkrands") was brought down by [Glenn Loovens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Loovens "Glenn Loovens") on 81 minutes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-27)[Barry Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Ferguson "Barry Ferguson") scored the subsequent penalty.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-28) The second leg in Rotterdam ended 3–2 in Feyenoord's favor, the match was notable for the sending off of one player on each side [Patrick Paauwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Paauwe "Patrick Paauwe") for Feyenoord and [Neil McCann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_McCann "Neil McCann") for Rangers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-29)

Feyenoord were paired with fellow Dutch side [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven") in the quarter-finals, and the tie came down to a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)"), which Feyenoord won 5–4.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-30) The first leg was drawn 1–1 with Feyenoord taking the lead in first half injury time through Pierre van Hooijdonk.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-31) PSV equalised two minutes after the restart when [Mateja Kežman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateja_Ke%C5%BEman "Mateja Kežman") scored on 47 minutes.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-32) The second leg was again drawn 1–1, with PSV taking the lead on 75 minutes, when [Mark van Bommel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_van_Bommel "Mark van Bommel") scored from outside the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) That looked to have sent PSV into the semi-finals, but with seconds remaining, Van Hooijdonk scored from [Johan Elmander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Elmander "Johan Elmander")'s cross to send the tie into extra-time.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) PSV were reduced to ten men in extra time when Van Bommel was sent off for a second bookable offence but they still managed to hold out for the extra 30 minutes to force a penalty shootout.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) All penalties were converted until [Giorgi Gakhokidze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgi_Gakhokidze "Giorgi Gakhokidze") stepped up, and saw his penalty saved. Feyenoord converted their subsequent penalties, with Van Hooijdonk putting away the vital fifth penalty.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-34) Like Borussia, Feyenoord faced opposition from the city of [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") in the semi-finals, in the shape of [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Semi-finals-19) Around 10,000 Feyenoord fans made the trip to the scene of Feyenoord's [1970 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_European_Cup_Final "1970 European Cup Final") victory for the first leg.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-35) Feyenoord won the first leg 1–0 to gain a vital away goal after [Iván Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iv%C3%A1n_C%C3%B3rdoba "Iván Córdoba") scored an [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-36) The second leg started well for Feyenoord after going 2–0 up inside 34 minutes, due to goals from Van Hooijdonk and [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson"), to put Feyenoord 3–0 up on aggregate.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-37) Inter came back into the tie in the last minutes when they pulled two goals back through [Javier Zanetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Zanetti "Javier Zanetti") and [Mohamed Kallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Kallon "Mohamed Kallon"), but Feyenoord secured their place in the final with a 3–2 aggregate victory.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-38)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Match")]

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg/250px-FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg)

[Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") scored twice for Feyenoord in the first half

The first shot on goal was registered by [Bonaventure Kalou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonaventure_Kalou "Bonaventure Kalou"), who forced a save out of [Jens Lehmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Lehmann "Jens Lehmann").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) After 10 minutes, [Shinji Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinji_Ono "Shinji Ono") spotted Lehmann off his line but sent his lofted shot wide of the target.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) This sparked Dortmund into life; they were thwarted when [Patrick Paauwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Paauwe "Patrick Paauwe") intercepted [Jan Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Koller "Jan Koller") just as he was looking to get his shot away. On 15 minutes, they came even closer to breaking the deadlock, when Amoroso picked out [Tomáš Rosický](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Rosick%C3%BD "Tomáš Rosický"); however, he shot straight at [Edwin Zoetebier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Zoetebier "Edwin Zoetebier").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) On 19 minutes, [Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") came close to scoring with a free kick, which hit the right-hand post. Feyenoord's [Tomasz Rząsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomasz_Rz%C4%85sa "Tomasz Rząsa") was then booked for dissent on 23 minutes, and following the resulting free kick, [Evanílson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan%C3%ADlson_(footballer,_born_1975) "Evanílson (footballer, born 1975)") came close to scoring, though his shot went over the crossbar after [Ewerthon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerthon "Ewerthon")'s pass had sent him through.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)

The deadlock was broken on 31 minutes when Jürgen Kohler, who was playing his last game for Dortmund, pulled back [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson") in the Dortmund penalty area; Kohler was shown a straight red card, and Van Hooijdonk converted the subsequent penalty, dispatching it to [Jens Lehmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Lehmann "Jens Lehmann")'s right hand side.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Feyenoord made it 2–0 seven minutes later when Van Hooijdonk, scored a free kick from the edge of the area, his eighth goal over the course of the season's competition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Second half")]

After half time, Dortmund were handed a way back into the match when [Márcio Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") was brought down by Patrick Paauwe.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Paauwe was spared Kohler's fate as he only received a yellow card. Amoroso scored the following penalty and the score was 2–1.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Two minutes later, Amoroso was cautioned for diving in an attempt to win another spot kick. Just three minutes after Dortmund scored, Jon Dahl Tomasson who was playing his last game for Feyenoord before his move to Milan,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) scored after beating the offside trap, and being put through by Shinji Ono. Dortmund once again found a way back into the match when Jan Koller volleyed home his shot from 25 metres on 58 minutes, after capitalizing on a weak defensive header.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-39) Dortmund now assumed the ascendancy with attack after attack, whilst Feyenoord seemed content to sit back and try to see the game out. Dortmund tried everything to find the equaliser replacing [Lars Ricken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ricken "Lars Ricken") with [Jörg Heinrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B6rg_Heinrich "Jörg Heinrich"), and Ewerthon was replaced by [Otto Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Addo "Otto Addo"), however it was to no avail as Feyenoord saw the game out to win 3–2 and continue their streak of never losing a European final.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-40)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Post-match")]

A huge party erupted both inside and outside De Kuip not only because of the title, but also because the final was held two days after Rotterdam's politician [Pim Fortuyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pim_Fortuyn "Pim Fortuyn") was murdered.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-44) Many [Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") fans were still full of emotion before and after the match. As a result of Fortuyn's murder, the victory was not officially celebrated in Coolsingel Square with their fans.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-45) During Feyenoord's UEFA Cup run, a parody was launched of the song "Put Your Hands Up" by Black & White Brothers, "Put Your Hands Up for Pi-Air", as a tribute to Pierre van Hooijdonk.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-46)

The **2002 UEFA Cup final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match played on 8 May 2002, between [Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") of the Netherlands and [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") of Germany at the [Feijenoord Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Feyenoord's home ground. It was the 31st [UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Cup_and_Europa_League_finals "List of UEFA Cup and Europa League finals") and it was also the first time that the final had been played at a finalist's home ground since the introduction of single-legged finals in the UEFA Cup in 1998.

Prior to this match, Feyenoord had not won a European trophy since 1974, when they beat [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") to win the [UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_UEFA_Cup_final "1974 UEFA Cup final") four years after winning the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969%E2%80%9370_European_Cup "1969–70 European Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-3) Dortmund, who had already won the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga") title, were hoping to become the second German club, as well as the fourth club overall, to [have won all three pre-1999 major European trophies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_competition_records_and_statistics#List_of_teams_to_have_won_the_three_main_European_club_competitions "UEFA club competition records and statistics") ([European Cup/Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), UEFA Cup/Europa League and the now-defunct [Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup")), having won the [1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965%E2%80%9366_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup") and the [1996–97 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_UEFA_Champions_League "1996–97 UEFA Champions League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-4)

Feyenoord won the match 3–2, marking the first European triumph for a Dutch club in seven years, after Ajax won the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1995 UEFA Champions League final").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-5) As of 2025, this was the most recent European final won by a Dutch club.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Feyenoord and Borussia Dortmund had the two highest scorers in the competition that season in Pierre van Hooijdonk, who finished top of the scoring charts with eight goals, and Márcio Amoroso, who scored five goals overall. Both players added to their tallies during this match with Van Hooijdonk scoring two goals and Amoroso scoring one goal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-topscorer-6)

The match was the last for [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") veteran [Jürgen Kohler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Kohler "Jürgen Kohler"), who was retiring after this match,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) however, the match did not go as intended as he was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejection_(sports) "Ejection (sports)") after 31 minutes. The sides had met twice before in European competition, drawing on both occasions in the [1999–2000 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_UEFA_Champions_League "1999–2000 UEFA Champions League"). Borussia Dortmund were also boosted before kick-off by the news that [Stefan Reuter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Reuter "Stefan Reuter") had passed a late fitness test on his injured back.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)

### Borussia Dortmund

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Borussia Dortmund")]

See also: [2001–02 Borussia Dortmund season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_Borussia_Dortmund_season "2001–02 Borussia Dortmund season")

Dortmund started off their campaign in the third qualifying of the Champions League round defeating [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") 5–1 over two legs.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-9) BVB needed to win their last group game against [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") to have any chance of making it to the second group stage, but they lost 2–0 and were eliminated from Group B on goal difference, after finishing on the same points as [Boavista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boavista_F.C. "Boavista F.C.").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-11)

Dortmund were drawn against [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Copenhagen "F.C. Copenhagen") of [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") in the third round and won the first leg 1–0 away from home with [Heiko Herrlich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heiko_Herrlich "Heiko Herrlich") scoring in injury time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) The second leg produced the same result, this time, [Jan-Derek Sørensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan-Derek_S%C3%B8rensen "Jan-Derek Sørensen") scored in the 89th minute to secure Dortmund a place in the fourth round.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-13) In the fourth round, Dortmund were drawn against [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille_OSC "Lille OSC") of France, who had also joined the UEFA Cup, after finishing third in their Champions League group.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-15) Dortmund played the first leg away from home and got an away goal, after a 1–1 draw.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-16) Dortmund had opened the scoring in the 67th minute when [Ewerthon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerthon "Ewerthon") scored after a rebound, though the lead only lasted five minutes as [Salaheddine Bassir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaheddine_Bassir "Salaheddine Bassir") scored a half-volley on 72 minutes to tie the game 1–1, going into the second leg in Dortmund. In a rain-soaked second leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion"), the match finished in a 0–0 draw, meaning Borussia went through to the quarter-finals on the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-17)

Dortmund were drawn against [Slovan Liberec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Slovan_Liberec "FC Slovan Liberec") of the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic") in the quarter-finals, the first leg was drawn 0–0 draw in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"). The draw was significant because it was the first time in the competition, that Liberec had failed to win at home.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-18) Dortmund won the second leg 4–0, after goals from [Márcio Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") on 51 minutes, [Jan Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Koller "Jan Koller") on 57 minutes, [Lars Ricken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ricken "Lars Ricken") on 70 minutes, and finally Ewerthon on 89 minutes. Borussia faced stronger opponents in the semi-finals, when they were drawn with the then five times champions of Europe, [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Semi-finals-19) Nevertheless, Borussia won the first leg 4–0, after a hat-trick from Márcio Amoroso, and a goal on 63 minutes from [Jörg Heinrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B6rg_Heinrich "Jörg Heinrich").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Amoroso_puts_Dortmund_in_control-20) Milan manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") admitted he was not surprised with the result, stating that, "We knew they had quick strikers. I am more surprised by the terrible performance of our team. The problem stemmed from the wings. I had no reason to change the team because [Rui Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rui_Costa "Rui Costa") has not trained for 10 days. It will be very difficult but it is our duty to give it our best and to try and qualify."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Amoroso_puts_Dortmund_in_control-20) In the second leg, Milan won 3–1, with [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi"), and [Cosmin Contra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmin_Contra "Cosmin Contra") scoring within 18 minutes. However, Milan did not get their third goal until injury time when [Serginho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serginho_(footballer,_born_1971) "Serginho (footballer, born 1971)") scored a penalty after Inzaghi was adjudged to have been pulled back by [Christoph Metzelder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christoph_Metzelder "Christoph Metzelder"). With Milan still needing one goal to force extra time, Lars Ricken scored for Dortmund in the fourth minute of injury time to put the club into their first European final since winning the [1997 Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "1997 UEFA Champions League Final").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-21)

### Feyenoord

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Feyenoord")]

See also: [2001–02 Feyenoord season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_Feyenoord_season "2001–02 Feyenoord season")

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg/250px-De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:De_Kuip_Rotterdam_The_Netherlands.jpg)

De Kuip Stadium venue of the 2002 UEFA Cup Final

Feyenoord went straight to the first group stage of the Champions League after finishing second in the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") but were eliminated after only winning one game, and finishing six points behind [Sparta Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Sparta_Prague "AC Sparta Prague"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-22) and were consequently drawn against [SC Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Freiburg "SC Freiburg") of Germany in the third round of the UEFA Cup.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-23) Feyenoord won the first leg 1–0, after a late goal from [Shinji Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinji_Ono "Shinji Ono").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-24) The second leg was drawn 2–2, however Feyenoord came close to going out, as Freiburg took a 2–0 lead on 49 minutes with goals from [Sebastian Kehl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Kehl "Sebastian Kehl") and [Levan Kobiashvili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levan_Kobiashvili "Levan Kobiashvili"), to make the aggregate score 2–1 in Freiburg's favour. But on 57 minutes, [Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") pulled a goal back, to make it 2–2 on aggregate, which would see Feyenoord going through due to the away goal rule.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-25) Feyenoord secured their place in the fourth round when [Leonardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Santiago "Leonardo Santiago") scored in the 86th minute.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-26) Feyenoord faced [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.") of Scotland in the fourth round with the tie proving to be a close affair. The first leg ended 1–1, in [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), Feyenoord had gone ahead on 72 minutes through Shinji Ono, but Rangers equalised after [Peter Løvenkrands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_L%C3%B8venkrands "Peter Løvenkrands") was brought down by [Glenn Loovens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Loovens "Glenn Loovens") on 81 minutes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-27)[Barry Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Ferguson "Barry Ferguson") scored the subsequent penalty.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-28) The second leg in Rotterdam ended 3–2 in Feyenoord's favor, the match was notable for the sending off of one player on each side [Patrick Paauwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Paauwe "Patrick Paauwe") for Feyenoord and [Neil McCann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_McCann "Neil McCann") for Rangers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-29)

Feyenoord were paired with fellow Dutch side [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven") in the quarter-finals, and the tie came down to a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)"), which Feyenoord won 5–4.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-30) The first leg was drawn 1–1 with Feyenoord taking the lead in first half injury time through Pierre van Hooijdonk.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-31) PSV equalised two minutes after the restart when [Mateja Kežman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateja_Ke%C5%BEman "Mateja Kežman") scored on 47 minutes.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-32) The second leg was again drawn 1–1, with PSV taking the lead on 75 minutes, when [Mark van Bommel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_van_Bommel "Mark van Bommel") scored from outside the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) That looked to have sent PSV into the semi-finals, but with seconds remaining, Van Hooijdonk scored from [Johan Elmander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Elmander "Johan Elmander")'s cross to send the tie into extra-time.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) PSV were reduced to ten men in extra time when Van Bommel was sent off for a second bookable offence but they still managed to hold out for the extra 30 minutes to force a penalty shootout.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Feyenoord-33) All penalties were converted until [Giorgi Gakhokidze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgi_Gakhokidze "Giorgi Gakhokidze") stepped up, and saw his penalty saved. Feyenoord converted their subsequent penalties, with Van Hooijdonk putting away the vital fifth penalty.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-34) Like Borussia, Feyenoord faced opposition from the city of [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") in the semi-finals, in the shape of [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Semi-finals-19) Around 10,000 Feyenoord fans made the trip to the scene of Feyenoord's [1970 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_European_Cup_Final "1970 European Cup Final") victory for the first leg.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-35) Feyenoord won the first leg 1–0 to gain a vital away goal after [Iván Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iv%C3%A1n_C%C3%B3rdoba "Iván Córdoba") scored an [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-36) The second leg started well for Feyenoord after going 2–0 up inside 34 minutes, due to goals from Van Hooijdonk and [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson"), to put Feyenoord 3–0 up on aggregate.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-37) Inter came back into the tie in the last minutes when they pulled two goals back through [Javier Zanetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Zanetti "Javier Zanetti") and [Mohamed Kallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Kallon "Mohamed Kallon"), but Feyenoord secured their place in the final with a 3–2 aggregate victory.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-38)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Match")]

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg/250px-FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FvS_Feyenoord_Pierre_van_Hooijdonk_01.jpg)

[Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") scored twice for Feyenoord in the first half

The first shot on goal was registered by [Bonaventure Kalou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonaventure_Kalou "Bonaventure Kalou"), who forced a save out of [Jens Lehmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Lehmann "Jens Lehmann").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) After 10 minutes, [Shinji Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinji_Ono "Shinji Ono") spotted Lehmann off his line but sent his lofted shot wide of the target.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) This sparked Dortmund into life; they were thwarted when [Patrick Paauwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Paauwe "Patrick Paauwe") intercepted [Jan Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Koller "Jan Koller") just as he was looking to get his shot away. On 15 minutes, they came even closer to breaking the deadlock, when Amoroso picked out [Tomáš Rosický](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Rosick%C3%BD "Tomáš Rosický"); however, he shot straight at [Edwin Zoetebier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Zoetebier "Edwin Zoetebier").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) On 19 minutes, [Pierre van Hooijdonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_van_Hooijdonk "Pierre van Hooijdonk") came close to scoring with a free kick, which hit the right-hand post. Feyenoord's [Tomasz Rząsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomasz_Rz%C4%85sa "Tomasz Rząsa") was then booked for dissent on 23 minutes, and following the resulting free kick, [Evanílson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan%C3%ADlson_(footballer,_born_1975) "Evanílson (footballer, born 1975)") came close to scoring, though his shot went over the crossbar after [Ewerthon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewerthon "Ewerthon")'s pass had sent him through.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)

The deadlock was broken on 31 minutes when Jürgen Kohler, who was playing his last game for Dortmund, pulled back [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson") in the Dortmund penalty area; Kohler was shown a straight red card, and Van Hooijdonk converted the subsequent penalty, dispatching it to [Jens Lehmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Lehmann "Jens Lehmann")'s right hand side.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Feyenoord made it 2–0 seven minutes later when Van Hooijdonk, scored a free kick from the edge of the area, his eighth goal over the course of the season's competition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Second half")]

After half time, Dortmund were handed a way back into the match when [Márcio Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") was brought down by Patrick Paauwe.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Paauwe was spared Kohler's fate as he only received a yellow card. Amoroso scored the following penalty and the score was 2–1.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) Two minutes later, Amoroso was cautioned for diving in an attempt to win another spot kick. Just three minutes after Dortmund scored, Jon Dahl Tomasson who was playing his last game for Feyenoord before his move to Milan,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7) scored after beating the offside trap, and being put through by Shinji Ono. Dortmund once again found a way back into the match when Jan Koller volleyed home his shot from 25 metres on 58 minutes, after capitalizing on a weak defensive header.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-39) Dortmund now assumed the ascendancy with attack after attack, whilst Feyenoord seemed content to sit back and try to see the game out. Dortmund tried everything to find the equaliser replacing [Lars Ricken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ricken "Lars Ricken") with [Jörg Heinrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B6rg_Heinrich "Jörg Heinrich"), and Ewerthon was replaced by [Otto Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Addo "Otto Addo"), however it was to no avail as Feyenoord saw the game out to win 3–2 and continue their streak of never losing a European final.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-Final-7)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-40)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2002_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Post-match")]

A huge party erupted both inside and outside De Kuip not only because of the title, but also because the final was held two days after Rotterdam's politician [Pim Fortuyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pim_Fortuyn "Pim Fortuyn") was murdered.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-44) Many [Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") fans were still full of emotion before and after the match. As a result of Fortuyn's murder, the victory was not officially celebrated in Coolsingel Square with their fans.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-45) During Feyenoord's UEFA Cup run, a parody was launched of the song "Put Your Hands Up" by Black & White Brothers, "Put Your Hands Up for Pi-Air", as a tribute to Pierre van Hooijdonk.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-46)

The [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") is a seasonal [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition established in 1955.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-History-1) Prior to the [1992–93 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_UEFA_Champions_League "1992–93 UEFA Champions League"), the tournament was named the European Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-History-1) The UEFA Champions League is open to the league champions of all [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") (Union of European Football Associations) member associations (except [Liechtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liechtenstein "Liechtenstein"), which has no league competition), as well as to the clubs finishing from second to fourth positions in the strongest leagues.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-2) Originally, only the champions of their respective national league and the defending champions of the competition were allowed to participate. However, this was changed in 1997 to allow the runners-up of the stronger leagues to compete as well, and again in 1999 when third and fourth-placed teams of the said leagues also became eligible.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-3) In the Champions League era, the defending champions of the competition did not automatically qualify until the rules were changed in 2005 to allow title holders [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") to enter the competition.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-4)

Teams that have won the UEFA Champions League three consecutive times, or five times overall, receive a [multiple-winner badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Multiple-winner_badge "European Champion Clubs' Cup").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-5) Six teams have earned this privilege: [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax"), [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich"), [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), Liverpool, and [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-7) Until 2009, clubs that had earned that badge were allowed to keep the [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and a new one was commissioned;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-8) since 2009, the winning team each year has received a full-size replica of the trophy, while the original is retained by UEFA.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-9)

A total of 24 clubs have won the Champions League/European Cup. Real Madrid holds the record for the most victories, having won the competition 15 times, including the inaugural edition. They have also won the competition the most consecutive times, with five straight titles from 1956 to 1960. [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") have been runners-up the most times, losing seven finals. [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") is the only team to reach three finals without having won the trophy while [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_Reims "Stade de Reims"), [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF"), and [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") have finished as runners-up twice without winning. Spain has provided the most champions, with twenty wins from two clubs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-uefa-10) England have produced fifteen winners from a record six clubs and Italy have produced twelve winners from three clubs. English teams were banned from the competition for five years following the [Heysel disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster "Heysel Stadium disaster") in 1985.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-11) The current champions are [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), who beat Arsenal 4–3 on [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") following a 1–1 draw after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2026 UEFA Champions League final").

While the venue for the final is chosen well in advance, on four occasions clubs have reached a final scheduled to be played in their own stadium; Real Madrid won their second European Cup in the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") in 1957, while in 1965 Inter Milan also won their second title in the final at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"). In 1984, the [Stadio Olimpico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Olimpico "Stadio Olimpico") in Rome was the venue and saw [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") defeated on penalties by Liverpool, while 2012 saw the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena") host the final between Bayern Munich and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."), which the English club also won on penalties.

The [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") is a seasonal [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition established in 1955.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-History-1) Prior to the [1992–93 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_UEFA_Champions_League "1992–93 UEFA Champions League"), the tournament was named the European Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-History-1) The UEFA Champions League is open to the league champions of all [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") (Union of European Football Associations) member associations (except [Liechtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liechtenstein "Liechtenstein"), which has no league competition), as well as to the clubs finishing from second to fourth positions in the strongest leagues.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-2) Originally, only the champions of their respective national league and the defending champions of the competition were allowed to participate. However, this was changed in 1997 to allow the runners-up of the stronger leagues to compete as well, and again in 1999 when third and fourth-placed teams of the said leagues also became eligible.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-3) In the Champions League era, the defending champions of the competition did not automatically qualify until the rules were changed in 2005 to allow title holders [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") to enter the competition.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-4)

Teams that have won the UEFA Champions League three consecutive times, or five times overall, receive a [multiple-winner badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Multiple-winner_badge "European Champion Clubs' Cup").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-5) Six teams have earned this privilege: [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax"), [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich"), [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), Liverpool, and [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-7) Until 2009, clubs that had earned that badge were allowed to keep the [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and a new one was commissioned;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-8) since 2009, the winning team each year has received a full-size replica of the trophy, while the original is retained by UEFA.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-9)

A total of 24 clubs have won the Champions League/European Cup. Real Madrid holds the record for the most victories, having won the competition 15 times, including the inaugural edition. They have also won the competition the most consecutive times, with five straight titles from 1956 to 1960. [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") have been runners-up the most times, losing seven finals. [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") is the only team to reach three finals without having won the trophy while [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_Reims "Stade de Reims"), [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF"), and [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") have finished as runners-up twice without winning. Spain has provided the most champions, with twenty wins from two clubs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-uefa-10) England have produced fifteen winners from a record six clubs and Italy have produced twelve winners from three clubs. English teams were banned from the competition for five years following the [Heysel disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster "Heysel Stadium disaster") in 1985.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Champions_League_finals#cite_note-11) The current champions are [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), who beat Arsenal 4–3 on [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") following a 1–1 draw after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2026 UEFA Champions League final").

While the venue for the final is chosen well in advance, on four occasions clubs have reached a final scheduled to be played in their own stadium; Real Madrid won their second European Cup in the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") in 1957, while in 1965 Inter Milan also won their second title in the final at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"). In 1984, the [Stadio Olimpico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Olimpico "Stadio Olimpico") in Rome was the venue and saw [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") defeated on penalties by Liverpool, while 2012 saw the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena") host the final between Bayern Munich and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."), which the English club also won on penalties.

The [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"), formerly the UEFA Cup, is an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition established in 1971 by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-rsssf-1) It is considered the second most important international competition for European clubs, after the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). Clubs qualify for the Europa League based on their performance in national leagues and cup competitions. For the first 25 years of the competition, the final was contested over [two legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_match "Two-legged match"), one at each participating club's stadium, but in 1998, [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") defeated [Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Lazio "SS Lazio") in the competition's first single-legged final held at a neutral venue, the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes") in Paris.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-2)[Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") won the [inaugural competition in 1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971%E2%80%9372_UEFA_Cup "1971–72 UEFA Cup"), defeating [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") 3–2 on aggregate.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-3) Eleven finals have featured teams from the same national association: Italy ([1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_UEFA_Cup_final "1990 UEFA Cup final"), [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_UEFA_Cup_final "1991 UEFA Cup final"), [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Cup_final "1995 UEFA Cup final") and [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Cup_final "1998 UEFA Cup final")), England ([1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_UEFA_Cup_final "1972 UEFA Cup final"), [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2019 UEFA Europa League final") and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2025 UEFA Europa League final")), Spain ([2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Cup_final "2007 UEFA Cup final") and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2012 UEFA Europa League final")), Germany ([1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_UEFA_Cup_final "1980 UEFA Cup final")) and Portugal ([2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2011 UEFA Europa League final")).

[Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") holds the record for the most victories, having won the competition seven times since its inception.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-4)[Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") (winners in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_UEFA_Cup_final "1985 UEFA Cup final") and [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_UEFA_Cup_final "1986 UEFA Cup final")) and Sevilla (winners in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Cup_final "2006 UEFA Cup final") and 2007, and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2014 UEFA Europa League final"), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2015 UEFA Europa League final") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2016 UEFA Europa League final")) are the only teams to have retained their title. The competition has been won fourteen times by teams from Spain, more than any other country.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-rsssf-1) The last champions before the UEFA Cup was renamed to UEFA Europa League were [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk"), who beat [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") 2–1 after extra time in the [2009 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final "2009 UEFA Cup final").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-5)[Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") and [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") have lost the most finals, with three losses in the competition. The current champions are [Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C."), who defeated [SC Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Freiburg "SC Freiburg") 3–0 in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2026 UEFA Europa League final").

While the [Inter-Cities Fairs Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup "Inter-Cities Fairs Cup") is considered to be the predecessor to the UEFA Cup, UEFA does not recognise the Fairs Cup as one of its official club competitions, and therefore its records are not included in the list.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-6)

The [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"), formerly the UEFA Cup, is an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition established in 1971 by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-rsssf-1) It is considered the second most important international competition for European clubs, after the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). Clubs qualify for the Europa League based on their performance in national leagues and cup competitions. For the first 25 years of the competition, the final was contested over [two legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_match "Two-legged match"), one at each participating club's stadium, but in 1998, [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") defeated [Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Lazio "SS Lazio") in the competition's first single-legged final held at a neutral venue, the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes") in Paris.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-2)[Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") won the [inaugural competition in 1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971%E2%80%9372_UEFA_Cup "1971–72 UEFA Cup"), defeating [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") 3–2 on aggregate.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-3) Eleven finals have featured teams from the same national association: Italy ([1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_UEFA_Cup_final "1990 UEFA Cup final"), [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_UEFA_Cup_final "1991 UEFA Cup final"), [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Cup_final "1995 UEFA Cup final") and [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Cup_final "1998 UEFA Cup final")), England ([1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_UEFA_Cup_final "1972 UEFA Cup final"), [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2019 UEFA Europa League final") and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2025 UEFA Europa League final")), Spain ([2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_UEFA_Cup_final "2007 UEFA Cup final") and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2012 UEFA Europa League final")), Germany ([1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_UEFA_Cup_final "1980 UEFA Cup final")) and Portugal ([2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2011 UEFA Europa League final")).

[Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") holds the record for the most victories, having won the competition seven times since its inception.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-4)[Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") (winners in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_UEFA_Cup_final "1985 UEFA Cup final") and [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_UEFA_Cup_final "1986 UEFA Cup final")) and Sevilla (winners in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Cup_final "2006 UEFA Cup final") and 2007, and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2014 UEFA Europa League final"), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2015 UEFA Europa League final") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2016 UEFA Europa League final")) are the only teams to have retained their title. The competition has been won fourteen times by teams from Spain, more than any other country.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-rsssf-1) The last champions before the UEFA Cup was renamed to UEFA Europa League were [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk"), who beat [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") 2–1 after extra time in the [2009 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final "2009 UEFA Cup final").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-5)[Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") and [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") have lost the most finals, with three losses in the competition. The current champions are [Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C."), who defeated [SC Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Freiburg "SC Freiburg") 3–0 in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Europa_League_final "2026 UEFA Europa League final").

While the [Inter-Cities Fairs Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup "Inter-Cities Fairs Cup") is considered to be the predecessor to the UEFA Cup, UEFA does not recognise the Fairs Cup as one of its official club competitions, and therefore its records are not included in the list.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UEFA_Europa_League_finals#cite_note-6)

The **2005 UEFA Cup final** was the final match of the [2004–05 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup"), the 34th season of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup "UEFA Cup"), [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA")'s second-tier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament. The match was contested by [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP") and [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow") on 18 May 2005; CSKA won the match 3–1. Sporting CP opened the scoring in the first half from full-back [Rogério](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Fid%C3%A9lis_R%C3%A9gis "Rogério Fidélis Régis"), before [Aleksei Berezutskiy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksei_Berezutski "Aleksei Berezutski") equalised in the second half. [Yuri Zhirkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Zhirkov "Yuri Zhirkov") would give the Russian side the lead nine minutes after CSKA's equalising goal, and the Moscow outfit would close out the scoring 15 minutes from the end after a quick CSKA counterattack saw [Vágner Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1gner_Love "Vágner Love") become the youngest player to score in a UEFA Cup final at the age of 20 years, 341 days,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-6) firing the ball past Sporting goalkeeper [Ricardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_(footballer,_born_1976) "Ricardo (footballer, born 1976)") to give the Russian side a first UEFA Cup trophy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-11) It was also the first European trophy won by a Russian club, in what was the first final since [Dynamo Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Moscow "FC Dynamo Moscow")—then part of the [Russian SFSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic") of the Soviet Union—lost the [1972 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1972 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), and the first European title for a side from what was the Soviet Union since [Dynamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv"), now part of [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine"), won the [1986 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1986 European Cup Winners' Cup final").

The match was played at the [Estádio José Alvalade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade "Estádio José Alvalade") – home ground of finalists Sporting CP – in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) Until then, it was the third European football final to be held in Portugal, after the [1967 European Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_final "1967 European Cup final"), which was held in another venue in the [Lisbon District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_District "Lisbon District"), the [Estádio Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Nacional "Estádio Nacional") in [Oeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oeiras,_Portugal "Oeiras, Portugal"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-13)[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), which was held at the [old Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz_(1954) "Estádio da Luz (1954)") in the city.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

The **2005 UEFA Cup final** was the final match of the [2004–05 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup"), the 34th season of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup "UEFA Cup"), [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA")'s second-tier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament. The match was contested by [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP") and [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow") on 18 May 2005; CSKA won the match 3–1. Sporting CP opened the scoring in the first half from full-back [Rogério](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Fid%C3%A9lis_R%C3%A9gis "Rogério Fidélis Régis"), before [Aleksei Berezutskiy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksei_Berezutski "Aleksei Berezutski") equalised in the second half. [Yuri Zhirkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Zhirkov "Yuri Zhirkov") would give the Russian side the lead nine minutes after CSKA's equalising goal, and the Moscow outfit would close out the scoring 15 minutes from the end after a quick CSKA counterattack saw [Vágner Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1gner_Love "Vágner Love") become the youngest player to score in a UEFA Cup final at the age of 20 years, 341 days,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-6) firing the ball past Sporting goalkeeper [Ricardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_(footballer,_born_1976) "Ricardo (footballer, born 1976)") to give the Russian side a first UEFA Cup trophy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-11) It was also the first European trophy won by a Russian club, in what was the first final since [Dynamo Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Moscow "FC Dynamo Moscow")—then part of the [Russian SFSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic") of the Soviet Union—lost the [1972 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1972 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), and the first European title for a side from what was the Soviet Union since [Dynamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv"), now part of [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine"), won the [1986 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1986 European Cup Winners' Cup final").

The match was played at the [Estádio José Alvalade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade "Estádio José Alvalade") – home ground of finalists Sporting CP – in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) Until then, it was the third European football final to be held in Portugal, after the [1967 European Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_final "1967 European Cup final"), which was held in another venue in the [Lisbon District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_District "Lisbon District"), the [Estádio Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Nacional "Estádio Nacional") in [Oeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oeiras,_Portugal "Oeiras, Portugal"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-13)[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), which was held at the [old Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz_(1954) "Estádio da Luz (1954)") in the city.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **2015 Russian Cup final** decided the winner of the [2014–15 Russian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Russian_Cup "2014–15 Russian Cup"), the 23rd season of Russia's main football cup. It was played on 21 May 2015 at the [Central Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Stadium_(Astrakhan) "Central Stadium (Astrakhan)") in [Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrakhan "Astrakhan"), between [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lokomotiv_Moscow "FC Lokomotiv Moscow") and [Kuban Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Kuban_Krasnodar "FC Kuban Krasnodar"). [Lokomotiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lokomotiv_Moscow "FC Lokomotiv Moscow") came back from behind and emerged victorious with a 3-1 win in extra time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-1)

The winner qualified for the group stage of the [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Europa_League "2015–16 UEFA Europa League") and also faced the champions of the [2014–15 Russian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Russian_Premier_League "2014–15 Russian Premier League"), [Zenit Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg") in the [Russian Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Super_Cup "2015 Russian Super Cup") on 12 July 2015.

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Russian_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

The Russian Cup final was held for the first time ever at [Central Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Stadium_(Astrakhan) "Central Stadium (Astrakhan)") in [Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrakhan "Astrakhan"). [Kuban Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuban_Stadium "Kuban Stadium") in [Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar "Krasnodar") and [Otkrytie Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otkrytie_Arena "Otkrytie Arena") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow") were touted to be other potential alternatives but ultimately the stadium was announced by the [Russian Football Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union "Russian Football Union") as the venue of the final through an official statement on Twitter on 30 March 2015.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

**Central Stadium** is the home stadium of [Volgar Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volgar_Astrakhan "FC Volgar Astrakhan") and it holds 17,500 people, all seated. The stadium was originally built in 1955 but it underwent a total reconstruction in the summer of 2013.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-3) The stadium has been earmarked as a training facility for the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Russian_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

Lokomotiv played their 7th Russian Cup final, second only to [CSKA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow")'s 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-4) Prior to the 2015 final, they have won five, against the seven won by their cross town rivals. Their most recent appearance at the final was in 2007. Indeed, they faced the now-defunct [FC Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Moscow "FC Moscow") and won the contest courtesy of a goal from [Garry O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_O'Connor "Garry O'Connor") in extra-time.

As for Kuban, it was their first ever appearance at the Russian Cup final. Indeed, their best performance ever in the Russian Cup came in [2012–13 Russian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Russian_Cup "2012–13 Russian Cup"), when they were eliminated by [Zenit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg") on penalties in the quarter-finals. As a side note, [Leonid Kuchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Kuchuk "Leonid Kuchuk"), the current manager of Kuban, faced Lokomotiv in the final after he was sacked from the same position earlier this season following a disappointing start at the helm of the Muscovite club.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-5)

It was also the first time that the two clubs met in the Russian Cup final.
