The **2015 Russian Cup final** decided the winner of the [2014–15 Russian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Russian_Cup "2014–15 Russian Cup"), the 23rd season of Russia's main football cup. It was played on 21 May 2015 at the [Central Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Stadium_(Astrakhan) "Central Stadium (Astrakhan)") in [Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrakhan "Astrakhan"), between [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lokomotiv_Moscow "FC Lokomotiv Moscow") and [Kuban Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Kuban_Krasnodar "FC Kuban Krasnodar"). [Lokomotiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lokomotiv_Moscow "FC Lokomotiv Moscow") came back from behind and emerged victorious with a 3-1 win in extra time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-1)

The winner qualified for the group stage of the [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Europa_League "2015–16 UEFA Europa League") and also faced the champions of the [2014–15 Russian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Russian_Premier_League "2014–15 Russian Premier League"), [Zenit Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg") in the [Russian Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Super_Cup "2015 Russian Super Cup") on 12 July 2015.

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Russian_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

The Russian Cup final was held for the first time ever at [Central Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Stadium_(Astrakhan) "Central Stadium (Astrakhan)") in [Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrakhan "Astrakhan"). [Kuban Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuban_Stadium "Kuban Stadium") in [Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar "Krasnodar") and [Otkrytie Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otkrytie_Arena "Otkrytie Arena") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow") were touted to be other potential alternatives but ultimately the stadium was announced by the [Russian Football Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union "Russian Football Union") as the venue of the final through an official statement on Twitter on 30 March 2015.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

**Central Stadium** is the home stadium of [Volgar Astrakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volgar_Astrakhan "FC Volgar Astrakhan") and it holds 17,500 people, all seated. The stadium was originally built in 1955 but it underwent a total reconstruction in the summer of 2013.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-3) The stadium has been earmarked as a training facility for the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_Russian_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

Lokomotiv played their 7th Russian Cup final, second only to [CSKA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow")'s 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-4) Prior to the 2015 final, they have won five, against the seven won by their cross town rivals. Their most recent appearance at the final was in 2007. Indeed, they faced the now-defunct [FC Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Moscow "FC Moscow") and won the contest courtesy of a goal from [Garry O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_O'Connor "Garry O'Connor") in extra-time.

As for Kuban, it was their first ever appearance at the Russian Cup final. Indeed, their best performance ever in the Russian Cup came in [2012–13 Russian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Russian_Cup "2012–13 Russian Cup"), when they were eliminated by [Zenit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg "FC Zenit Saint Petersburg") on penalties in the quarter-finals. As a side note, [Leonid Kuchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Kuchuk "Leonid Kuchuk"), the current manager of Kuban, faced Lokomotiv in the final after he was sacked from the same position earlier this season following a disappointing start at the helm of the Muscovite club.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Russian_Cup_final#cite_note-5)

It was also the first time that the two clubs met in the Russian Cup final.

The **2009 UEFA Cup Final** was the final match of the [2008–09 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup "2008–09 UEFA Cup"), the 38th season of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup "UEFA Cup"), [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA")'s second-tier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament. It was also the last final to be held under the UEFA Cup name, as the competition was rebranded as the UEFA Europa League from the [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Europa_League "2009–10 UEFA Europa League"). The final was contested by [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") and [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), with Shakhtar winning the match 2–1 after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)"). All three goalscorers in the game were Brazilians; lone striker [Luiz Adriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Adriano "Luiz Adriano") opened the scoring for Shakhtar midway through the first half, before [Naldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naldo_(footballer,_born_1982) "Naldo (footballer, born 1982)") equalised from a free kick ten minutes later. The second half was goalless and the match went to extra time; after only seven minutes, [Jádson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1dson "Jádson") scored for Shakhtar to secure the club's first major European trophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-4)

UEFA Cup trophy on display at the [Donbas Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donbas_Arena "Donbas Arena") museum.

The match was played at the [Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9E%C3%BCkr%C3%BC_Saraco%C4%9Flu_Stadium "Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium") – home ground of [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") – in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 20 May 2009.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-5) It was the second European football final to be held in Turkey, after the [2005 UEFA Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final"), which was held in another Istanbul venue, the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium"). It was also the first European football final to be held outside the geographical Europe, as Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium lies across the [Bosphorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosphorus "Bosphorus") from the city centre, and hence, in geographical Asia.

Former Fenerbahçe player [Can Bartu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can_Bartu "Can Bartu") was appointed as ambassador of the final.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The 2009 UEFA Cup final marked the first meeting between [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") and [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), although Shakhtar had previously played nine matches against German sides (won 4, lost 3), while Werder had played just four matches against Ukrainian teams (won 2, lost 1). Both teams were playing in their first UEFA Cup final, and Shakhtar were playing in their first final in any of the three major UEFA competitions; Werder Bremen beat [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") 2–0 in the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-6)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Venue")]

The 2009 UEFA Cup final also marked the first time that the [Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9E%C3%BCkr%C3%BC_Saraco%C4%9Flu_Stadium "Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium") had hosted a major European final, as well as being the first time that the UEFA Cup final had been held in Turkey;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-7) the [2005 UEFA Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final") was held at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") across the [Bosporus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosporus "Bosporus") from the Şükrü Saracoğlu.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-8) It is the only European final to not be played in Europe, as the Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium is technically in Asia.

### Shakhtar Donetsk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Shakhtar Donetsk")]

As champions of the [2007–08 Vyshcha Liha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Vyshcha_Liha "2007–08 Vyshcha Liha"), Shakhtar were awarded a spot in the third qualifying round of the [2008–09 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League "2008–09 UEFA Champions League"). Here they were drawn against Croatian league winners [Dinamo Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb"). Shakhtar easily progressed over the two-legged tie with two victories and an aggregate score of 5–1. Shakhtar thus qualified for the Champions League group stage for the third season in a row.

Shakhtar were drawn in [Group C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_C "2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage") with [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"), [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP"), and [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel"). The group stage campaign started brightly for the Ukrainians, with a 2–1 over Basel in the Swiss city. In the second game, Shakhtar hosted Barcelona and the two sides were set to share the points at 1–1 until [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time in the second half and the [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") giants won 2–1. Two successive 1–0 defeats to Sporting CP, home and away, saw Shakhtar's hopes of progressing to the knockout rounds of the Champions League dashed. Shakhtar, however, were well positioned to claim third place, above Basel, and secure passage to the UEFA Cup knockout rounds if they took points from their last two games in the group stage. Shakhtar dismantled Basel 5–0 in [Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donetsk "Donetsk") and famously defeated a youthful Barcelona side 3–2 at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou"), (Barcelona had already secured first place in the group before the final match was played and were resting players ahead of an _[El Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_Cl%C3%A1sico "El Clásico")_ league game against [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF")), thus Shakhtar finished the group stage with nine points in third place, eight points clear of Basel and just three points behind second placed Sporting CP.

In the [Round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Round_of_32 "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase") in the UEFA Cup, Shakhtar were paired with English side [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."). With the first leg at the [RSK Olimpiyskyi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Stadium_(Donetsk) "Lokomotiv Stadium (Donetsk)"), Shakhtar were frustrated by their inability to turn their dominance over Tottenham into goals, until substitute [Yevhen Seleznyov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevhen_Seleznyov "Yevhen Seleznyov") scored on his first touch, with a header in the 79th minute. [Jádson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1dson "Jádson") doubled Shakhtar's lead just two minutes later, after playing a one-two with [Willian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willian_(footballer,_born_1988) "Willian (footballer, born 1988)"). Taking with them a 2–0 aggregate lead to London, Shakhtar were favoured to progress to the Round of 16, but a goal from Tottenham's [Giovani dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovani_dos_Santos "Giovani dos Santos") in the 55th minute gave the English side a glimmer of hope. [Fernandinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernandinho_(footballer,_born_May_1985) "Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)") answered with a goal, however, in the 86th minute for Shakhtar, which put Shakhtar into the next round with a 3–1 aggregate victory.

The [Round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Round_of_16 "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase") saw old [Soviet League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Top_League "Soviet Top League") rivals [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow") and Shakhtar matched against each other, with the first leg in Moscow. [Vágner Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1gner_Love "Vágner Love") scored a [penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") and CSKA won the first leg 1–0. In the return leg in Donetsk, Fernandinho converted a penalty in the 54th minute and evened the aggregate scoreline to 1–1. In the 70th minute, [2004–05 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup") winners CSKA were left stunned when goalkeeper [Igor Akinfeev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Akinfeev "Igor Akinfeev"), under pressure from [Oleksandr Kucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleksandr_Kucher "Oleksandr Kucher"), could only clear a looping cross from Fernandinho just a few meters ahead of him, where [Luiz Adriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Adriano "Luiz Adriano") was perfectly positioned to hit it first time and score. Shakhtar won the match 2–0, and on aggregate 2–1, progressing to the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup for the first time in their history.

Shakhtar were drawn against French club [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") in the [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Quarter-finals "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase"). Goals from [Tomáš Hübschman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_H%C3%BCbschman "Tomáš Hübschman") and Jádson gave Shakhtar a 2–0 win in the RSK Olimpiyskyi Stadium. In the return leg in Marseille, Shakhtar got an important away goal in the 30th minute through a close-range Fernandinho strike, where he blasted it past the Marseille goalkeeper from a very tight angle, after [Ilsinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilsinho "Ilsinho") had played him through. Although [Hatem Ben Arfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatem_Ben_Arfa "Hatem Ben Arfa") levelled the score at 1–1 in the 43rd minute, Marseille never looked liked getting the three goals that was required of them in order to progress, and in the 90th minute, adding to Marseille's wounds, Luiz Adriano scored to make it 2–1 and thus 4–1 on aggregate. Shakhtar had progressed to a European cup competition semi-final for the first time in their history with this victory.

In the [semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Semi-finals "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase"), Shakhtar could have been drawn against German clubs [Hamburger SV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburger_SV "Hamburger SV") or [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), but instead a German–Ukrainian final was guaranteed when Hamburg and Werder Bremen were paired with each other, while Shakhtar were drawn with fellow Ukrainian club [Dynamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv"). Dynamo and Shakhtar have been fierce rivals since the [Ukrainian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Premier_League "Ukrainian Premier League")'s formation in 1991 as they have often battled each other for 1st place in the league. The draw of Dynamo-Shakhtar was met with great excitement by the Ukrainian public, who eagerly anticipated the showdown. Both stadiums were easily sold out for this fixture. Dynamo hosted the first leg in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"), and it got off to a bad start for Shakhtar when [Dmytro Chyhrynskyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmytro_Chyhrynskyi "Dmytro Chyhrynskyi") scored an [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal") to give Dynamo the lead 1–0. The match was tense and thus not many clear cut chances to score were made, but Dynamo were clearly on top and a Shakhtar equaliser was looking unlikely until the 68th minute when substitute Willian crossed and Fernandinho bundled it into the goal to level the score at 1–1. Dynamo's [Olexandr Aliyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olexandr_Aliyev "Olexandr Aliyev") had a chance to give the Kyiv side the lead again in the 78th minute, but Shakhtar goalkeeper [Andriy Pyatov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Pyatov "Andriy Pyatov") saved well and the game ended 1–1. Shakhtar took their crucial away goal to Donetsk and things were looking very rosy when Jadson scored in the 17th minute in the return leg to put the aggregate scoreline at 2–1. In the 37th minute, Dynamo correctly had a goal ruled offsides. Shortly after the start of the second half, [Ismaël Bangoura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isma%C3%ABl_Bangoura "Ismaël Bangoura") equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed for Bangoura to have a clear shot on goal, which he finished well. With the aggregate at 2–2 and heading for [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time") and potentially a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)"), a moment of brilliance in the 89th minute from Ilsinho sent Shakhtar to Istanbul. After collecting a long pass on the right-wing, Ilsinho cut in towards goal, shifted his way past three Dynamo defenders and coolly placed the ball where the Dynamo keeper had no chance. The match finished 2–1 and Shakhtar won 3–2 on aggregate and thus became the first ever Ukrainian side to reach a UEFA Cup Final.

### Werder Bremen

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Werder Bremen")]

Werder finished the [2007–08 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Bundesliga "2007–08 Bundesliga") in second place and received a spot in the 2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage as a result. They were matched up against [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan"), [Panathinaikos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathinaikos_F.C. "Panathinaikos F.C."), and [Anorthosis Famagusta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anorthosis_Famagusta_FC "Anorthosis Famagusta FC") in [Group B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_B "2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage"). The Champions League campaign got off to a poor start for Werder when the first tie of the round against heavy underdog Cypriot side Anorthosis ended in a 0–0 draw in [Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremen "Bremen"). Werder rebounded in the second match with a 1–1 draw in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") against Internazionale, thanks to a [Claudio Pizarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Pizarro "Claudio Pizarro") equaliser in the 62nd minute. An entertaining 2–2 draw in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") against Panathinaikos followed, before disaster struck in the return leg in Bremen, where Panathinaikos defeated their German hosts by a score of 3–0. Werder looked as though they were heading for a fourth-place finish in the group when in the next game in [Nicosia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicosia "Nicosia"), Anorthosis were leading 2–0 after 72 minutes, but a trip on [Aaron Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Hunt "Aaron Hunt") in the penalty area allowed for [Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_(footballer,_born_1985) "Diego (footballer, born 1985)") to score a penalty kick to make the score 2–1. [Hugo Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Almeida "Hugo Almeida") rescued a point for Werder in the 87th minute, when he scored after a cross from [Mesut Özil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesut_%C3%96zil "Mesut Özil") was helped on by [Duško Tošić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Du%C5%A1ko_To%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Duško Tošić"). Needing a win at home against the group favourites Internazionale and an Anorthosis loss to Panathinaikos in order to secure third place and thus progression to the UEFA Cup knockout rounds, Werder were staring elimination from European cup competition in the face. Werder dominated the match against the Italians and were rewarded for their determination to score in the 63rd minute when Pizarro scored on the rebound from a spilled shot by Özil. After Werder established their lead, further good news made its way to the [Weserstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weserstadion "Weserstadion"), where news of a Panathinaikos goal against Anorthosis lifted spirits. [Markus Rosenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Rosenberg "Markus Rosenberg") extended Werder's lead in the 81st minute, and although Internazionale pulled a goal back through an 88th minute [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimovi%C4%87 "Zlatan Ibrahimović") strike, Werder came out deserved winners 2–1. Panathinaikos held on to their 1–0 lead against Anorthosis and after both games had finished, Werder secured third place and a spot in the UEFA Cup knockout rounds.

Just when Werder thought things would ease for them once they parachuted into the UEFA Cup, Werder were told that they faced another trip to the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), except this time it would be against [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), the favourites to win the UEFA Cup. In the home leg in Bremen, Milan went ahead in the 36th minute thanks to a [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi") goal. The Germans did not give up however, and after creating a host of chances, Diego finally finished one off in the 84th minute to level the score at 1–1. Heading to the San Siro with the aggregate scoreline all even, Milan jumped ahead in the first half with two goals from [Andrea Pirlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo") and [Alexandre Pato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Pato "Alexandre Pato") respectively. The task was daunting, but Werder were up to it, and in the 68th minute Pizarro scored a header from a Diego [free-kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_free_kick "Direct free kick"). Werder got the decisive goal ten minutes later after yet another Pizarro headed goal, this time from a cross from [Sebastian Boenisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Boenisch "Sebastian Boenisch"). The match finished 2–2 and Werder won the round with an aggregate score of 3–3, through the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule").

In the Round of 16, Werder were paired with French side [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne"). [Naldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naldo_(footballer,_born_1982) "Naldo (footballer, born 1982)") put Werder ahead in the 20th minute, but Werder were left frustrated in the Weserstadion as they could not convert their dominance into more goals. In the return leg at the [Stade Geoffroy-Guichard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Geoffroy-Guichard "Stade Geoffroy-Guichard"), Werder got off to the best of starts, with [Sebastian Prödl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Pr%C3%B6dl "Sebastian Prödl") scoring in the fourth minute and Pizarro adding a second goal in the 27th minute. Saint-Étienne then needed four goals to win the tie. A goal in the 64th minute by [Yohan Benalouane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yohan_Benalouane "Yohan Benalouane") rejuvenated the match, but by the time the French got their second goal in the 90th minute, the fixture was all but over.

Werder were once again facing an Italian side; this time in the quarter-finals, and with their new Italian opponents being [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio"). It looked as though the job was done for the Bremen club when they had a 3–0 lead over Udinese after just 69 minutes at the Weserstadion, through two goals from Diego and a solitary strike from Almeida. But in the 87th minute, [Fabio Quagliarella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Quagliarella "Fabio Quagliarella") breathed new life into Udinese's hopes, when he got a goal back from close range. One of the most entertaining matches of the entire tournament followed in the return leg at the [Stadio Friuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Friuli "Stadio Friuli"). [Gökhan Inler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6khan_Inler "Gökhan Inler") opened the scoring for the hosts with a fantastic 30-metre goal that left Werder keeper [Tim Wiese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Wiese "Tim Wiese") with no chance of saving. Diego equalised in the 28th minute, before Quagliarella restored the Udinese lead just two minutes later by lobbing the ball over Wiese. Quagliarella scored his second and Udinese's third only eight minutes later and the aggregate was even at 4–4 and the match heading to extra time if the score stayed at 3–1. The match restarted in the second half with the same frantic pace it had in the first half, and after Quagliarella barely missed an opportunity to score a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick "Hat-trick"), Diego headed in from an Almeida shot which bounced off the bar to bring the score to 3–2. Udinese now needed two more goals to go through. [Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_dal_Belo "Felipe dal Belo") and [Kwadwo Asamoah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwadwo_Asamoah "Kwadwo Asamoah") had the best scoring opportunities for Udinese, but it wasn't meant to be, and after Udinese keeper [Samir Handanović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Handanovi%C4%87 "Samir Handanović") saved a Diego penalty kick, on the resulting corner, Pizarro turned in [Per Mertesacker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Mertesacker "Per Mertesacker")'s header in the 73rd minute to wrap up the tie at 3–3 and 6–4 on aggregate.

In the semi-finals, Werder were drawn against their local rivals Hamburg. Werder defeated Hamburg in a penalty shootout in a [German Cup semi-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_DFB-Pokal#Semifinals "2008–09 DFB-Pokal") just a week before the first leg of the UEFA Cup semi-final. With animosity running high between the two clubs and their respective supporters, this promised to be a fascinating clash for German football fans. The first leg was once again hosted by Werder, but this time Werder got off to a poor start, with Hamburg having the better chances to score in the opening, before they finally converted one of their chances in the 28th minute with [Piotr Trochowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piotr_Trochowski "Piotr Trochowski") heading in. The Hamburg goal woke up Werder, but Pizarro, Almeida, and substitute Rosenborg all squandered their chances to equalise. Taking a 1–0 lead with them to the [HSH Nordbank Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSH_Nordbank_Arena "HSH Nordbank Arena"), Hamburg were confident of progressing to the Istanbul final, while it looked as though Werder would fail in the semi-finals of the UEFA Cup for the fourth time. It looked all over in the second leg when [Ivica Olić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Oli%C4%87 "Ivica Olić") finished well in the 13th minute. But sixteen minutes later Diego and Pizarro played a one-two, and Diego put it past Hamburg 'keeper [Frank Rost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rost "Frank Rost") to level the score at 1–1 and pull the aggregate to 1–2. Shortly afterwards, Diego's shot from 25 metres rattled the crossbar. In the 41st minute, Diego received a yellow card for shoving fellow Brazilian [Alex Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Sandro_da_Silva "Alex Sandro da Silva"), which ruled him out of the final. After a host of chances for both sides, in the 66th minute, Pizarro got the ball in the middle of the pitch, made a short run, and his curling shot from about 30 metres made its way past Rost to give Werder the lead 2–1. Things got even better for Werder in the 83rd minute when [Frank Baumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Baumann_(footballer) "Frank Baumann (footballer)") headed in to make it 3–2 on aggregate; Hamburg then needed two goals in the last seven minutes plus stoppage time to progress. Olić responded in the 87th minute with another goal to even the aggregate score at 3–3, however Werder would still go through on the away goals rule. As Hamburg searched for a goal, the game fizzled out and Werder had won their ticket to Istanbul.

The **2009 UEFA Cup Final** was the final match of the [2008–09 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup "2008–09 UEFA Cup"), the 38th season of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup "UEFA Cup"), [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA")'s second-tier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament. It was also the last final to be held under the UEFA Cup name, as the competition was rebranded as the UEFA Europa League from the [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Europa_League "2009–10 UEFA Europa League"). The final was contested by [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") and [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), with Shakhtar winning the match 2–1 after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)"). All three goalscorers in the game were Brazilians; lone striker [Luiz Adriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Adriano "Luiz Adriano") opened the scoring for Shakhtar midway through the first half, before [Naldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naldo_(footballer,_born_1982) "Naldo (footballer, born 1982)") equalised from a free kick ten minutes later. The second half was goalless and the match went to extra time; after only seven minutes, [Jádson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1dson "Jádson") scored for Shakhtar to secure the club's first major European trophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-4)

UEFA Cup trophy on display at the [Donbas Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donbas_Arena "Donbas Arena") museum.

The match was played at the [Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9E%C3%BCkr%C3%BC_Saraco%C4%9Flu_Stadium "Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium") – home ground of [Fenerbahçe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_S.K._(football) "Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)") – in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 20 May 2009.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-5) It was the second European football final to be held in Turkey, after the [2005 UEFA Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final"), which was held in another Istanbul venue, the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium"). It was also the first European football final to be held outside the geographical Europe, as Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium lies across the [Bosphorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosphorus "Bosphorus") from the city centre, and hence, in geographical Asia.

Former Fenerbahçe player [Can Bartu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can_Bartu "Can Bartu") was appointed as ambassador of the final.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The 2009 UEFA Cup final marked the first meeting between [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") and [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), although Shakhtar had previously played nine matches against German sides (won 4, lost 3), while Werder had played just four matches against Ukrainian teams (won 2, lost 1). Both teams were playing in their first UEFA Cup final, and Shakhtar were playing in their first final in any of the three major UEFA competitions; Werder Bremen beat [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") 2–0 in the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-6)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Venue")]

The 2009 UEFA Cup final also marked the first time that the [Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9E%C3%BCkr%C3%BC_Saraco%C4%9Flu_Stadium "Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium") had hosted a major European final, as well as being the first time that the UEFA Cup final had been held in Turkey;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-7) the [2005 UEFA Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final") was held at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") across the [Bosporus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosporus "Bosporus") from the Şükrü Saracoğlu.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Cup_final#cite_note-8) It is the only European final to not be played in Europe, as the Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium is technically in Asia.

### Shakhtar Donetsk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Shakhtar Donetsk")]

As champions of the [2007–08 Vyshcha Liha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Vyshcha_Liha "2007–08 Vyshcha Liha"), Shakhtar were awarded a spot in the third qualifying round of the [2008–09 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League "2008–09 UEFA Champions League"). Here they were drawn against Croatian league winners [Dinamo Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb"). Shakhtar easily progressed over the two-legged tie with two victories and an aggregate score of 5–1. Shakhtar thus qualified for the Champions League group stage for the third season in a row.

Shakhtar were drawn in [Group C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_C "2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage") with [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"), [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP"), and [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel"). The group stage campaign started brightly for the Ukrainians, with a 2–1 over Basel in the Swiss city. In the second game, Shakhtar hosted Barcelona and the two sides were set to share the points at 1–1 until [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time in the second half and the [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") giants won 2–1. Two successive 1–0 defeats to Sporting CP, home and away, saw Shakhtar's hopes of progressing to the knockout rounds of the Champions League dashed. Shakhtar, however, were well positioned to claim third place, above Basel, and secure passage to the UEFA Cup knockout rounds if they took points from their last two games in the group stage. Shakhtar dismantled Basel 5–0 in [Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donetsk "Donetsk") and famously defeated a youthful Barcelona side 3–2 at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou"), (Barcelona had already secured first place in the group before the final match was played and were resting players ahead of an _[El Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_Cl%C3%A1sico "El Clásico")_ league game against [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF")), thus Shakhtar finished the group stage with nine points in third place, eight points clear of Basel and just three points behind second placed Sporting CP.

In the [Round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Round_of_32 "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase") in the UEFA Cup, Shakhtar were paired with English side [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."). With the first leg at the [RSK Olimpiyskyi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Stadium_(Donetsk) "Lokomotiv Stadium (Donetsk)"), Shakhtar were frustrated by their inability to turn their dominance over Tottenham into goals, until substitute [Yevhen Seleznyov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevhen_Seleznyov "Yevhen Seleznyov") scored on his first touch, with a header in the 79th minute. [Jádson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1dson "Jádson") doubled Shakhtar's lead just two minutes later, after playing a one-two with [Willian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willian_(footballer,_born_1988) "Willian (footballer, born 1988)"). Taking with them a 2–0 aggregate lead to London, Shakhtar were favoured to progress to the Round of 16, but a goal from Tottenham's [Giovani dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovani_dos_Santos "Giovani dos Santos") in the 55th minute gave the English side a glimmer of hope. [Fernandinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernandinho_(footballer,_born_May_1985) "Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)") answered with a goal, however, in the 86th minute for Shakhtar, which put Shakhtar into the next round with a 3–1 aggregate victory.

The [Round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Round_of_16 "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase") saw old [Soviet League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Top_League "Soviet Top League") rivals [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow") and Shakhtar matched against each other, with the first leg in Moscow. [Vágner Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1gner_Love "Vágner Love") scored a [penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") and CSKA won the first leg 1–0. In the return leg in Donetsk, Fernandinho converted a penalty in the 54th minute and evened the aggregate scoreline to 1–1. In the 70th minute, [2004–05 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Cup "2004–05 UEFA Cup") winners CSKA were left stunned when goalkeeper [Igor Akinfeev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Akinfeev "Igor Akinfeev"), under pressure from [Oleksandr Kucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleksandr_Kucher "Oleksandr Kucher"), could only clear a looping cross from Fernandinho just a few meters ahead of him, where [Luiz Adriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Adriano "Luiz Adriano") was perfectly positioned to hit it first time and score. Shakhtar won the match 2–0, and on aggregate 2–1, progressing to the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup for the first time in their history.

Shakhtar were drawn against French club [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") in the [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Quarter-finals "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase"). Goals from [Tomáš Hübschman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_H%C3%BCbschman "Tomáš Hübschman") and Jádson gave Shakhtar a 2–0 win in the RSK Olimpiyskyi Stadium. In the return leg in Marseille, Shakhtar got an important away goal in the 30th minute through a close-range Fernandinho strike, where he blasted it past the Marseille goalkeeper from a very tight angle, after [Ilsinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilsinho "Ilsinho") had played him through. Although [Hatem Ben Arfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatem_Ben_Arfa "Hatem Ben Arfa") levelled the score at 1–1 in the 43rd minute, Marseille never looked liked getting the three goals that was required of them in order to progress, and in the 90th minute, adding to Marseille's wounds, Luiz Adriano scored to make it 2–1 and thus 4–1 on aggregate. Shakhtar had progressed to a European cup competition semi-final for the first time in their history with this victory.

In the [semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Cup_final_phase#Semi-finals "2008–09 UEFA Cup final phase"), Shakhtar could have been drawn against German clubs [Hamburger SV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburger_SV "Hamburger SV") or [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), but instead a German–Ukrainian final was guaranteed when Hamburg and Werder Bremen were paired with each other, while Shakhtar were drawn with fellow Ukrainian club [Dynamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv"). Dynamo and Shakhtar have been fierce rivals since the [Ukrainian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Premier_League "Ukrainian Premier League")'s formation in 1991 as they have often battled each other for 1st place in the league. The draw of Dynamo-Shakhtar was met with great excitement by the Ukrainian public, who eagerly anticipated the showdown. Both stadiums were easily sold out for this fixture. Dynamo hosted the first leg in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"), and it got off to a bad start for Shakhtar when [Dmytro Chyhrynskyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmytro_Chyhrynskyi "Dmytro Chyhrynskyi") scored an [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal") to give Dynamo the lead 1–0. The match was tense and thus not many clear cut chances to score were made, but Dynamo were clearly on top and a Shakhtar equaliser was looking unlikely until the 68th minute when substitute Willian crossed and Fernandinho bundled it into the goal to level the score at 1–1. Dynamo's [Olexandr Aliyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olexandr_Aliyev "Olexandr Aliyev") had a chance to give the Kyiv side the lead again in the 78th minute, but Shakhtar goalkeeper [Andriy Pyatov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Pyatov "Andriy Pyatov") saved well and the game ended 1–1. Shakhtar took their crucial away goal to Donetsk and things were looking very rosy when Jadson scored in the 17th minute in the return leg to put the aggregate scoreline at 2–1. In the 37th minute, Dynamo correctly had a goal ruled offsides. Shortly after the start of the second half, [Ismaël Bangoura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isma%C3%ABl_Bangoura "Ismaël Bangoura") equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed for Bangoura to have a clear shot on goal, which he finished well. With the aggregate at 2–2 and heading for [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time") and potentially a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)"), a moment of brilliance in the 89th minute from Ilsinho sent Shakhtar to Istanbul. After collecting a long pass on the right-wing, Ilsinho cut in towards goal, shifted his way past three Dynamo defenders and coolly placed the ball where the Dynamo keeper had no chance. The match finished 2–1 and Shakhtar won 3–2 on aggregate and thus became the first ever Ukrainian side to reach a UEFA Cup Final.

### Werder Bremen

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2009_UEFA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Werder Bremen")]

Werder finished the [2007–08 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Bundesliga "2007–08 Bundesliga") in second place and received a spot in the 2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage as a result. They were matched up against [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan"), [Panathinaikos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathinaikos_F.C. "Panathinaikos F.C."), and [Anorthosis Famagusta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anorthosis_Famagusta_FC "Anorthosis Famagusta FC") in [Group B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_B "2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage"). The Champions League campaign got off to a poor start for Werder when the first tie of the round against heavy underdog Cypriot side Anorthosis ended in a 0–0 draw in [Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremen "Bremen"). Werder rebounded in the second match with a 1–1 draw in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") against Internazionale, thanks to a [Claudio Pizarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Pizarro "Claudio Pizarro") equaliser in the 62nd minute. An entertaining 2–2 draw in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") against Panathinaikos followed, before disaster struck in the return leg in Bremen, where Panathinaikos defeated their German hosts by a score of 3–0. Werder looked as though they were heading for a fourth-place finish in the group when in the next game in [Nicosia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicosia "Nicosia"), Anorthosis were leading 2–0 after 72 minutes, but a trip on [Aaron Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Hunt "Aaron Hunt") in the penalty area allowed for [Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_(footballer,_born_1985) "Diego (footballer, born 1985)") to score a penalty kick to make the score 2–1. [Hugo Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Almeida "Hugo Almeida") rescued a point for Werder in the 87th minute, when he scored after a cross from [Mesut Özil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesut_%C3%96zil "Mesut Özil") was helped on by [Duško Tošić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Du%C5%A1ko_To%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Duško Tošić"). Needing a win at home against the group favourites Internazionale and an Anorthosis loss to Panathinaikos in order to secure third place and thus progression to the UEFA Cup knockout rounds, Werder were staring elimination from European cup competition in the face. Werder dominated the match against the Italians and were rewarded for their determination to score in the 63rd minute when Pizarro scored on the rebound from a spilled shot by Özil. After Werder established their lead, further good news made its way to the [Weserstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weserstadion "Weserstadion"), where news of a Panathinaikos goal against Anorthosis lifted spirits. [Markus Rosenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Rosenberg "Markus Rosenberg") extended Werder's lead in the 81st minute, and although Internazionale pulled a goal back through an 88th minute [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimovi%C4%87 "Zlatan Ibrahimović") strike, Werder came out deserved winners 2–1. Panathinaikos held on to their 1–0 lead against Anorthosis and after both games had finished, Werder secured third place and a spot in the UEFA Cup knockout rounds.

Just when Werder thought things would ease for them once they parachuted into the UEFA Cup, Werder were told that they faced another trip to the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), except this time it would be against [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), the favourites to win the UEFA Cup. In the home leg in Bremen, Milan went ahead in the 36th minute thanks to a [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi") goal. The Germans did not give up however, and after creating a host of chances, Diego finally finished one off in the 84th minute to level the score at 1–1. Heading to the San Siro with the aggregate scoreline all even, Milan jumped ahead in the first half with two goals from [Andrea Pirlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo") and [Alexandre Pato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Pato "Alexandre Pato") respectively. The task was daunting, but Werder were up to it, and in the 68th minute Pizarro scored a header from a Diego [free-kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_free_kick "Direct free kick"). Werder got the decisive goal ten minutes later after yet another Pizarro headed goal, this time from a cross from [Sebastian Boenisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Boenisch "Sebastian Boenisch"). The match finished 2–2 and Werder won the round with an aggregate score of 3–3, through the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule").

In the Round of 16, Werder were paired with French side [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne"). [Naldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naldo_(footballer,_born_1982) "Naldo (footballer, born 1982)") put Werder ahead in the 20th minute, but Werder were left frustrated in the Weserstadion as they could not convert their dominance into more goals. In the return leg at the [Stade Geoffroy-Guichard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Geoffroy-Guichard "Stade Geoffroy-Guichard"), Werder got off to the best of starts, with [Sebastian Prödl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Pr%C3%B6dl "Sebastian Prödl") scoring in the fourth minute and Pizarro adding a second goal in the 27th minute. Saint-Étienne then needed four goals to win the tie. A goal in the 64th minute by [Yohan Benalouane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yohan_Benalouane "Yohan Benalouane") rejuvenated the match, but by the time the French got their second goal in the 90th minute, the fixture was all but over.

Werder were once again facing an Italian side; this time in the quarter-finals, and with their new Italian opponents being [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio"). It looked as though the job was done for the Bremen club when they had a 3–0 lead over Udinese after just 69 minutes at the Weserstadion, through two goals from Diego and a solitary strike from Almeida. But in the 87th minute, [Fabio Quagliarella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Quagliarella "Fabio Quagliarella") breathed new life into Udinese's hopes, when he got a goal back from close range. One of the most entertaining matches of the entire tournament followed in the return leg at the [Stadio Friuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Friuli "Stadio Friuli"). [Gökhan Inler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6khan_Inler "Gökhan Inler") opened the scoring for the hosts with a fantastic 30-metre goal that left Werder keeper [Tim Wiese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Wiese "Tim Wiese") with no chance of saving. Diego equalised in the 28th minute, before Quagliarella restored the Udinese lead just two minutes later by lobbing the ball over Wiese. Quagliarella scored his second and Udinese's third only eight minutes later and the aggregate was even at 4–4 and the match heading to extra time if the score stayed at 3–1. The match restarted in the second half with the same frantic pace it had in the first half, and after Quagliarella barely missed an opportunity to score a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick "Hat-trick"), Diego headed in from an Almeida shot which bounced off the bar to bring the score to 3–2. Udinese now needed two more goals to go through. [Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_dal_Belo "Felipe dal Belo") and [Kwadwo Asamoah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwadwo_Asamoah "Kwadwo Asamoah") had the best scoring opportunities for Udinese, but it wasn't meant to be, and after Udinese keeper [Samir Handanović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Handanovi%C4%87 "Samir Handanović") saved a Diego penalty kick, on the resulting corner, Pizarro turned in [Per Mertesacker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Mertesacker "Per Mertesacker")'s header in the 73rd minute to wrap up the tie at 3–3 and 6–4 on aggregate.

In the semi-finals, Werder were drawn against their local rivals Hamburg. Werder defeated Hamburg in a penalty shootout in a [German Cup semi-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_DFB-Pokal#Semifinals "2008–09 DFB-Pokal") just a week before the first leg of the UEFA Cup semi-final. With animosity running high between the two clubs and their respective supporters, this promised to be a fascinating clash for German football fans. The first leg was once again hosted by Werder, but this time Werder got off to a poor start, with Hamburg having the better chances to score in the opening, before they finally converted one of their chances in the 28th minute with [Piotr Trochowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piotr_Trochowski "Piotr Trochowski") heading in. The Hamburg goal woke up Werder, but Pizarro, Almeida, and substitute Rosenborg all squandered their chances to equalise. Taking a 1–0 lead with them to the [HSH Nordbank Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSH_Nordbank_Arena "HSH Nordbank Arena"), Hamburg were confident of progressing to the Istanbul final, while it looked as though Werder would fail in the semi-finals of the UEFA Cup for the fourth time. It looked all over in the second leg when [Ivica Olić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Oli%C4%87 "Ivica Olić") finished well in the 13th minute. But sixteen minutes later Diego and Pizarro played a one-two, and Diego put it past Hamburg 'keeper [Frank Rost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rost "Frank Rost") to level the score at 1–1 and pull the aggregate to 1–2. Shortly afterwards, Diego's shot from 25 metres rattled the crossbar. In the 41st minute, Diego received a yellow card for shoving fellow Brazilian [Alex Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Sandro_da_Silva "Alex Sandro da Silva"), which ruled him out of the final. After a host of chances for both sides, in the 66th minute, Pizarro got the ball in the middle of the pitch, made a short run, and his curling shot from about 30 metres made its way past Rost to give Werder the lead 2–1. Things got even better for Werder in the 83rd minute when [Frank Baumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Baumann_(footballer) "Frank Baumann (footballer)") headed in to make it 3–2 on aggregate; Hamburg then needed two goals in the last seven minutes plus stoppage time to progress. Olić responded in the 87th minute with another goal to even the aggregate score at 3–3, however Werder would still go through on the away goals rule. As Hamburg searched for a goal, the game fizzled out and Werder had won their ticket to Istanbul.

The **2015 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2014–15 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League "2014–15 UEFA Champions League"), the 60th season of Europe's premier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), and the 23rd season since it was renamed from the European Champion Clubs' Cup to the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was played at the [Olympiastadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), Germany, on 6 June 2015, between Italian side [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") and Spanish side [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").

For the second time – after [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final") – both teams came into the final with the possibility of definitively winning a [continental treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)"), having each won their national league and cup for the season. Barcelona scored the only goal of the first half after four minutes, through [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"). Ten minutes after the interval, Juventus equalised with a goal by [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata"). In the 68th minute, [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") put Barcelona back in the lead, and Barcelona's win was confirmed when [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") scored with the last kick of the game. It was Barcelona's fifth trophy in the competition, and sealed their second treble, the other coming in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"). It was also Juventus' sixth defeat in a European Cup final, the most by any club, a record they previously shared with [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") and [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica").

As winners, Barcelona earned the right to play against the winners of the [2014–15 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League "2014–15 UEFA Europa League"), [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in the [2015 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup "2015 UEFA Super Cup"), and won that match 5–4. They also qualified to enter the [2015 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2015 FIFA Club World Cup") in Japan as the UEFA representative, going on to beat Argentina's [River Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_River_Plate "CA River Plate") in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final "2015 FIFA Club World Cup final").

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Olympicstadium2.jpg/250px-Olympicstadium2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympicstadium2.jpg)

The Olympiastadion in Berlin hosted the final.

The [Olympiastadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") was announced as the venue for the final at the UEFA Executive Committee meeting in London on 23 May 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5) This was the first European Cup/Champions League final hosted in Berlin.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-6)

The current Olympiastadion was built for the [1936 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") in the western part of the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-7) Since 1985, the stadium has hosted the finals of both the [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal "DFB-Pokal") and its [female equivalent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal_(women) "DFB-Pokal (women)"). The Olympiastadion hosts the [Internationales Stadionfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISTAF_Berlin "ISTAF Berlin"), which was an [IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") event from 1998 to 2009. The stadium hosted the [2009 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Host1-8)

Aside from its use as an Olympic stadium, the Olympiastadion has a strong footballing tradition, having been the home of [Hertha BSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertha_BSC "Hertha BSC") since 1963.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-9) It was also used for three matches at the [1974 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup"), and was renovated ahead of the [2006 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), at which it hosted six matches, including the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2006 FIFA World Cup final").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-report-10)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

This was the eighth European Cup/UEFA Champions League final for both Juventus and Barcelona.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-11) Juventus won two of their previous finals ([1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_European_Cup_final "1985 European Cup final"), [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1996 UEFA Champions League final")) and lost five ([1973](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_European_Cup_final "1973 European Cup final"), [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_European_Cup_final "1983 European Cup final"), [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1997 UEFA Champions League final"), [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1998 UEFA Champions League final"), [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final")), while Barcelona won four of their previous finals ([1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_final "1992 European Cup final"), [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2006 UEFA Champions League final"), [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"), [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2011 UEFA Champions League final")) and lost three ([1961](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_European_Cup_final "1961 European Cup final"), [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_European_Cup_final "1986 European Cup final"), [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final")). Barcelona also played in six [Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup") finals (winning in [1979](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1979 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1982 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1989 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1997 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final"), and losing in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1969 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1991 European Cup Winners' Cup final")), while Juventus also played in one Cup Winners' Cup final (winning in [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1984 European Cup Winners' Cup final")) and four [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") finals (winning in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_UEFA_Cup_final "1977 UEFA Cup final"), [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_UEFA_Cup_final "1990 UEFA Cup final"), [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UEFA_Cup_final "1993 UEFA Cup final"), and losing in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Cup_final "1995 UEFA Cup final")).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-12)

The two teams had previously played six times in UEFA club competitions, but never in a final. In their previous UEFA club competition meetings, Barcelona won 2–1 on aggregate in the [1985–86 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985%E2%80%9386_European_Cup "1985–86 European Cup") quarter-finals and 3–2 on aggregate in the [1990–91 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1990–91 European Cup Winners' Cup") semi-finals, while Juventus won 3–2 on aggregate in the [2002–03 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_UEFA_Champions_League "2002–03 UEFA Champions League") quarter-finals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-13) They also played in the 1952 [Latin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Cup "Latin Cup") semi-finals, won by Barcelona 4–2, and the [1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970%E2%80%9371_Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup "1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup") second round, won by Juventus 4–2 on aggregate.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14)

Similar to the [2010 UEFA Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final"), both teams entered the final in the possibility of winning the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football) "Treble (association football)") of domestic league, domestic cup and Champions League titles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-15) Juventus were crowned champions of the [2014–15 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Serie_A "2014–15 Serie A") on 2 May, and won the [2015 Coppa Italia final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Coppa_Italia_final "2015 Coppa Italia final") eighteen days later. Barcelona were crowned champions of the [2014–15 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_La_Liga "2014–15 La Liga") on 17 May, and won the [2015 Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Copa_del_Rey_final "2015 Copa del Rey final") thirteen days later. While it would have been the first treble for Juventus, Barcelona had previously won the treble in [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_FC_Barcelona_season "2008–09 FC Barcelona season").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-16)
