### Juventus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Juventus")]

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Carlos_T%C3%A9vez%2C_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus%2C_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG/250px-Carlos_T%C3%A9vez%2C_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus%2C_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carlos_T%C3%A9vez,_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus,_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG)

[Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez") scored seven goals in Juventus' run to the final.

As winners of the [2013–14 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Serie_A "2013–14 Serie A"), Juventus qualified automatically for the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage "2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage"). They were seeded second in Group A featuring – in seeded order – [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") (champions of the [2013–14 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga")), [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") (champions of the [2013–14 Super League Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Super_League_Greece "2013–14 Super League Greece")), and [Malmö FF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malm%C3%B6_FF "Malmö FF") (champions of the [2013 Allsvenskan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Allsvenskan "2013 Allsvenskan")).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17)

Their campaign began on 16 September, hosting Malmö at the [Juventus Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_Stadium "Juventus Stadium"), winning 2–0 through second-half goals by [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) On 1 October, they travelled to face Atlético at the [Vicente Calderón Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium"), losing by a sole goal from [Arda Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arda_Turan "Arda Turan") late on, a result that left all four teams level on three points apiece.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) Three weeks later Juventus again lost by one goal on their travels, [Pajtim Kasami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pajtim_Kasami "Pajtim Kasami") scoring in the first half for Olympiacos, whose goalkeeper [Roberto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Jim%C3%A9nez_Gago "Roberto Jiménez Gago") played a key role.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20) On 4 November, hosting the Greeks, Juventus won 3–2 after trailing 1–2, getting two goals in as many minutes from Roberto's [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal") and [Paul Pogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Pogba "Paul Pogba")'s winning strike.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21)

On 26 November, Juventus won away for the first time in the group, with second-half goals from [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente") and Tevez at Malmö's [Swedbank Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedbank_Stadion "Swedbank Stadion").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-22) In the final group game on 9 December, they hosted a goalless draw against Atlético, which sent both teams through, but Juventus in second place.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-23)

As group runners-up, Juventus had to face a group winner – Germans [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") of Group D – in the [last 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"). They won 2–1 at home in the first leg on 24 February 2015, with all the goals in the first half – visitor [Marco Reus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Reus "Marco Reus") equalised either side of strikes from Tevez and [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-24) The same forwards were on target in the second leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion") on 18 March – Tevez scored twice, including in the third minute – as Juventus won 3–0, and 5–1 on aggregate.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25)

In the quarter-finals, Juventus faced [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC"), runners-up in the [2013–14 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Ligue_1 "2013–14 Ligue 1"). The only goal of the tie came in the first leg at home on 14 April, [Arturo Vidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Vidal "Arturo Vidal") scoring a [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") after [Ricardo Carvalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Carvalho "Ricardo Carvalho") tripped Morata.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26) It was their first advancement into the semi-finals for 12 years.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-27)

On 5 May, Juventus hosted reigning champions [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") at Juventus Stadium. Morata opened the scoring against his former team, and [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") equalised before half time. Tevez scored the winning goal from the penalty spot after he was fouled by [Dani Carvajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Carvajal "Dani Carvajal").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) Eight days later, the two teams drew at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"): Ronaldo scored a penalty after [Giorgio Chiellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Chiellini "Giorgio Chiellini") fouled [James Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodr%C3%ADguez "James Rodríguez"), but in the second half Morata equalised. Juventus advanced to the final 3–2 on aggregate.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29)

### Barcelona

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Barcelona")]

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg/250px-2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg)

[Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") scored ten times in Barcelona's progress to the final, including a hat-trick away to [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL_FC "APOEL FC").

Barcelona qualified for the group stage as runners-up to Atlético in the previous season's La Liga. They were the top seeds in Group F, alongside – in order – [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC") (winners of the [2013–14 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Ligue_1 "2013–14 Ligue 1")), [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") (winners of the [2013–14 Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Eredivisie "2013–14 Eredivisie")) and [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL_FC "APOEL FC") (winners of the [2013–14 Cypriot First Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Cypriot_First_Division "2013–14 Cypriot First Division")).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30)

In their first game of the group, defender [Gerard Piqué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Piqu%C3%A9 "Gerard Piqué") headed the only goal to defeat [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL "APOEL") at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") on 17 September.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) However, thirteen days later at the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes"), they fell 3–2 to Paris Saint-Germain.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-32) On 21 October, Barcelona hosted Ajax and got first-half goals through [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") and [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"); [Anwar El Ghazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_El_Ghazi "Anwar El Ghazi") scored for the visitors with two minutes to play but [Sandro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandro_Ram%C3%ADrez "Sandro Ramírez")'s added-time strike confirmed a 3–1 win.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) Barcelona travelled to the [Amsterdam Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Arena "Amsterdam Arena") on 5 November and defeated Ajax 2–0 with a Messi goal in each half; he equalled the tournament's record of 71 overall goals.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34)

On 25 November, Barcelona played APOEL at the [GSP Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GSP_Stadium "GSP Stadium") in [Nicosia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicosia "Nicosia"), winning 4–0 with a hat-trick from Messi and a further goal from [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez"); Messi became the competition's all-time top scorer.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) Barcelona won the group with a 3–1 home win over PSG on 10 December. They initially fell behind to a goal by [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimovi%C4%87 "Zlatan Ibrahimović"), but replied with a goal each from the South American forward line of Messi, Neymar and Suárez.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36)

In the last 16, Barcelona faced [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C."), winners of the [2013–14 Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League") and Group E runners-up. In the first leg at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium") on 24 February 2015, Suárez scored twice in the first 30 minutes, and [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") got a goal back for the hosts after the break.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-37) In the return game on 18 March, City goalkeeper [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart") limited Barcelona to a single goal by [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"), and Barcelona advanced 3–1 on aggregate.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-38)

Barcelona met PSG again in the quarter-finals. On 15 April in Paris, Neymar scored the only goal of the first half and Suárez added two more, with the hosts getting a consolation through [Jérémy Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Mathieu "Jérémy Mathieu")'s own goal.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) Six days later, two first-half goals from Neymar sealed a 5–1 aggregate win.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-40)

In the semi-finals, Barcelona's opponents were [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayern_Munich "Bayern Munich"), winners of the [2013–14 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Bundesliga "2013–14 Bundesliga"). They hosted the first leg on 6 May, breaking the deadlock with two late goals from Messi in a three-minute spell, and an added-time addition by Neymar.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-41) Six days later at the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena"), Bayern took the lead through [Medhi Benatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medhi_Benatia "Medhi Benatia"), and Neymar put Barcelona into the lead by half time. Second-half goals by [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") and [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_M%C3%BCller "Thomas Müller") gave Bayern a 3–2 win on the night, but Barcelona advanced 5–3 on aggregate.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42)

[Karl-Heinz Riedle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Riedle "Karl-Heinz Riedle") was named as the ambassador for the final.

Former Germany international player [Karl-Heinz Riedle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Riedle "Karl-Heinz Riedle"), who won the Champions League with [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") against Juventus in 1997, was named the ambassador for the final.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43)

### Logo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Logo")]

UEFA unveiled the visual identity of the final on 29 August 2014. It blends the stadium with the city's [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

### Ticketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ticketing")]

With a stadium capacity of 70,500, a total amount of 46,000 tickets were available to fans and the general public, with the two finalist teams receiving 20,000 tickets each and with 6,000 tickets being available for sale to fans worldwide via UEFA.com from 5 to 23 March 2015 in four price categories: €390, €280, €160, and €70.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The rest of 24,500 tickets were allocated to sponsors and officials.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46)

### Related events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Related events")]

The [2015 UEFA Women's Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League_final "2015 UEFA Women's Champions League final") was held on 14 May 2015 at the [Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark "Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark") in Berlin. Unlike recent years, in which the Women's Champions League final was held in the same week as the men's Champions League final, the two matches are separated by almost a month, as the [2015 FIFA Women's World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup "2015 FIFA Women's World Cup") started in early June.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47)

The annual UEFA Champions Festival was held between 4–7 June 2015 in the streets around [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Match")]

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Officials")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG/250px-C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG)

[Cüneyt Çakır](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r "Cüneyt Çakır") was the final's referee.

In May 2015, the officials were chosen for the final by UEFA, led by Turkish referee [Cüneyt Çakır](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r "Cüneyt Çakır"). His compatriots Bahattin Duran and Tarık Ongun were chosen as assistant referees, and fellow Turks [Hüseyin Göçek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%BCseyin_G%C3%B6%C3%A7ek "Hüseyin Göçek") and Barış Şimşek the additional assistants, with Mustafa Emre Eyisoy the reserve assistant. [Jonas Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Eriksson_(referee) "Jonas Eriksson (referee)"), of Sweden, was chosen as fourth official.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-50) Çakır is a UEFA elite referee, and has refereed at [UEFA Euro 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 "UEFA Euro 2012") and the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), as well as the [2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_Final "2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final").

Çakır was scrutinised by the British media in 2013 when he sent off [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s [Nani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nani_(footballer) "Nani (footballer)") in a Champions League round of 16 match and the English team went on to lose to Real Madrid.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-51) Manager [Alex Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson") was so enraged by the decision that he refused to speak to the media after the game.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-52) UEFA confirmed that no action would be taken against the referee, concluding that he made the correct judgement.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-53)

### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Team selection")]

Juventus defender [Giorgio Chiellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Chiellini "Giorgio Chiellini") was ruled out of the final with a calf injury picked up in training on 3 June.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-54) Barcelona had no injury concerns before the final.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55)

Barcelona's [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") had previously been involved in two controversies with players in the Juventus squad: in 2012, he was found guilty by an FA commission of using racially insulting language towards [Patrice Evra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Evra "Patrice Evra") in a game between their respective former clubs [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") and Manchester United, and at the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") he escaped punishment for biting Chiellini but was punished retrospectively. Evra stated that he would shake Suárez's hand before the game, after Suarez had refused to shake his hand in their last match.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Summary")]

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg/250px-2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg)

[Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)") came on as a substitute for the last of his 767 Barcelona appearances.

In the second minute, Barcelona's [Javier Mascherano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Mascherano "Javier Mascherano") conceded a corner kick, which Juventus aimed at Evra but Barcelona cleared it. However two minutes later, [Jordi Alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordi_Alba "Jordi Alba") made a run on Barcelona's left, passing to [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") and then [Andrés Iniesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Iniesta "Andrés Iniesta") who set up [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić") to score the first goal from close range. Rakitić's goal was Barcelona's fastest goal in a Champions League final,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57) and the fourth fastest in a Champions League final overall.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58) In the 11th minute, [Arturo Vidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Vidal "Arturo Vidal") of Juventus received the first yellow card for fouling [Sergio Busquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets"). At half time, Barcelona led 1–0.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

Ten minutes into the second half, Juventus equalised: [Claudio Marchisio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Marchisio "Claudio Marchisio") back-heeled the ball to right-back [Stephan Lichtsteiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephan_Lichtsteiner "Stephan Lichtsteiner"), who set up [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez"). Barcelona goalkeeper [Marc-André ter Stegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc-Andr%C3%A9_ter_Stegen "Marc-André ter Stegen") blocked the shot from Tevez, but [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata") levelled the scores by putting the rebound into the net. In the 67th minute, Juventus appealed for a penalty when [Paul Pogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Pogba "Paul Pogba") went down in the area when challenged by [Dani Alves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Alves "Dani Alves"), but the referee did not give it. Two minutes later, Barcelona took the lead again when [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") shot from the edge of the area, [Gianluigi Buffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Buffon "Gianluigi Buffon") blocked it and Suárez put in the rebound. Soon after, Neymar put the ball into the net from Alba's cross, but it was disallowed as the referee deemed that Neymar had headed it into his own hand.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

In the 78th minute, Barcelona substituted Iniesta, who gave his captain's armband to [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)"), making his 767th and final appearance for Barcelona.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-xavi-60) Soon after, Juventus made three substitutions in quick succession: Vidal was replaced with [Roberto Pereyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Pereyra "Roberto Pereyra") and Morata with [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente"), while Evra made way for [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman"). In added time, Barcelona made their final two changes, as Rakitić made way for [Jérémy Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Mathieu "Jérémy Mathieu") and the limping Suárez for [Pedro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_(footballer,_born_1987) "Pedro (footballer, born 1987)").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) In the final added minute, Alves handled the ball near the halfway line, and Juventus launched the resulting free kick towards the Barcelona goal, where it was cleared. The ensuing counter-attack ended with Pedro giving an assist to Neymar, who scored the final kick to make it 3–1.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 122](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Neymar_%2816245492137%29.jpg/250px-Neymar_%2816245492137%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neymar_(16245492137).jpg)

[Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar")'s tenth goal of the season in the final meant that three players shared the honour of top scorer.

With the win, Barcelona became the first European club to achieve the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)") twice.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) Their fifth European title put them joint third with [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C."), until Liverpool won the [2019 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2019 UEFA Champions League final") to achieve their sixth title. Bayern also went on to win their sixth trophy a year later, in the [2020 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2020 UEFA Champions League final"). If only the Champions League era is considered, this is their fourth title, putting them one title behind [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-records-65) Madrid extended their lead by winning a fifth title in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2016 UEFA Champions League final") and, as of [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2024 UEFA Champions League final"), they have won nine titles in the Champions League era.

[![Image 123](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg/250px-Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg)

The UEFA Champions League trophy in [FC Barcelona Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_Museum "FC Barcelona Museum").

On the other hand, Juventus became the first team to lose six finals: they previously shared the record with [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") and [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-records-65)[Patrice Evra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Evra "Patrice Evra") became the first player to play in four losing UEFA Champions League finals, having previously been a runner-up in 2004 (with [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC")), 2009 and 2011 (both with Manchester United).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)

Neymar's goal meant that three players shared the title of top scorer in the competition, alongside Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. He became the first player since [Kaká](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kak%C3%A1 "Kaká") in [2006–07](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_UEFA_Champions_League "2006–07 UEFA Champions League") to be top scorer apart from those two. Messi was the top assister with six, with Ronaldo among the runners-up with four. After the final, both Messi and Ronaldo had a record 77 Champions League goals, but Ronaldo had one more if qualifiers were to be included.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-67)

The **2015 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2014–15 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League "2014–15 UEFA Champions League"), the 60th season of Europe's premier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), and the 23rd season since it was renamed from the European Champion Clubs' Cup to the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was played at the [Olympiastadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), Germany, on 6 June 2015, between Italian side [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") and Spanish side [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").

For the second time – after [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final") – both teams came into the final with the possibility of definitively winning a [continental treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)"), having each won their national league and cup for the season. Barcelona scored the only goal of the first half after four minutes, through [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"). Ten minutes after the interval, Juventus equalised with a goal by [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata"). In the 68th minute, [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") put Barcelona back in the lead, and Barcelona's win was confirmed when [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") scored with the last kick of the game. It was Barcelona's fifth trophy in the competition, and sealed their second treble, the other coming in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"). It was also Juventus' sixth defeat in a European Cup final, the most by any club, a record they previously shared with [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") and [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica").

As winners, Barcelona earned the right to play against the winners of the [2014–15 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League "2014–15 UEFA Europa League"), [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in the [2015 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup "2015 UEFA Super Cup"), and won that match 5–4. They also qualified to enter the [2015 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2015 FIFA Club World Cup") in Japan as the UEFA representative, going on to beat Argentina's [River Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_River_Plate "CA River Plate") in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final "2015 FIFA Club World Cup final").

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Olympicstadium2.jpg/250px-Olympicstadium2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympicstadium2.jpg)

The Olympiastadion in Berlin hosted the final.

The [Olympiastadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") was announced as the venue for the final at the UEFA Executive Committee meeting in London on 23 May 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5) This was the first European Cup/Champions League final hosted in Berlin.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-6)

The current Olympiastadion was built for the [1936 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") in the western part of the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-7) Since 1985, the stadium has hosted the finals of both the [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal "DFB-Pokal") and its [female equivalent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal_(women) "DFB-Pokal (women)"). The Olympiastadion hosts the [Internationales Stadionfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISTAF_Berlin "ISTAF Berlin"), which was an [IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") event from 1998 to 2009. The stadium hosted the [2009 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Host1-8)

Aside from its use as an Olympic stadium, the Olympiastadion has a strong footballing tradition, having been the home of [Hertha BSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertha_BSC "Hertha BSC") since 1963.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-9) It was also used for three matches at the [1974 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup"), and was renovated ahead of the [2006 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), at which it hosted six matches, including the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2006 FIFA World Cup final").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-report-10)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

This was the eighth European Cup/UEFA Champions League final for both Juventus and Barcelona.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-11) Juventus won two of their previous finals ([1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_European_Cup_final "1985 European Cup final"), [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1996 UEFA Champions League final")) and lost five ([1973](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_European_Cup_final "1973 European Cup final"), [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_European_Cup_final "1983 European Cup final"), [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1997 UEFA Champions League final"), [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1998 UEFA Champions League final"), [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final")), while Barcelona won four of their previous finals ([1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_final "1992 European Cup final"), [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2006 UEFA Champions League final"), [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"), [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2011 UEFA Champions League final")) and lost three ([1961](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_European_Cup_final "1961 European Cup final"), [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_European_Cup_final "1986 European Cup final"), [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final")). Barcelona also played in six [Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup") finals (winning in [1979](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1979 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1982 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1989 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1997 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final"), and losing in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1969 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1991 European Cup Winners' Cup final")), while Juventus also played in one Cup Winners' Cup final (winning in [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1984 European Cup Winners' Cup final")) and four [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") finals (winning in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_UEFA_Cup_final "1977 UEFA Cup final"), [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_UEFA_Cup_final "1990 UEFA Cup final"), [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UEFA_Cup_final "1993 UEFA Cup final"), and losing in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Cup_final "1995 UEFA Cup final")).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-12)

The two teams had previously played six times in UEFA club competitions, but never in a final. In their previous UEFA club competition meetings, Barcelona won 2–1 on aggregate in the [1985–86 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985%E2%80%9386_European_Cup "1985–86 European Cup") quarter-finals and 3–2 on aggregate in the [1990–91 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1990–91 European Cup Winners' Cup") semi-finals, while Juventus won 3–2 on aggregate in the [2002–03 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_UEFA_Champions_League "2002–03 UEFA Champions League") quarter-finals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-13) They also played in the 1952 [Latin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Cup "Latin Cup") semi-finals, won by Barcelona 4–2, and the [1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970%E2%80%9371_Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup "1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup") second round, won by Juventus 4–2 on aggregate.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14)

Similar to the [2010 UEFA Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final"), both teams entered the final in the possibility of winning the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football) "Treble (association football)") of domestic league, domestic cup and Champions League titles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-15) Juventus were crowned champions of the [2014–15 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Serie_A "2014–15 Serie A") on 2 May, and won the [2015 Coppa Italia final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Coppa_Italia_final "2015 Coppa Italia final") eighteen days later. Barcelona were crowned champions of the [2014–15 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_La_Liga "2014–15 La Liga") on 17 May, and won the [2015 Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Copa_del_Rey_final "2015 Copa del Rey final") thirteen days later. While it would have been the first treble for Juventus, Barcelona had previously won the treble in [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_FC_Barcelona_season "2008–09 FC Barcelona season").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-16)

### Juventus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Juventus")]

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Carlos_T%C3%A9vez%2C_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus%2C_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG/250px-Carlos_T%C3%A9vez%2C_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus%2C_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carlos_T%C3%A9vez,_Real_Madrid_vs_Juventus,_24_October_2013_Champions_League.JPG)

[Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez") scored seven goals in Juventus' run to the final.

As winners of the [2013–14 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Serie_A "2013–14 Serie A"), Juventus qualified automatically for the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage "2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage"). They were seeded second in Group A featuring – in seeded order – [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") (champions of the [2013–14 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga")), [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") (champions of the [2013–14 Super League Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Super_League_Greece "2013–14 Super League Greece")), and [Malmö FF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malm%C3%B6_FF "Malmö FF") (champions of the [2013 Allsvenskan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Allsvenskan "2013 Allsvenskan")).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17)

Their campaign began on 16 September, hosting Malmö at the [Juventus Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_Stadium "Juventus Stadium"), winning 2–0 through second-half goals by [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) On 1 October, they travelled to face Atlético at the [Vicente Calderón Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium"), losing by a sole goal from [Arda Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arda_Turan "Arda Turan") late on, a result that left all four teams level on three points apiece.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) Three weeks later Juventus again lost by one goal on their travels, [Pajtim Kasami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pajtim_Kasami "Pajtim Kasami") scoring in the first half for Olympiacos, whose goalkeeper [Roberto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Jim%C3%A9nez_Gago "Roberto Jiménez Gago") played a key role.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20) On 4 November, hosting the Greeks, Juventus won 3–2 after trailing 1–2, getting two goals in as many minutes from Roberto's [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal") and [Paul Pogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Pogba "Paul Pogba")'s winning strike.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21)

On 26 November, Juventus won away for the first time in the group, with second-half goals from [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente") and Tevez at Malmö's [Swedbank Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedbank_Stadion "Swedbank Stadion").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-22) In the final group game on 9 December, they hosted a goalless draw against Atlético, which sent both teams through, but Juventus in second place.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-23)

As group runners-up, Juventus had to face a group winner – Germans [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") of Group D – in the [last 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"). They won 2–1 at home in the first leg on 24 February 2015, with all the goals in the first half – visitor [Marco Reus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Reus "Marco Reus") equalised either side of strikes from Tevez and [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-24) The same forwards were on target in the second leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion") on 18 March – Tevez scored twice, including in the third minute – as Juventus won 3–0, and 5–1 on aggregate.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25)

In the quarter-finals, Juventus faced [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC"), runners-up in the [2013–14 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Ligue_1 "2013–14 Ligue 1"). The only goal of the tie came in the first leg at home on 14 April, [Arturo Vidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Vidal "Arturo Vidal") scoring a [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") after [Ricardo Carvalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Carvalho "Ricardo Carvalho") tripped Morata.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26) It was their first advancement into the semi-finals for 12 years.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-27)

On 5 May, Juventus hosted reigning champions [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") at Juventus Stadium. Morata opened the scoring against his former team, and [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") equalised before half time. Tevez scored the winning goal from the penalty spot after he was fouled by [Dani Carvajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Carvajal "Dani Carvajal").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) Eight days later, the two teams drew at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"): Ronaldo scored a penalty after [Giorgio Chiellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Chiellini "Giorgio Chiellini") fouled [James Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodr%C3%ADguez "James Rodríguez"), but in the second half Morata equalised. Juventus advanced to the final 3–2 on aggregate.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29)

### Barcelona

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Barcelona")]

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg/250px-2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_64_crop.jpg)

[Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") scored ten times in Barcelona's progress to the final, including a hat-trick away to [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL_FC "APOEL FC").

Barcelona qualified for the group stage as runners-up to Atlético in the previous season's La Liga. They were the top seeds in Group F, alongside – in order – [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC") (winners of the [2013–14 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Ligue_1 "2013–14 Ligue 1")), [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") (winners of the [2013–14 Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Eredivisie "2013–14 Eredivisie")) and [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL_FC "APOEL FC") (winners of the [2013–14 Cypriot First Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Cypriot_First_Division "2013–14 Cypriot First Division")).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30)

In their first game of the group, defender [Gerard Piqué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Piqu%C3%A9 "Gerard Piqué") headed the only goal to defeat [APOEL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APOEL "APOEL") at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") on 17 September.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) However, thirteen days later at the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes"), they fell 3–2 to Paris Saint-Germain.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-32) On 21 October, Barcelona hosted Ajax and got first-half goals through [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") and [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"); [Anwar El Ghazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_El_Ghazi "Anwar El Ghazi") scored for the visitors with two minutes to play but [Sandro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandro_Ram%C3%ADrez "Sandro Ramírez")'s added-time strike confirmed a 3–1 win.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) Barcelona travelled to the [Amsterdam Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Arena "Amsterdam Arena") on 5 November and defeated Ajax 2–0 with a Messi goal in each half; he equalled the tournament's record of 71 overall goals.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34)

On 25 November, Barcelona played APOEL at the [GSP Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GSP_Stadium "GSP Stadium") in [Nicosia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicosia "Nicosia"), winning 4–0 with a hat-trick from Messi and a further goal from [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez"); Messi became the competition's all-time top scorer.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) Barcelona won the group with a 3–1 home win over PSG on 10 December. They initially fell behind to a goal by [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimovi%C4%87 "Zlatan Ibrahimović"), but replied with a goal each from the South American forward line of Messi, Neymar and Suárez.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36)

In the last 16, Barcelona faced [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C."), winners of the [2013–14 Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League") and Group E runners-up. In the first leg at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium") on 24 February 2015, Suárez scored twice in the first 30 minutes, and [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") got a goal back for the hosts after the break.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-37) In the return game on 18 March, City goalkeeper [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart") limited Barcelona to a single goal by [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"), and Barcelona advanced 3–1 on aggregate.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-38)

Barcelona met PSG again in the quarter-finals. On 15 April in Paris, Neymar scored the only goal of the first half and Suárez added two more, with the hosts getting a consolation through [Jérémy Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Mathieu "Jérémy Mathieu")'s own goal.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) Six days later, two first-half goals from Neymar sealed a 5–1 aggregate win.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-40)

In the semi-finals, Barcelona's opponents were [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayern_Munich "Bayern Munich"), winners of the [2013–14 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Bundesliga "2013–14 Bundesliga"). They hosted the first leg on 6 May, breaking the deadlock with two late goals from Messi in a three-minute spell, and an added-time addition by Neymar.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-41) Six days later at the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena"), Bayern took the lead through [Medhi Benatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medhi_Benatia "Medhi Benatia"), and Neymar put Barcelona into the lead by half time. Second-half goals by [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") and [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_M%C3%BCller "Thomas Müller") gave Bayern a 3–2 win on the night, but Barcelona advanced 5–3 on aggregate.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42)

### Ambassador

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Ambassador")]

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Karl-Heinz_Riedle%2C_2012.jpg/250px-Karl-Heinz_Riedle%2C_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Karl-Heinz_Riedle,_2012.jpg)

[Karl-Heinz Riedle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Riedle "Karl-Heinz Riedle") was named as the ambassador for the final.

Former Germany international player [Karl-Heinz Riedle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Riedle "Karl-Heinz Riedle"), who won the Champions League with [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") against Juventus in 1997, was named the ambassador for the final.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43)

### Logo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Logo")]

UEFA unveiled the visual identity of the final on 29 August 2014. It blends the stadium with the city's [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

### Ticketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ticketing")]

With a stadium capacity of 70,500, a total amount of 46,000 tickets were available to fans and the general public, with the two finalist teams receiving 20,000 tickets each and with 6,000 tickets being available for sale to fans worldwide via UEFA.com from 5 to 23 March 2015 in four price categories: €390, €280, €160, and €70.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The rest of 24,500 tickets were allocated to sponsors and officials.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46)

### Related events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Related events")]

The [2015 UEFA Women's Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League_final "2015 UEFA Women's Champions League final") was held on 14 May 2015 at the [Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark "Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark") in Berlin. Unlike recent years, in which the Women's Champions League final was held in the same week as the men's Champions League final, the two matches are separated by almost a month, as the [2015 FIFA Women's World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup "2015 FIFA Women's World Cup") started in early June.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47)

The annual UEFA Champions Festival was held between 4–7 June 2015 in the streets around [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

### Opening ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Opening ceremony")]

The UEFA Champions League Anthem is performed by German soprano [Nina Maria Fischer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Maria_Fischer?action=edit&redlink=1 "Nina Maria Fischer (page does not exist)") and Spanish tenor [Manuel Gomez Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Gomez_Ruiz?action=edit&redlink=1 "Manuel Gomez Ruiz (page does not exist)"), the first time it had been performed as a duet.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-49)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Match")]

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Officials")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG/250px-C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r.JPG)

[Cüneyt Çakır](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r "Cüneyt Çakır") was the final's referee.

In May 2015, the officials were chosen for the final by UEFA, led by Turkish referee [Cüneyt Çakır](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BCneyt_%C3%87ak%C4%B1r "Cüneyt Çakır"). His compatriots Bahattin Duran and Tarık Ongun were chosen as assistant referees, and fellow Turks [Hüseyin Göçek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%BCseyin_G%C3%B6%C3%A7ek "Hüseyin Göçek") and Barış Şimşek the additional assistants, with Mustafa Emre Eyisoy the reserve assistant. [Jonas Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Eriksson_(referee) "Jonas Eriksson (referee)"), of Sweden, was chosen as fourth official.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-50) Çakır is a UEFA elite referee, and has refereed at [UEFA Euro 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 "UEFA Euro 2012") and the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), as well as the [2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_Final "2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final").

Çakır was scrutinised by the British media in 2013 when he sent off [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s [Nani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nani_(footballer) "Nani (footballer)") in a Champions League round of 16 match and the English team went on to lose to Real Madrid.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-51) Manager [Alex Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson") was so enraged by the decision that he refused to speak to the media after the game.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-52) UEFA confirmed that no action would be taken against the referee, concluding that he made the correct judgement.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-53)

### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Team selection")]

Juventus defender [Giorgio Chiellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Chiellini "Giorgio Chiellini") was ruled out of the final with a calf injury picked up in training on 3 June.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-54) Barcelona had no injury concerns before the final.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55)

Barcelona's [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") had previously been involved in two controversies with players in the Juventus squad: in 2012, he was found guilty by an FA commission of using racially insulting language towards [Patrice Evra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Evra "Patrice Evra") in a game between their respective former clubs [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") and Manchester United, and at the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") he escaped punishment for biting Chiellini but was punished retrospectively. Evra stated that he would shake Suárez's hand before the game, after Suarez had refused to shake his hand in their last match.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Summary")]

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg/250px-2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2012_2013_-_06_Xavi_Hern%C3%A1ndez.jpg)

[Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)") came on as a substitute for the last of his 767 Barcelona appearances.

In the second minute, Barcelona's [Javier Mascherano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Mascherano "Javier Mascherano") conceded a corner kick, which Juventus aimed at Evra but Barcelona cleared it. However two minutes later, [Jordi Alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordi_Alba "Jordi Alba") made a run on Barcelona's left, passing to [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") and then [Andrés Iniesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Iniesta "Andrés Iniesta") who set up [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić") to score the first goal from close range. Rakitić's goal was Barcelona's fastest goal in a Champions League final,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57) and the fourth fastest in a Champions League final overall.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58) In the 11th minute, [Arturo Vidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Vidal "Arturo Vidal") of Juventus received the first yellow card for fouling [Sergio Busquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets"). At half time, Barcelona led 1–0.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

Ten minutes into the second half, Juventus equalised: [Claudio Marchisio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Marchisio "Claudio Marchisio") back-heeled the ball to right-back [Stephan Lichtsteiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephan_Lichtsteiner "Stephan Lichtsteiner"), who set up [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez"). Barcelona goalkeeper [Marc-André ter Stegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc-Andr%C3%A9_ter_Stegen "Marc-André ter Stegen") blocked the shot from Tevez, but [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata") levelled the scores by putting the rebound into the net. In the 67th minute, Juventus appealed for a penalty when [Paul Pogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Pogba "Paul Pogba") went down in the area when challenged by [Dani Alves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Alves "Dani Alves"), but the referee did not give it. Two minutes later, Barcelona took the lead again when [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") shot from the edge of the area, [Gianluigi Buffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Buffon "Gianluigi Buffon") blocked it and Suárez put in the rebound. Soon after, Neymar put the ball into the net from Alba's cross, but it was disallowed as the referee deemed that Neymar had headed it into his own hand.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

In the 78th minute, Barcelona substituted Iniesta, who gave his captain's armband to [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)"), making his 767th and final appearance for Barcelona.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-xavi-60) Soon after, Juventus made three substitutions in quick succession: Vidal was replaced with [Roberto Pereyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Pereyra "Roberto Pereyra") and Morata with [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente"), while Evra made way for [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman"). In added time, Barcelona made their final two changes, as Rakitić made way for [Jérémy Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Mathieu "Jérémy Mathieu") and the limping Suárez for [Pedro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_(footballer,_born_1987) "Pedro (footballer, born 1987)").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) In the final added minute, Alves handled the ball near the halfway line, and Juventus launched the resulting free kick towards the Barcelona goal, where it was cleared. The ensuing counter-attack ended with Pedro giving an assist to Neymar, who scored the final kick to make it 3–1.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-59)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 122](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Neymar_%2816245492137%29.jpg/250px-Neymar_%2816245492137%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neymar_(16245492137).jpg)

[Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar")'s tenth goal of the season in the final meant that three players shared the honour of top scorer.

With the win, Barcelona became the first European club to achieve the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)") twice.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) Their fifth European title put them joint third with [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C."), until Liverpool won the [2019 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2019 UEFA Champions League final") to achieve their sixth title. Bayern also went on to win their sixth trophy a year later, in the [2020 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2020 UEFA Champions League final"). If only the Champions League era is considered, this is their fourth title, putting them one title behind [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-records-65) Madrid extended their lead by winning a fifth title in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2016 UEFA Champions League final") and, as of [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2024 UEFA Champions League final"), they have won nine titles in the Champions League era.

[![Image 123](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg/250px-Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Col%C2%B7leccions_del_Museu_del_FC_Barcelona_27.jpg)

The UEFA Champions League trophy in [FC Barcelona Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_Museum "FC Barcelona Museum").

On the other hand, Juventus became the first team to lose six finals: they previously shared the record with [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") and [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-records-65)[Patrice Evra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Evra "Patrice Evra") became the first player to play in four losing UEFA Champions League finals, having previously been a runner-up in 2004 (with [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC")), 2009 and 2011 (both with Manchester United).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)

Neymar's goal meant that three players shared the title of top scorer in the competition, alongside Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. He became the first player since [Kaká](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kak%C3%A1 "Kaká") in [2006–07](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_UEFA_Champions_League "2006–07 UEFA Champions League") to be top scorer apart from those two. Messi was the top assister with six, with Ronaldo among the runners-up with four. After the final, both Messi and Ronaldo had a record 77 Champions League goals, but Ronaldo had one more if qualifiers were to be included.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-67)
