#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 39](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1c/PaoloMaldini.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PaoloMaldini.jpg)

Milan captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") scored in the first minute of the match

Liverpool fielded a [4–4–1–1 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%931%E2%80%931 "Formation (association football)"), with the surprise inclusion in the squad being [Harry Kewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kewell "Harry Kewell"), who played just behind Milan Baroš, who himself had been picked ahead of Djibril Cissé. The inclusion of Kewell meant [Dietmar Hamann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Hamann "Dietmar Hamann") was left on the [substitutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)")' bench and [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso") and [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") started in the centre of midfield. Milan fielded a 4–4–2 diamond formation, with [Hernán Crespo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Crespo "Hernán Crespo") preferred to [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson") and [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi"), who was not included in the match day squad. Liverpool lined up in their red home kit, whilst Milan wore a changed strip of all white, which they historically used in European Cup finals. Liverpool won the [coin toss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin_flipping "Coin flipping") and kicked off.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29)

Milan scored within the first minute of the match after captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") volleyed in an [Andrea Pirlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo")[free kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indirect_free_kick "Indirect free kick") that had been conceded by [Djimi Traoré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djimi_Traor%C3%A9 "Djimi Traoré"). The goal made Maldini the oldest scorer in the history of the competition.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29) Liverpool responded almost immediately; [John Arne Riise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Arne_Riise "John Arne Riise"), who was picked out by a [corner kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") from Steven Gerrard, hit a volley from the edge of the penalty box. His shot was cleared only for Gerrard to cross in from the right wing, which [Sami Hyypiä](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Hyypi%C3%A4 "Sami Hyypiä") headed towards goal producing a save out of [Dida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dida_(footballer,_born_1973) "Dida (footballer, born 1973)"). Milan almost extended their lead in the 13th minute, after Crespo's header was cleared off the goal line by [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)"). A few minutes later, Liverpool made a substitution after Harry Kewell picked up a groin injury; he was replaced by [Vladimír Šmicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_%C5%A0micer "Vladimír Šmicer"). Soon after, [Kaká](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kak%C3%A1 "Kaká") passed through to [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") who put his shot past Liverpool goalkeeper [Jerzy Dudek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek "Jerzy Dudek"), but Shevchenko was adjudged to have been in an [offside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offside_(association_football) "Offside (association football)") position and the goal did not stand. Shevchenko had another chance to score a few minutes later; after being played onside by Traore, his shot was saved by Dudek after he came under pressure from the Liverpool defence. Luis García had two chances to score following Shevchenko's shot; the first shot from the edge of the penalty area went well over the [crossbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sport) "Goal (sport)") and after he was headed through by Baroš his next shot went wide. Straight after this attack, Crespo went through on goal only to be flagged for offside. Almost immediately after this, Liverpool had a penalty claim turned down after [Alessandro Nesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nesta "Alessandro Nesta") allegedly handballed. Milan countered and scored; Kaka dribbled the ball into the Liverpool half and passed to Shevchenko, who passed to Crespo at the far post to score and make it 2–0. Minutes later, Crespo extended Milan's lead with a chip over Dudek after Kaka provided the assist to make it 3–0.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Second half")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/The_big_4-0.jpg/250px-The_big_4-0.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_big_4-0.jpg)

[Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") scored a goal and won a penalty as Liverpool came from behind to win the final

At the start of the second half, Liverpool made a substitution with Dietmar Hamann replacing [Steve Finnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Finnan "Steve Finnan") and also changed to a 3–4–2–1 formation to reduce the deficit, with Riise and Šmicer on the flanks, Alonso and Hamann as holding midfielders and Gerrard playing as an attacking midfielder.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30) Liverpool had the best chance early on with Xabi Alonso sending an effort from 35 yards (32 m) narrowly past Milan's right hand post. Two minutes later, Shevchenko forced a save from Dudek with a strong free-kick from just outside the Liverpool box.

A minute after this, Liverpool scored through captain Gerrard, who connected with Riise's cross and lofted a header past Dida.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) Soon afterwards, Liverpool scored again as Šmicer beat Dida with a long-range shot into the bottom left-hand corner to leave Liverpool a goal behind. Three minutes after Šmicer's goal, Liverpool were awarded a penalty, after Gerrard made a run into the Milan box for Baros' lay-off and was brought down by [Gennaro Gattuso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gennaro_Gattuso "Gennaro Gattuso"). Alonso's penalty was saved, but he scored from the rebound to equalise for Liverpool. Milan and Liverpool had chances to take the lead after this, but [Clarence Seedorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_Seedorf "Clarence Seedorf") and Riise failed to score.

Milan almost took the lead in the 70th minute, after Dudek dropped a low cross towards Shevchenko, whose effort was cleared off the line by Traoré. Gerrard then had a chance to score but he sent his shot over the crossbar. About ten minutes later García could not control a pass from Gerrard which led to a Milan attack, Crespo played the ball back to Kaka, whose subsequent shot was blocked by Jamie Carragher. A number of substitutions were made before full-time with Liverpool replacing Milan Baroš with Djibril Cissé, while Milan replaced Hernán Crespo and Clarence Seedorf with Jon Dahl Tomasson and [Serginho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serginho_(footballer,_born_1971) "Serginho (footballer, born 1971)") respectively. Milan had the last chance before full-time but Kaka failed to direct [Jaap Stam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Stam "Jaap Stam")'s header towards goal, meaning the final went to [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") for the 13th time in the competition's history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

#### Extra time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Extra time")]

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg/250px-Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg)

Liverpool goalkeeper [Jerzy Dudek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek "Jerzy Dudek") described his second save from [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") in the 117th minute as "the save of my life".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Double_save-33)

Liverpool kicked off the first half of extra time. Pirlo had a chance in the early stages, but he put his shot over the crossbar. Tomasson came close in the later stages of the first period of extra time, but he could not make contact with the ball. Šmicer required treatment for [cramp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramp "Cramp") towards the end of the first period, as a number of Liverpool players felt fatigued. Liverpool had most of the early exchanges after winning two corners, but could not score. Shortly afterwards, Milan made their final substitution, replacing Gennaro Gattuso with [Rui Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rui_Costa "Rui Costa").

The best chance of the second half of extra time came in the 117th minute (three minutes from penalties) when Shevchenko shot at goal. Dudek saved, only for it to rebound back out to Shevchenko, who again shot from under 3 yards (2.7 m), which Dudek saved again, pushing the shot over the bar.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Double_save-33) Liverpool had one last chance at the end of extra time, but John Arne Riise's free kick was blocked, and following this the referee signalled the end of extra time, which meant a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") would decide the championship.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

#### Penalties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Penalties")]

Liverpool and Milan had each won their last European Cups after winning penalty shoot-outs, and it was also the second time in three years that the final would be decided this way; previously, in the [2003 all-Italian final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final") at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford"), Milan had defeated Juventus 3–2.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29) Milan were first to take a penalty, but Serginho – who had taken Milan's first penalty in 2003 and scored – shot over the crossbar after attempts from Dudek to distract him, which mimicked [Bruce Grobbelaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Grobbelaar "Bruce Grobbelaar")'s "spaghetti legs" antics during the shootout in the [1984 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_European_Cup_final "1984 European Cup final") against [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma"). Dietmar Hamann took Liverpool's first penalty and, despite having a broken toe,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34) he scored to put Liverpool 1–0 up. Andrea Pirlo was next for Milan, and his penalty was saved by Dudek who dived low to his right. Cisse then scored his penalty to put Liverpool 2–0 up. Tomasson scored Milan's next penalty to make the score 2–1 in Liverpool's favour. Riise was next for Liverpool, but his penalty was saved by Dida. Kaká then scored the subsequent penalty to level the scores at 2–2. Šmicer took the next Liverpool penalty and scored with his eventual last competitive kick for Liverpool to put them on the brink of victory.

Shevchenko, who had scored the decisive penalty against Juventus' [Gianluigi Buffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Buffon "Gianluigi Buffon") in 2003, then had to score to keep Milan in the shootout.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) He hit his penalty straight down the middle of the goal and Dudek went down to his right, but blocked the shot with his left hand to give Liverpool a 3–2 win in the shoot-out.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Post-match")]

> Liverpool have their hands on the European Cup again, and this time [it's for keeps!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently "European Champion Clubs' Cup") That trophy isn't going anywhere but Anfield. Liverpool become only the third club in the history of the competition to win it five times, and earn the right to keep the cup forever.

—[Clive Tyldesley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Tyldesley "Clive Tyldesley") commentary on [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") as Gerrard lifted the trophy.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-37)

Liverpool's triumph marked their fifth European Cup and the first by an English team since [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") had defeated Bayern Munich in the [1999 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final") in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"). By winning the European Cup for a fifth time, Liverpool earned the privilege of wearing a [multiple-winner badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Multiple-winner_badge "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and the right to [keep the trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently "European Champion Clubs' Cup") (under normal competition rules, the winning club can keep the trophy for only 10 months, as they must deliver it to UEFA two months before the next year's final). Liverpool were given ownership of the trophy every winner had held aloft since [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1995 UEFA Champions League final") (after Milan were permanently given the previous trophy after their fifth win in [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final")).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-38) The [2005–06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League") participants competed for a new identical trophy. The rule to keep the trophy, which had been in effect since the [1968–69 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968%E2%80%9369_European_Cup "1968–69 European Cup"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) was changed for the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League "2008–09 UEFA Champions League") so that the actual trophy remained with UEFA at all times. Liverpool became the fifth and final club to be given this honour after Real Madrid, Ajax, Bayern Munich and Milan – all of whom had either won at least five times or three times consecutively.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UEFA_honours-40)

[![Image 127](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/CL_parade_Lpool.jpg/250px-CL_parade_Lpool.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CL_parade_Lpool.jpg)

The Liverpool team parading the Champions League trophy in Liverpool city centre after their victory.

Liverpool celebrated their victory by parading the trophy around [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") in an open-top [double-decker bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-decker_bus "Double-decker bus") the day after the final. They were cheered by approximately 1 million supporters, with an estimated 300,000 fans located around [St George's Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_Hall,_Liverpool "St George's Hall, Liverpool") – the final destination of the parade.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Parade-41) Business experts estimated that one in five workers took time off following the victory. It was also estimated that Liverpudlians drank around 10,000 bottles of champagne after the match, with supermarket chain [Sainsbury's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainsbury's "Sainsbury's") stating: "We've never seen anything like it. We would usually expect to sell this much champagne at Christmas".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Parade-41)

[![Image 128](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/2005_European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-2005_European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2005_European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup_(cropped).jpg)

The [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") trophy won by Liverpool in Istanbul, on display in the club's museum a few weeks after the match.

Liverpool manager [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") admitted after the match that the manner of his side's victory had stunned him and he stated: "My problem is that I don't have words to express the things that I feel at this moment".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42) Praise for Liverpool also came from outside England, including from Argentine legend [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona"), who said, "Even the Brazil team that won the [1970 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup") could not have staged a comeback with Milan leading 3–0... The English club proved that miracles really do exist. I've now made Liverpool my English team. They showed that football is the most beautiful sport of all. You knew they could defend, but the team showed they could play too and wrote a page in the history books. The match will last forever. The Liverpool supporters didn't let me go to sleep the night before. There were 10 of them to every three Milan supporters. They showed their unconditional support at half-time when they were losing 3–0 and still they didn't stop singing."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43)[Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff") similarly praised the supporters after the game, saying "There's not one club in Europe with an anthem like "[You'll Never Walk Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You'll_Never_Walk_Alone "You'll Never Walk Alone")." There's not one club in the world so united with the fans. I sat there watching the Liverpool fans and they sent shivers down my spine. A mass of 40,000 people became one force behind their team".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

Benítez was also prepared to break up his winning side after the final with a number of players expected to leave the club to make way for new arrivals. One of those leaving was [Vladimír Šmicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_%C5%A0micer "Vladimír Šmicer"), who had scored Liverpool's second goal in Istanbul, and whose contract was known not to be renewed before the final, meaning he entered knowing the final was his last game for the club. Milan were similarly astonished at the manner in which they had lost the final. Manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") said, "We had six minutes of madness in which we threw away the position we had reached until then".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-shattered-45) The result compounded Milan's failure to win [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") a week before the match. Milan's vice-president, [Adriano Galliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adriano_Galliani "Adriano Galliani"), played down the loss, asserting: "Even if we come second in the league, and second in the Champions League, this is not a disastrous season for us". Captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") was less optimistic, stating that the reverse was a "huge disappointment", but he added that Milan would accept the defeat and "go out with their heads high".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-shattered-45)

[![Image 129](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Liverpool_2005_ucl_medal.jpg/250px-Liverpool_2005_ucl_medal.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Liverpool_2005_ucl_medal.jpg)

Liverpool shirt from the final and a winners medal in the club's museum

Much discussion after the final centered on the future of Liverpool captain [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") who had been linked with a move to rivals [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."). Gerrard stated in the immediate aftermath of the victory, "How can I think of leaving Liverpool after a night like this?"[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46) Media reports then quoted Gerrard as saying he wished to leave Liverpool, citing events that had occurred in the month after the Champions League victory as the reason. On 6 July, however, Liverpool chief executive [Rick Parry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Parry "Rick Parry") released a statement confirming that Gerrard would remain at the club,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47) and Gerrard signed a new four-year contract on 8 July.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48) He ultimately never played for another club in Europe, as he departed for the [Los Angeles Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Galaxy "Los Angeles Galaxy") of [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") a decade later.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-49)

Despite winning the competition and the precedent that the holders defend their trophy, Liverpool's place in next season's Champions League was still in doubt. Prior to the 2005 Champions League final, [The Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") (FA) of England had decided on 5 May that only the top four finishers in the Premier League would qualify and Liverpool ended their domestic season in fifth place behind [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. The **2005 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2004–05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League")[UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), Europe's primary club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition. The showpiece event was contested between [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") of Italy and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") of England at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul") on 25 May 2005. Liverpool, who had won the competition four times, were appearing in their sixth final, and their first since [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_European_Cup_final "1985 European Cup final"). Milan, who had won the competition six times, were appearing in their second final in three years and tenth overall.

Each club needed to progress through the group stage and knockout rounds to reach the final, playing 12 matches in total. Liverpool finished second in their group behind [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2004 UEFA Champions League final") runners-up [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") and subsequently beat [Bayer Leverkusen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_04_Leverkusen "Bayer 04 Leverkusen"), [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") to progress to the final. Milan won their group ahead of [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") and faced [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") and [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven") before reaching the final.

Milan were regarded as favourites before the match and took the lead within the first minute through captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini"). Milan striker [Hernán Crespo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Crespo "Hernán Crespo") added two more goals before half-time to make it 3–0. In the second half Liverpool launched a comeback and scored three goals in a dramatic six-minute spell to level the scores at 3–3, with goals from [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard"), [Vladimír Šmicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_%C5%A0micer "Vladimír Šmicer") and [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso"). The scores remained the same during extra time, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was required to decide the champions. The score was 3–2 to Liverpool when [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko")'s penalty was saved by Liverpool goalkeeper [Jerzy Dudek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek "Jerzy Dudek"). It was Liverpool's fifth European Cup, which meant they were [awarded the trophy permanently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and the right to wear a [multiple-winner badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Multiple-winner_badge "European Champion Clubs' Cup"). Liverpool's comeback gave rise to the final being known as the _**Miracle of Istanbul**_, and is regarded as one of the greatest finals in the history of the tournament.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Winter-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-6)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

This was Liverpool's sixth final and it was their first appearance since the [1985 European Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_European_Cup_final "1985 European Cup final"), when they lost 1–0 to Juventus and were subsequently banned from European competition for six years due to the [Heysel Stadium disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster "Heysel Stadium disaster"). They had previously won the European Cup on four occasions in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_European_Cup_final "1977 European Cup final"), [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_European_Cup_final "1978 European Cup final"), [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_European_Cup_final "1981 European Cup final") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_European_Cup_final "1984 European Cup final"). The match was Milan's tenth appearance in the final. They had won on six occasions ([1963](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_European_Cup_final "1963 European Cup final"), [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_European_Cup_final "1969 European Cup final"), [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_final "1989 European Cup final"), [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final "1990 European Cup final"), [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final"), [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final")), and lost three times ([1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_European_Cup_final "1958 European Cup final"), [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1993 UEFA Champions League final"), [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1995 UEFA Champions League final")). In total the teams had participated in 14 finals between them.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-background-7) Prior to the game, Milan were assured of entering the Champions League the following season after finishing second in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Serie_A "2004–05 Serie A").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-8) Liverpool meanwhile had failed to finish in the top four in the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_FA_Premier_League "2004–05 FA Premier League"), and had to win the final to enter the competition the following season. Even if they did win the match, they were not assured of a place after UEFA failed to confirm whether they would allow Liverpool to defend the championship.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-9)[The Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") supported Liverpool, stating, "We have already submitted a written request to have an additional place, should they win the Champions League".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-10) Milan manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") said "I think a team that wins should have the right to defend it but we may just do the English federation a favour and solve this."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-11)

Milan were regarded as favourites and their team included many players who had experienced success in the competition. The most notable was captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini"), who had won the competition four times previously, all with Milan, and [Clarence Seedorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_Seedorf "Clarence Seedorf"), who had won the competition three times with three clubs. Liverpool had been considered underdogs throughout the competition, but had beaten more favoured opposition, including Juventus and Chelsea, to reach the final. Liverpool manager [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") acknowledged this: "Maybe Milan are favourites, but we have confidence, and we can win".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-preview-12)[Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") manager [Arsène Wenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ars%C3%A8ne_Wenger "Arsène Wenger") felt Liverpool would win the match: "I fancy Liverpool as Milan look jaded physically and certainly mentally, by losing the [Serie A] title, I think they have never had a better chance than now to beat Milan." Liverpool defender [Jamie Carragher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Carragher "Jamie Carragher") was not so optimistic, stating that the Liverpool side were not as good as the one that had won the [2001 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_UEFA_Cup_final "2001 UEFA Cup final"): "No disrespect to the squad we have got now but it is obvious we are not as strong as we were when we won the UEFA Cup in 2001. Back then we had a settled team and that season when we went into games against Barcelona and Roma, we always felt we were as good as them."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-13)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Venue")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Istanbul_Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium_1.jpg/250px-Istanbul_Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Istanbul_Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium_1.jpg)

The [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") held the final

The final was held at Istanbul's [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium"); it was the first time a European final had been held in Turkey. There were reservations about holding the final in Turkey but UEFA chief executive, [Lars-Christer Olsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars-Christer_Olsson "Lars-Christer Olsson") was satisfied by the assurances of the Turkish authorities: "The conditions there are the same, generally, as for all countries and they have given guarantees, this is important, especially since their experiences last autumn. We have also asked for additional investments in the infrastructure around the stadium and they have agreed to this, too."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14)

## Route to the final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Route to the final")]

Further information: [2004–05 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Gerrard_plinth%2C_96_Avenue.jpg/250px-Gerrard_plinth%2C_96_Avenue.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gerrard_plinth,_96_Avenue.jpg)

The [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") plinth outside [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield") inscribed with 86 minutes (the time of his strike for Liverpool against Olympiacos) and the commentary: "Oh, you beauty! What a hit son! What a hit!"

Teams qualified for the Champions League group stage, either directly or through three preliminary rounds, based on both their position in the preceding domestic league and [the strength of that league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#League_coefficient "UEFA coefficient"). The competition proper started with the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League#Group_stage "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"), contested as eight double [round-robin groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament") of four teams, with the top two qualifying for the knockout stages. The [knockout stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League#Knockout_stage "2004–05 UEFA Champions League") ties from the round of 16 to the semi-finals were decided based on [home and away matches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UEFA-15)

[Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") entered the competition in the group stage after winning [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Serie_A "2003–04 Serie A"). They won their group ahead of [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") and faced [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") and [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven") before reaching the final.

[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") entered the competition in the third qualifying round after finishing fourth in the [2003–04 FA Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_FA_Premier_League "2003–04 FA Premier League"). They faced Austrian side [GAK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grazer_AK "Grazer AK") and won the first leg 2–0 at Graz after two goals from [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") Steven Gerrard. They lost the second leg 1–0 at [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield") but progressed to the group stage by virtue of winning the tie 2–1 on aggregate. Liverpool finished second in their group behind [2004 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2004 UEFA Champions League final") runners-up [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC"). In Liverpool's [final group stage match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Liverpool_v_Olympiacos "2004–05 UEFA Champions League group stage") against [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") on 8 December, [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") scored a 25-yard half volley in the 86th minute to send the club through to the knockout round.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-16) A strike that saw co-commentator [Andy Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Gray_(footballer,_born_1955) "Andy Gray (footballer, born 1955)") exclaim, "Oh, you beauty! What a hit son! What a hit!", Gerrard stated it was his most important, if not his best, goal for Liverpool to date.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) In the knockout rounds, Liverpool beat [Bayer Leverkusen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_04_Leverkusen "Bayer 04 Leverkusen"), [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") to progress to the final. The winning goal in the semi-final scored by [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)") was dubbed a [ghost goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_goal#Etymology "Ghost goal") by Chelsea manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) He did however recognise the atmosphere generated by Liverpool fans in the match: "I felt the power of Anfield, it was magnificent."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21)

## Pre-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pre-match")]

### Ticketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ticketing")]

Each team was allocated 20,000 tickets for the final, out of a total of 69,000. 14,400 tickets were made available to the general public, with half of those allocated through a ballot on UEFA's website, and the other half reserved for Turkish fans by the [Turkish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Football_Federation "Turkish Football Federation"). The final 14,600 tickets were distributed to UEFA's "football family", consisting of UEFA officials, national football associations, commercial partners and broadcasters.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-24) Hotel rooms in the city were scarce, with the 100,000 available quickly booked by travel agents and fans.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25) At least 30,000 Liverpool fans made the trip to Istanbul, but only 20,000 were expected to have tickets. The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") reported early arrivals were lively but there was no violence and the mood between the two fans was friendly.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26)

### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Team selection")]

Milan were expected to field a [4–4–2 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%932 "Formation (association football)"), and there was much speculation about who would partner [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") in attack. [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi") and [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson") were touted, but it was expected that on-loan striker [Hernán Crespo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Crespo "Hernán Crespo") would be chosen. This was echoed by Milan manager Ancelotti: "I will not say if he will play from the start, but he will definitely play."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-preview-12) Liverpool were also expected to adopt a 4–4–2 formation. [Dietmar Hamann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Hamann "Dietmar Hamann") was expected to start ahead of [Igor Bišćan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Bi%C5%A1%C4%87an "Igor Bišćan"), and when questioned over whether [Djibril Cissé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djibril_Ciss%C3%A9 "Djibril Cissé") or [Milan Baroš](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Baro%C5%A1 "Milan Baroš") would start as main striker, Benítez replied, "Both are good enough, maybe both can play, why not?"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-preview-12)

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Officials")]

The referee for the final was [Manuel Mejuto González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Mejuto_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Manuel Mejuto González"), who led an all-Spanish crew of officials. His assistant referees were Oscar Martínez Samaniego and Clemente Ayete Plou, and the fourth official was [Arturo Daudén Ibáñez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Daud%C3%A9n_Ib%C3%A1%C3%B1ez "Arturo Daudén Ibáñez"). Mejuto González was only the third Spanish referee to officiate a European Cup final, following [Manuel Díaz Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_D%C3%ADaz_Vega "Manuel Díaz Vega") in [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1996 UEFA Champions League final") and [José María Ortiz de Mendíbil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Ortiz_de_Mend%C3%ADbil "José María Ortiz de Mendíbil") in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_European_Cup_final "1969 European Cup final").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-27)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 39](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1c/PaoloMaldini.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PaoloMaldini.jpg)

Milan captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") scored in the first minute of the match

Liverpool fielded a [4–4–1–1 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%931%E2%80%931 "Formation (association football)"), with the surprise inclusion in the squad being [Harry Kewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kewell "Harry Kewell"), who played just behind Milan Baroš, who himself had been picked ahead of Djibril Cissé. The inclusion of Kewell meant [Dietmar Hamann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Hamann "Dietmar Hamann") was left on the [substitutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)")' bench and [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso") and [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") started in the centre of midfield. Milan fielded a 4–4–2 diamond formation, with [Hernán Crespo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Crespo "Hernán Crespo") preferred to [Jon Dahl Tomasson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Dahl_Tomasson "Jon Dahl Tomasson") and [Filippo Inzaghi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi "Filippo Inzaghi"), who was not included in the match day squad. Liverpool lined up in their red home kit, whilst Milan wore a changed strip of all white, which they historically used in European Cup finals. Liverpool won the [coin toss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin_flipping "Coin flipping") and kicked off.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29)

Milan scored within the first minute of the match after captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") volleyed in an [Andrea Pirlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo")[free kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indirect_free_kick "Indirect free kick") that had been conceded by [Djimi Traoré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djimi_Traor%C3%A9 "Djimi Traoré"). The goal made Maldini the oldest scorer in the history of the competition.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29) Liverpool responded almost immediately; [John Arne Riise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Arne_Riise "John Arne Riise"), who was picked out by a [corner kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") from Steven Gerrard, hit a volley from the edge of the penalty box. His shot was cleared only for Gerrard to cross in from the right wing, which [Sami Hyypiä](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Hyypi%C3%A4 "Sami Hyypiä") headed towards goal producing a save out of [Dida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dida_(footballer,_born_1973) "Dida (footballer, born 1973)"). Milan almost extended their lead in the 13th minute, after Crespo's header was cleared off the goal line by [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)"). A few minutes later, Liverpool made a substitution after Harry Kewell picked up a groin injury; he was replaced by [Vladimír Šmicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_%C5%A0micer "Vladimír Šmicer"). Soon after, [Kaká](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kak%C3%A1 "Kaká") passed through to [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") who put his shot past Liverpool goalkeeper [Jerzy Dudek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek "Jerzy Dudek"), but Shevchenko was adjudged to have been in an [offside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offside_(association_football) "Offside (association football)") position and the goal did not stand. Shevchenko had another chance to score a few minutes later; after being played onside by Traore, his shot was saved by Dudek after he came under pressure from the Liverpool defence. Luis García had two chances to score following Shevchenko's shot; the first shot from the edge of the penalty area went well over the [crossbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sport) "Goal (sport)") and after he was headed through by Baroš his next shot went wide. Straight after this attack, Crespo went through on goal only to be flagged for offside. Almost immediately after this, Liverpool had a penalty claim turned down after [Alessandro Nesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nesta "Alessandro Nesta") allegedly handballed. Milan countered and scored; Kaka dribbled the ball into the Liverpool half and passed to Shevchenko, who passed to Crespo at the far post to score and make it 2–0. Minutes later, Crespo extended Milan's lead with a chip over Dudek after Kaka provided the assist to make it 3–0.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Second half")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/The_big_4-0.jpg/250px-The_big_4-0.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_big_4-0.jpg)

[Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") scored a goal and won a penalty as Liverpool came from behind to win the final

At the start of the second half, Liverpool made a substitution with Dietmar Hamann replacing [Steve Finnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Finnan "Steve Finnan") and also changed to a 3–4–2–1 formation to reduce the deficit, with Riise and Šmicer on the flanks, Alonso and Hamann as holding midfielders and Gerrard playing as an attacking midfielder.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30) Liverpool had the best chance early on with Xabi Alonso sending an effort from 35 yards (32 m) narrowly past Milan's right hand post. Two minutes later, Shevchenko forced a save from Dudek with a strong free-kick from just outside the Liverpool box.

A minute after this, Liverpool scored through captain Gerrard, who connected with Riise's cross and lofted a header past Dida.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) Soon afterwards, Liverpool scored again as Šmicer beat Dida with a long-range shot into the bottom left-hand corner to leave Liverpool a goal behind. Three minutes after Šmicer's goal, Liverpool were awarded a penalty, after Gerrard made a run into the Milan box for Baros' lay-off and was brought down by [Gennaro Gattuso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gennaro_Gattuso "Gennaro Gattuso"). Alonso's penalty was saved, but he scored from the rebound to equalise for Liverpool. Milan and Liverpool had chances to take the lead after this, but [Clarence Seedorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_Seedorf "Clarence Seedorf") and Riise failed to score.

Milan almost took the lead in the 70th minute, after Dudek dropped a low cross towards Shevchenko, whose effort was cleared off the line by Traoré. Gerrard then had a chance to score but he sent his shot over the crossbar. About ten minutes later García could not control a pass from Gerrard which led to a Milan attack, Crespo played the ball back to Kaka, whose subsequent shot was blocked by Jamie Carragher. A number of substitutions were made before full-time with Liverpool replacing Milan Baroš with Djibril Cissé, while Milan replaced Hernán Crespo and Clarence Seedorf with Jon Dahl Tomasson and [Serginho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serginho_(footballer,_born_1971) "Serginho (footballer, born 1971)") respectively. Milan had the last chance before full-time but Kaka failed to direct [Jaap Stam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Stam "Jaap Stam")'s header towards goal, meaning the final went to [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") for the 13th time in the competition's history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

#### Extra time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Extra time")]

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg/250px-Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jerzy_Dudek_2006.jpg)

Liverpool goalkeeper [Jerzy Dudek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek "Jerzy Dudek") described his second save from [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") in the 117th minute as "the save of my life".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Double_save-33)

Liverpool kicked off the first half of extra time. Pirlo had a chance in the early stages, but he put his shot over the crossbar. Tomasson came close in the later stages of the first period of extra time, but he could not make contact with the ball. Šmicer required treatment for [cramp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramp "Cramp") towards the end of the first period, as a number of Liverpool players felt fatigued. Liverpool had most of the early exchanges after winning two corners, but could not score. Shortly afterwards, Milan made their final substitution, replacing Gennaro Gattuso with [Rui Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rui_Costa "Rui Costa").

The best chance of the second half of extra time came in the 117th minute (three minutes from penalties) when Shevchenko shot at goal. Dudek saved, only for it to rebound back out to Shevchenko, who again shot from under 3 yards (2.7 m), which Dudek saved again, pushing the shot over the bar.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Double_save-33) Liverpool had one last chance at the end of extra time, but John Arne Riise's free kick was blocked, and following this the referee signalled the end of extra time, which meant a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") would decide the championship.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

#### Penalties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Penalties")]

Liverpool and Milan had each won their last European Cups after winning penalty shoot-outs, and it was also the second time in three years that the final would be decided this way; previously, in the [2003 all-Italian final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2003 UEFA Champions League final") at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford"), Milan had defeated Juventus 3–2.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-minute-29) Milan were first to take a penalty, but Serginho – who had taken Milan's first penalty in 2003 and scored – shot over the crossbar after attempts from Dudek to distract him, which mimicked [Bruce Grobbelaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Grobbelaar "Bruce Grobbelaar")'s "spaghetti legs" antics during the shootout in the [1984 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_European_Cup_final "1984 European Cup final") against [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma"). Dietmar Hamann took Liverpool's first penalty and, despite having a broken toe,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34) he scored to put Liverpool 1–0 up. Andrea Pirlo was next for Milan, and his penalty was saved by Dudek who dived low to his right. Cisse then scored his penalty to put Liverpool 2–0 up. Tomasson scored Milan's next penalty to make the score 2–1 in Liverpool's favour. Riise was next for Liverpool, but his penalty was saved by Dida. Kaká then scored the subsequent penalty to level the scores at 2–2. Šmicer took the next Liverpool penalty and scored with his eventual last competitive kick for Liverpool to put them on the brink of victory.

Shevchenko, who had scored the decisive penalty against Juventus' [Gianluigi Buffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Buffon "Gianluigi Buffon") in 2003, then had to score to keep Milan in the shootout.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) He hit his penalty straight down the middle of the goal and Dudek went down to his right, but blocked the shot with his left hand to give Liverpool a 3–2 win in the shoot-out.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-guardian-28)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-clockwatch-32)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Post-match")]

> Liverpool have their hands on the European Cup again, and this time [it's for keeps!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently "European Champion Clubs' Cup") That trophy isn't going anywhere but Anfield. Liverpool become only the third club in the history of the competition to win it five times, and earn the right to keep the cup forever.

—[Clive Tyldesley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Tyldesley "Clive Tyldesley") commentary on [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") as Gerrard lifted the trophy.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-37)

Liverpool's triumph marked their fifth European Cup and the first by an English team since [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") had defeated Bayern Munich in the [1999 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final") in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"). By winning the European Cup for a fifth time, Liverpool earned the privilege of wearing a [multiple-winner badge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Multiple-winner_badge "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and the right to [keep the trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup#Clubs_awarded_the_trophy_permanently "European Champion Clubs' Cup") (under normal competition rules, the winning club can keep the trophy for only 10 months, as they must deliver it to UEFA two months before the next year's final). Liverpool were given ownership of the trophy every winner had held aloft since [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1995 UEFA Champions League final") (after Milan were permanently given the previous trophy after their fifth win in [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final")).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-38) The [2005–06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League "2005–06 UEFA Champions League") participants competed for a new identical trophy. The rule to keep the trophy, which had been in effect since the [1968–69 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968%E2%80%9369_European_Cup "1968–69 European Cup"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) was changed for the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League "2008–09 UEFA Champions League") so that the actual trophy remained with UEFA at all times. Liverpool became the fifth and final club to be given this honour after Real Madrid, Ajax, Bayern Munich and Milan – all of whom had either won at least five times or three times consecutively.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UEFA_honours-40)

[![Image 127](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/CL_parade_Lpool.jpg/250px-CL_parade_Lpool.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CL_parade_Lpool.jpg)

The Liverpool team parading the Champions League trophy in Liverpool city centre after their victory.

Liverpool celebrated their victory by parading the trophy around [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") in an open-top [double-decker bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-decker_bus "Double-decker bus") the day after the final. They were cheered by approximately 1 million supporters, with an estimated 300,000 fans located around [St George's Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_Hall,_Liverpool "St George's Hall, Liverpool") – the final destination of the parade.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Parade-41) Business experts estimated that one in five workers took time off following the victory. It was also estimated that Liverpudlians drank around 10,000 bottles of champagne after the match, with supermarket chain [Sainsbury's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainsbury's "Sainsbury's") stating: "We've never seen anything like it. We would usually expect to sell this much champagne at Christmas".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Parade-41)

[![Image 128](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/2005_European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-2005_European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2005_European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup_(cropped).jpg)

The [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") trophy won by Liverpool in Istanbul, on display in the club's museum a few weeks after the match.

Liverpool manager [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") admitted after the match that the manner of his side's victory had stunned him and he stated: "My problem is that I don't have words to express the things that I feel at this moment".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42) Praise for Liverpool also came from outside England, including from Argentine legend [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona"), who said, "Even the Brazil team that won the [1970 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup") could not have staged a comeback with Milan leading 3–0... The English club proved that miracles really do exist. I've now made Liverpool my English team. They showed that football is the most beautiful sport of all. You knew they could defend, but the team showed they could play too and wrote a page in the history books. The match will last forever. The Liverpool supporters didn't let me go to sleep the night before. There were 10 of them to every three Milan supporters. They showed their unconditional support at half-time when they were losing 3–0 and still they didn't stop singing."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43)[Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff") similarly praised the supporters after the game, saying "There's not one club in Europe with an anthem like "[You'll Never Walk Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You'll_Never_Walk_Alone "You'll Never Walk Alone")." There's not one club in the world so united with the fans. I sat there watching the Liverpool fans and they sent shivers down my spine. A mass of 40,000 people became one force behind their team".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

Benítez was also prepared to break up his winning side after the final with a number of players expected to leave the club to make way for new arrivals. One of those leaving was [Vladimír Šmicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladim%C3%ADr_%C5%A0micer "Vladimír Šmicer"), who had scored Liverpool's second goal in Istanbul, and whose contract was known not to be renewed before the final, meaning he entered knowing the final was his last game for the club. Milan were similarly astonished at the manner in which they had lost the final. Manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") said, "We had six minutes of madness in which we threw away the position we had reached until then".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-shattered-45) The result compounded Milan's failure to win [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") a week before the match. Milan's vice-president, [Adriano Galliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adriano_Galliani "Adriano Galliani"), played down the loss, asserting: "Even if we come second in the league, and second in the Champions League, this is not a disastrous season for us". Captain [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini") was less optimistic, stating that the reverse was a "huge disappointment", but he added that Milan would accept the defeat and "go out with their heads high".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-shattered-45)

Liverpool shirt from the final and a winners medal in the club's museum

Despite winning the competition and the precedent that the holders defend their trophy, Liverpool's place in next season's Champions League was still in doubt. The **2013 FA Cup final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match between [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") and [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on 11 May 2013 at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England, organised by [the Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") (FA). It marked the [132nd final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FA_Cup_Finals "List of FA Cup Finals") of the [Football Association Challenge Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Association_Challenge_Cup "Football Association Challenge Cup") (FA Cup), the world's oldest football cup competition. It was Wigan's first FA Cup final and Manchester City's tenth. En route to the final, Manchester City defeated [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C."), [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C."), [Barnsley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnsley_F.C. "Barnsley F.C.") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."); Wigan Athletic beat [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") (after a [replay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_(sports) "Replay (sports)")), [Macclesfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macclesfield_Town_F.C. "Macclesfield Town F.C."), [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C."), [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") and [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.").

The match [kicked off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-off_(association_football) "Kick-off (association football)") in the early evening in front of 86,254 spectators and was [refereed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") by [Andre Marriner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Marriner "Andre Marriner"). After a goalless first half, Manchester City's [Pablo Zabaleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Zabaleta "Pablo Zabaleta") was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sent_off "Sent off") for a second [yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_card#Yellow_card "Penalty card"), becoming the third player to be sent off in an FA Cup final. One minute into [injury time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury_time "Injury time"), Wigan Athletic won a [corner kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") which was taken by [Shaun Maloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Maloney "Shaun Maloney"): [Ben Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Watson_(footballer,_born_July_1985) "Ben Watson (footballer, born July 1985)") outjumped [Jack Rodwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Rodwell "Jack Rodwell") and [headed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Header_(association_football) "Header (association football)") the ball over [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart"), the Manchester City goalkeeper, and into the goal to secure a 1–0 win. The cup was jointly lifted by playing captain [Emmerson Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmerson_Boyce "Emmerson Boyce") and club captain [Gary Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Caldwell "Gary Caldwell"). Wigan Athletic's [Callum McManaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callum_McManaman "Callum McManaman") was named as [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match "Player of the match").

Manchester City and their semi-final opponent Chelsea had already qualified for the [following season's Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") by virtue of the clubs' league positions. Wigan Athletic secured qualification for the [2013–14 Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League") competition after they had won their semi-final against Millwall. Two days after the final, Manchester City sacked manager [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini"), confirming rumours of his fate before the match. Three days later, Wigan Athletic were [relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_and_relegation "Promotion and relegation") from the Premier League following a 4–1 loss to [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), becoming the first club to win the FA Cup and be relegated from the highest tier of English football in the same season.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The world's oldest football cup competition,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-finals-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-ArsenalManUtdChelseaLiverpool-2) the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup") is an annual [knockout tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knockout_tournament "Knockout tournament") involving professional and amateur men's [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs in the [English football league system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Leary201763-3) The final of the [2012–13 FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_FA_Cup "2012–13 FA Cup") was the 132nd to be played since the tournament was first held in 1872.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-finals-1)[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were making their tenth appearance in an FA Cup final since the club was founded in 1880.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-4) They had won the cup five times (in [1904](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_FA_Cup_final "1904 FA Cup final"), [1934](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1934_FA_Cup_final "1934 FA Cup final"), [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_FA_Cup_final "1956 FA Cup final"), [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_FA_Cup_final "1969 FA Cup final") and [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_FA_Cup_final "2011 FA Cup final")) and were runners-up four times ([1926](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1926_FA_Cup_final "1926 FA Cup final"), [1933](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_FA_Cup_final "1933 FA Cup final"), [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_FA_Cup_final "1955 FA Cup final") and [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_FA_Cup_final "1981 FA Cup final")).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-fafinals-5) Conversely, [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") were making their first appearance in an FA Cup Final since the club was founded in 1932.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-fafinals-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-6)

Manchester City had won both [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") games between the sides during [the regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Premier_League "2012–13 Premier League"). They secured a 2–0 victory at the [DW Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DW_Stadium "DW Stadium") in November 2012 with second-half goals from [Mario Balotelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Balotelli "Mario Balotelli") and [James Milner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Milner "James Milner") and a 1–0 win the following April at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium") after a late goal from [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-8) The final was being played before the last two games of the Premier League season,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-10) with Wigan Athletic in eighteenth place in the league, 40 points behind Manchester City in second position.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-11) Manchester City had beaten Wigan Athletic in each of the most recent seven Premier League matches between the sides.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) City had also beaten Wigan in both of their previous FA Cup ties; two 1–0 home wins back in [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970%E2%80%9371_FA_Cup "1970–71 FA Cup") and [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_FA_Cup "2005–06 FA Cup").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-13)

Wigan Athletic's leading scorer during the regular season was [Arouna Koné](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arouna_Kon%C3%A9 "Arouna Koné") who had 13 goals, 11 in the league and two in the FA Cup.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-14)[Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") led the scoring for Manchester City with 15 goals during the season, including 3 in the FA Cup.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-15)

EDS and Academy") player [Rony Lopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rony_Lopes "Rony Lopes") scored from close range to secure a 3–0 victory for his side.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-17) In doing so, he became the club's youngest ever goalscorer at the age of seventeen years and eight days.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-18) Manchester City progressed to a fourth round match against fellow Premier League side [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. [Yaya Touré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaya_Tour%C3%A9 "Yaya Touré") gave Manchester City the lead in the fifth minute, taking the ball past Leeds United goalkeeper [Jamie Ashdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Ashdown "Jamie Ashdown") and scoring after a pass from Tevez. Agüero then doubled his side's lead when he scored from the [penalty spot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") after he had been fouled by [Tom Lees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Lees "Tom Lees").
