Premier League side Wigan Athletic's FA Cup campaign also began in the third round, in which they faced [League One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_League_One "EFL League One") side [AFC Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") at the DW Stadium. [Roberto Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mart%C3%ADnez "Roberto Martínez") made nine changes to the team that had played in the league four days earlier.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-24)[Eunan O'Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunan_O'Kane "Eunan O'Kane") scored for the visiting side towards the end of the first half with a strike from distance. Wigan Athletic hit the Bournemouth crossbar twice in the second half before they won a penalty after [Simon Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Francis_(footballer) "Simon Francis (footballer)") fouled [Maynor Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maynor_Figueroa "Maynor Figueroa") in the area in the 70th minute. [Shwan Jalal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shwan_Jalal "Shwan Jalal") saved [Jordi Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordi_G%C3%B3mez "Jordi Gómez")'s penalty kick but Gómez scored from the rebound to make it 1–1, and ensured the tie would need to be settled in a [replay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_(sports) "Replay (sports)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-25) At [Dean Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Court "Dean Court") ten days later, the match was settled by a single goal: in the first half, Bournemouth's [Harry Arter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Arter "Harry Arter") conceded possession of the ball to [Mauro Boselli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Boselli "Mauro Boselli") whose shot from around 20 yards (18 m) flew into the top corner of the goal, securing a 1–0 win for Wigan Athletic.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-26) They were drawn against [non-league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") team [Macclesfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macclesfield_Town_F.C. "Macclesfield Town F.C.") in the fourth round. To avoid postponement, snow had to be cleared from the pitch at [Moss Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moss_Rose "Moss Rose") on the morning of the game. Six minutes into the match, [Thierry Audel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Audel "Thierry Audel") fouled [Callum McManaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callum_McManaman "Callum McManaman") in the Macclesfield [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area") and Gómez scored the resulting penalty to give Wigan Athletic the lead. The home side had several opportunities to score, including a header from Audel from 6 yards (5.5 m) which went straight to Wigan Athletic's debutant goalkeeper [Joel Robles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Robles "Joel Robles"). Macclesfield's appeals for a penalty late in the match were turned down by the referee and Wigan Athletic won 1–0. Victory gave them their second appearance in the fifth round of the FA Cup since the founding of the club.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-27)

In the fifth round, Wigan Athletic were drawn away against Championship team [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C."). McManaman gave the visiting side the lead in the 31st minute, shooting into the top corner of the goal after a pass from [James McArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_McArthur "James McArthur"). Five minutes before half-time, Koné doubled his side's lead after Gómez had passed from a McManaman cross before McArthur made it 3–0 when he scored in the 56th minute. [Lee Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Novak "Lee Novak") scored with a header from a [Calum Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Woods "Calum Woods") cross to reduce Huddersfield Town's deficit but with a minute of the match remaining, Koné scored his second to secure a 4–1 win for Wigan Athletic.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-28) Their quarter-final opponents were Premier League side [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") whom they faced at [Goodison Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodison_Park "Goodison Park"). Wigan Athletic scored three goals within four minutes in the first half: just after half an hour, Wigan Athletic's Figueroa opened the scoring when he headed in a corner. McManaman then doubled the lead when a mistake by [Phil Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Neville "Phil Neville") allowed him to take the ball past Everton's goalkeeper [Ján Mucha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1n_Mucha "Ján Mucha") and shoot. Gómez then struck a long-range shot into the Everton goal to make it 3–0, the final score. The win ensured Wigan Athletic would play in the first FA Cup semi-final appearance in the club's history.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-29)

Wigan Athletic's fifth appearance at Wembley Stadium saw them face Championship side [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") in the semi-final. In the first half, Koné's cross found [Shaun Maloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Maloney "Shaun Maloney") who volleyed the ball past [David Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Forde_(footballer) "David Forde (footballer)") in the Millwall goal to give Wigan Athletic the lead. With twelve minutes of the match remaining, Wigan Athletic broke out of defence and Gómez's pass found McManaman who took the ball round Forde to double his side's lead. Wigan Athletic won the match 2–0 and progressed to the first FA Cup final in the club's history.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-30)

Musical and pyrotechnic performance before the match

Before the match, it was reported in _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ that manager [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini")'s job was under threat after he failed to lead Manchester City to a defence of their league title. It was suggested that the [Málaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1laga_CF "Málaga CF") manager [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini") was to be Mancini's successor.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-31) The [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") for the match was [Andre Marriner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Marriner "Andre Marriner") who had officiated at Wembley Stadium twice previously, at the [2010 FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FA_Community_Shield "2010 FA Community Shield") and the [2010 Football League Championship play-off final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Football_League_Championship_play-off_final "2010 Football League Championship play-off final"). He was [assisted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_referee_(association_football) "Assistant referee (association football)") by Stephen Child and Simon Long, [Anthony Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Taylor_(referee) "Anthony Taylor (referee)") was the [fourth official](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_official "Fourth official") and Gary Beswick acted as the [reserve assistant referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_assistant_referee "Reserve assistant referee").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-referee-32)

Manchester City were considered strong favourites to win the match by the British media.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-teleprev-34) Wigan Athletic wore the club's black away [kit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_(association_football) "Kit (association football)") for the final, used the away team dressing room and were allocated the East End of the stadium. Manchester City fans occupied the West End and the team played in their home kit after winning the coin toss to decide who would wear which kit.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-35) Ticket prices for the final started at £45 and were available at £65, £85 and £115, with a £10 discount for concessions.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-36) Manchester City received an initial allocation of 25,000 tickets, later increased to 31,779, and Wigan Athletic requested 21,000 tickets, later increased to a 25,000 allocation.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-38)

Despite expectations in the media that Pantilimon would retain his position as the Manchester City goalkeeper for the final, he was dropped to the substitute's bench in place of [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-teleprev-34)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-39) Before the match, Mancini said "I decided this because I wanted this for this game but it doesn't change anything... We know Costel is a good keeper."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40) Manchester City had no injury problems, Touré being included in the team after suffering from a muscle problem.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-yaya-42) Manchester City made eight changes to the starting line-up from their previous match, a Premier League game against [West Bromwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."); only Hart, Nasri and Tevez keeping their place.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-43)[Antolín Alcaraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antol%C3%ADn_Alcaraz "Antolín Alcaraz") returned to the Wigan Athletic starting lineup after recovering from a [torn hamstring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulled_hamstring "Pulled hamstring") in place of [Gary Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Caldwell "Gary Caldwell"), and Figueroa was ruled out with a groin injury.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-yaya-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-wiganprev-45)[Ben Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Watson_(footballer,_born_July_1985) "Ben Watson (footballer, born July 1985)") dropped to the substitute's bench and was replaced by Gómez.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-wiganprev-45) Wigan Athletic adopted a 3–4–1–2 formation,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-:1-46) and Manchester City played as a [4–2–3–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%932%E2%80%933%E2%80%931 "Formation (association football)").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-timesrep-47)

The kick-off time for the final was 5:15 p.m. as opposed to the traditional 3 p.m. This was controversial, particularly with regard to both sets of supporters facing difficulties in guaranteeing train transport back to the North West of England after the match.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48) The secretary of the Manchester City Supporters Club stated that "Not only does it show that [the FA] don't care but it shows that they don't know", and a spokesperson for the Wigan Athletic Supporters Club noted that "The FA don't think about stuff like young children of four or six years old potentially not getting home till 2 a.m. if they are travelling by coach."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-49) It was also the subject of a cross-party [early day motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_day_motion "Early day motion") in the [House of Commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom "House of Commons of the United Kingdom").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-50)

Wigan Athletic owner [Dave Whelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Whelan "Dave Whelan") led out his team before kick-off along with manager Martínez.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-51) The traditional pre-match anthem, "[Abide with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abide_with_Me "Abide with Me")", was performed by musical quartet Amore alongside the [Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Royal Philharmonic Orchestra"). The [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Save_the_Queen "God Save the Queen") was also performed by Amore with the [Band of the Grenadier Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_of_the_Grenadier_Guards "Band of the Grenadier Guards").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-52) Paralympic footballer [Dave Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Clarke_(Paralympic_footballer) "David Clarke (Paralympic footballer)") and [David Bernstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bernstein_(executive) "David Bernstein (executive)"), chairman of the FA, were introduced to the teams prior to [kick-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-off_(association_football) "Kick-off (association football)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40) In the United Kingdom, the match was televised by [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") and [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Sport_ESPN "BT Sport ESPN").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-referee-32)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: First half")]

Wigan Athletic kicked off the match around 5:15 p.m. in front of a crowd of 86,254.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-53) Two minutes into the game, Zabaleta made a run down the right wing and crossed the ball, which took a deflection before falling to Silva whose volley was blocked by McArthur. Agüero was then fouled by Alcaraz on the edge of the Wigan Athletic penalty area but Tevez's subsequent free kick was blocked with the ball finding Touré whose shot was pushed away by Robles. In the ninth minute, Wigan Athletic's McManaman made a run down the right-hand side of the pitch after a pass from Koné. He cut inside and struck the ball from around 8 yards (7 m), but his shot went wide of the Manchester City post. Wigan Athletic then enjoyed a spell of pressure before Silva's 18th-minute shot for Manchester City was blocked. Midway through the half, Maloney's shot from around 30 yards (27 m) was off-target before [Matija Nastasić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matija_Nastasi%C4%87 "Matija Nastasić") failed to score with a long-range strike for Manchester City. In the 29th minute, Silva passed the ball into the Wigan Athletic penalty area and found Tevez, who stretched to shoot, but Robles made a save with his boot. Tevez's shot from the corner of the Wigan Athletic penalty area was too high before Gomez's strike from 25 yards (23 m) was blocked by Kompany. With nine minutes of the half remaining, Alcaraz ran through the middle of the pitch and passed to McManaman who went round Nastasić, before his shot was blocked by Zabaleta. Nasri's cross was then headed off-target by Silva. In the 41st minute, Zabaleta's shot was blocked but the ball fell to Barry whose curling strike was saved by Robles. Just before half-time, Robles saved Nasri's 20-yard (18 m) shot and the half ended 0–0.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Second half")]

[![Image 8: A packed football stadium with overcast sky in the 63rd minute](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg/250px-Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg)

Play during the second half of the match

Neither side made any changes to their playing personnel during the interval and Manchester City kicked off the second half. Two minutes in, McCarthy's shot was wide before Agüero's attempt to score was defended by [Emmerson Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmerson_Boyce "Emmerson Boyce"). A corner from Barry was then headed onto the roof of the Wigan Athletic net by Kompany. In the 54th minute, Manchester City made the first [substitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") of the game with Milner coming on to replace Nasri. On the hour mark, Zabaleta became the first player of the match to be shown the [yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_card#Yellow_card "Penalty card") after he committed a [professional foul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_foul "Professional foul") on McManaman who had made a break for Wigan Athletic. In the 64th minute, Gomez's shot from 25 yards (23 m) went over the Manchester City crossbar before Kompany tackled McManaman after the Wigan Athletic player had [dribbled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dribbling "Dribbling") past both Silva and [Gaël Clichy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ga%C3%ABl_Clichy "Gaël Clichy"). Five minutes later, [Jack Rodwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Rodwell "Jack Rodwell") was brought on in place of Tevez in Manchester City's second change of the game. In the 72nd minute, [Roger Espinoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Espinoza "Roger Espinoza") fouled Milner who took the resulting free kick himself, from which Rodwell's header was straight at Robles. Nastasić was then booked for a foul on McManaman before Maloney's cross struck the Manchester City crossbar. In the 81st minute, Wigan Athletic made their first substitution, with Ben Watson coming on to replace Gomez. Three minutes later, Kompany received a poor pass from Clichy in the centre circle which Koné intercepted. He passed to McManaman who was fouled by Zabaleta around 30 yards (27 m) from the Manchester City goal. As a result, Zabaleta was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sent_off "Sent off") after receiving a second booking, and became the third player to be dismissed in an FA Cup final. Barry was then shown the yellow card for bringing down Maloney. In the final minute of the match, Wigan Athletic won a corner which was played in by Maloney. Watson beat Rodwell to the ball at the near post and headed it inside the far post of the goal to give Wigan Athletic the lead. Three minutes into stoppage time, Robles was booked for time-wasting and Manchester City brought on [Edin Džeko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edin_D%C5%BEeko "Edin Džeko") for Barry. A minute later, the final whistle was blown and Wigan Athletic had won the match 1–0, securing the FA Cup for the first time in their history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 79](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/David_Sharpe%2C_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png/250px-David_Sharpe%2C_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Sharpe,_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png)

Members of the Wigan Athletic board holding the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup") trophy following their team's victory

The cup was jointly lifted by playing captain Boyce and club captain Caldwell.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-57) Wigan Athletic's McManaman was named [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match "Player of the match").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-man_of_the_match-55) On 20 May, Wigan Athletic had an open-top bus tour of the town to celebrate the FA Cup victory.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-58) Zabaleta became the third player to be sent off in an FA Cup final, after [Kevin Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Moran_(footballer) "Kevin Moran (footballer)") (in the [1985 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_FA_Cup_final "1985 FA Cup final")) and [José Antonio Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Reyes "José Antonio Reyes") (in [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FA_Cup_final "2005 FA Cup final")).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-61) As FA Cup winners, Wigan Athletic received £1.8 million from the FA Cup Prize Fund, and Manchester City earned £900,000.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-62)

[_Sporting Life_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Life_(British_newspaper) "Sporting Life (British newspaper)") described the win as the "biggest FA Cup final shock" since [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimbledon_F.C. "Wimbledon F.C.")'s defeat of [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in the [1988 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_FA_Cup_final "1988 FA Cup final").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-63) Other commentators went further with [Fox Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Sports "Fox Sports"), [BBC Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sport "BBC Sport") and _[FourFourTwo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FourFourTwo "FourFourTwo")_ all saying it was one of the biggest shocks in the competition's history, and [bookmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmaker "Bookmaker")[William Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hill_(bookmaker) "William Hill (bookmaker)") agreeing.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-inside-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-67) In a statistical analysis performed by _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_, the 2013 final was the tenth-biggest "surprise" result in the history of the FA Cup.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-68) European newspapers also commented on the shock result, _[La Gazzetta dello Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Gazzetta\_dello\_Sport "La Gazzetta dello Sport")_, _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Welt "Die Welt")_ and _[Le Figaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Figaro "Le Figaro")_ all noting the historical significance of the event.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-71)

Wigan Athletic lost their next Premier League match, a 4–1 defeat against Arsenal at the [Emirates Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirates_Stadium "Emirates Stadium"), and were consequently [relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_and_relegation "Promotion and relegation") to the Championship. In doing so, they became the first club ever to have won the FA Cup and be relegated from the top tier of English football in the same season.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-72) Mancini was dismissed days after the final with the club owners citing that he had "failed to achieve any of the club's targets, with the exception of qualification for next season's Champions League".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-mansack-73) His assistant, [Brian Kidd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Kidd "Brian Kidd"), took temporary charge of the club and they ended the season with a 2–0 victory at [Reading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_F.C. "Reading F.C.") followed by a 3–2 home defeat by [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") to finish second in the Premier League.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-75)

Because Manchester City and their semi-final opponent Chelsea had already qualified for the following season's [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") by virtue of their league positions, Wigan Athletic had already gained a place in the group stage of the [2013–14 Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League") competition by winning their semi-final match.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-76) They failed to progress to the knockout stage, finishing bottom of [Group D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage#Group_D "2013–14 UEFA Europa League group stage").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-77)

Pellegrini was appointed as the full-time replacement for Mancini in June 2013.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-78) Defender [Joleon Lescott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joleon_Lescott "Joleon Lescott") later reflected that "it was a little bit weird on the morning of the final. We were eating breakfast together and the TVs were on with Sky Sports News reporting that Mancini was going to get sacked".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-inside-64) In early June, Wigan's manager Martínez left the club and joined [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), being replaced at his former club by [Owen Coyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Coyle "Owen Coyle").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-80) The final drew a peak television audience of 9.4 million.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48) Despite the criticism of the early evening kick-off time, the BBC confirmed that subsequent finals would be started at a similar time as part of their new deal to broadcast the final from 2014. However, the broadcaster agreed to schedule the match as the last game of the domestic season.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48)

The clubs would meet in both domestic cups the following season at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium"); City defeated Wigan 5–0 in the [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Football_League_Cup "2013–14 Football League Cup") third round en route to the [title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Football_League_Cup_final "2014 Football League Cup final"), before Wigan defeated City again in the sixth round of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_FA_Cup "2013–14 FA Cup"), winning 2–1,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-81) but failed to retain the trophy after they lost in a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") against eventual winners Arsenal in the semi-final.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-82) They met for another FA Cup tie in the [2017–18 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_FA_Cup "2017–18 FA Cup") where Wigan, then in [League One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_League_One "EFL League One") (the [third tier of English football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system")), won the fifth round tie 1–0 at the [DW Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brick_Community_Stadium "Brick Community Stadium"),[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-83) which was described by BBC Sport as "one of the biggest FA Cup giant-killings".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-84)

The **2013 FA Cup final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match between [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") and [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on 11 May 2013 at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England, organised by [the Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") (FA). It marked the [132nd final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FA_Cup_Finals "List of FA Cup Finals") of the [Football Association Challenge Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Association_Challenge_Cup "Football Association Challenge Cup") (FA Cup), the world's oldest football cup competition. It was Wigan's first FA Cup final and Manchester City's tenth. En route to the final, Manchester City defeated [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C."), [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C."), [Barnsley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnsley_F.C. "Barnsley F.C.") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."); Wigan Athletic beat [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") (after a [replay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_(sports) "Replay (sports)")), [Macclesfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macclesfield_Town_F.C. "Macclesfield Town F.C."), [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C."), [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") and [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.").

The match [kicked off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-off_(association_football) "Kick-off (association football)") in the early evening in front of 86,254 spectators and was [refereed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") by [Andre Marriner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Marriner "Andre Marriner"). After a goalless first half, Manchester City's [Pablo Zabaleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Zabaleta "Pablo Zabaleta") was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sent_off "Sent off") for a second [yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_card#Yellow_card "Penalty card"), becoming the third player to be sent off in an FA Cup final. One minute into [injury time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury_time "Injury time"), Wigan Athletic won a [corner kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") which was taken by [Shaun Maloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Maloney "Shaun Maloney"): [Ben Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Watson_(footballer,_born_July_1985) "Ben Watson (footballer, born July 1985)") outjumped [Jack Rodwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Rodwell "Jack Rodwell") and [headed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Header_(association_football) "Header (association football)") the ball over [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart"), the Manchester City goalkeeper, and into the goal to secure a 1–0 win. The cup was jointly lifted by playing captain [Emmerson Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmerson_Boyce "Emmerson Boyce") and club captain [Gary Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Caldwell "Gary Caldwell"). Wigan Athletic's [Callum McManaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callum_McManaman "Callum McManaman") was named as [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match "Player of the match").

Manchester City and their semi-final opponent Chelsea had already qualified for the [following season's Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") by virtue of the clubs' league positions. Wigan Athletic secured qualification for the [2013–14 Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League") competition after they had won their semi-final against Millwall. Two days after the final, Manchester City sacked manager [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini"), confirming rumours of his fate before the match. Three days later, Wigan Athletic were [relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_and_relegation "Promotion and relegation") from the Premier League following a 4–1 loss to [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), becoming the first club to win the FA Cup and be relegated from the highest tier of English football in the same season.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

The world's oldest football cup competition,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-finals-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-ArsenalManUtdChelseaLiverpool-2) the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup") is an annual [knockout tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knockout_tournament "Knockout tournament") involving professional and amateur men's [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs in the [English football league system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Leary201763-3) The final of the [2012–13 FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_FA_Cup "2012–13 FA Cup") was the 132nd to be played since the tournament was first held in 1872.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-finals-1)[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were making their tenth appearance in an FA Cup final since the club was founded in 1880.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-4) They had won the cup five times (in [1904](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_FA_Cup_final "1904 FA Cup final"), [1934](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1934_FA_Cup_final "1934 FA Cup final"), [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_FA_Cup_final "1956 FA Cup final"), [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_FA_Cup_final "1969 FA Cup final") and [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_FA_Cup_final "2011 FA Cup final")) and were runners-up four times ([1926](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1926_FA_Cup_final "1926 FA Cup final"), [1933](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_FA_Cup_final "1933 FA Cup final"), [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_FA_Cup_final "1955 FA Cup final") and [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_FA_Cup_final "1981 FA Cup final")).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-fafinals-5) Conversely, [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") were making their first appearance in an FA Cup Final since the club was founded in 1932.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-fafinals-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-6)

Manchester City had won both [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") games between the sides during [the regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Premier_League "2012–13 Premier League"). They secured a 2–0 victory at the [DW Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DW_Stadium "DW Stadium") in November 2012 with second-half goals from [Mario Balotelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Balotelli "Mario Balotelli") and [James Milner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Milner "James Milner") and a 1–0 win the following April at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium") after a late goal from [Carlos Tevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Tevez "Carlos Tevez").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-8) The final was being played before the last two games of the Premier League season,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-10) with Wigan Athletic in eighteenth place in the league, 40 points behind Manchester City in second position.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-11) Manchester City had beaten Wigan Athletic in each of the most recent seven Premier League matches between the sides.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-12) City had also beaten Wigan in both of their previous FA Cup ties; two 1–0 home wins back in [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970%E2%80%9371_FA_Cup "1970–71 FA Cup") and [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_FA_Cup "2005–06 FA Cup").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-13)

Wigan Athletic's leading scorer during the regular season was [Arouna Koné](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arouna_Kon%C3%A9 "Arouna Koné") who had 13 goals, 11 in the league and two in the FA Cup.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-14)[Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") led the scoring for Manchester City with 15 goals during the season, including 3 in the FA Cup.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-15)

As a Premier League team, Manchester City entered the 2012–13 FA Cup in the third round, in which they were drawn at home against [EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_Championship "EFL Championship") team [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C."). Midway through the first half, Tevez gave Manchester City the lead with a [free kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_kick_(association_football) "Free kick (association football)") from around 25 yards (23 m). [Costel Pantilimon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costel_Pantilimon "Costel Pantilimon") then saved a [Fernando Forestieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Forestieri "Fernando Forestieri") shot for Watford. One minute before half-time, [Gareth Barry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Barry "Gareth Barry") doubled Manchester City's lead with a [header](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Header_(association_football) "Header (association football)"). In second-half [stoppage time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoppage_time "Stoppage time"), [Manchester City academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C._EDS_and_Academy "Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy") player [Rony Lopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rony_Lopes "Rony Lopes") scored from close range to secure a 3–0 victory for his side.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-17) In doing so, he became the club's youngest ever goalscorer at the age of seventeen years and eight days.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-18) Manchester City progressed to a fourth round match against fellow Premier League side [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") away at the [Britannia Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Stadium "Britannia Stadium"). Despite long spells of possession for the visiting team, the first half ended goalless. [David Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Silva "David Silva") struck the Stoke goalpost and Tevez saw shots saved by the Stoke goalkeeper [Thomas Sørensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_S%C3%B8rensen "Thomas Sørensen"), before [Pablo Zabaleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Zabaleta "Pablo Zabaleta") converted a cross from Agüero with four minutes remaining. Manchester City won the match 1–0 and progressed to the fifth round where they faced Championship side [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") at the City of Manchester Stadium.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-19)

[Yaya Touré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaya_Tour%C3%A9 "Yaya Touré") gave Manchester City the lead in the fifth minute, taking the ball past Leeds United goalkeeper [Jamie Ashdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Ashdown "Jamie Ashdown") and scoring after a pass from Tevez. Agüero then doubled his side's lead when he scored from the [penalty spot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") after he had been fouled by [Tom Lees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Lees "Tom Lees"). Tevez scored Manchester City's third from close range soon after half-time before Agüero scored 15 minutes from the end of the match to secure a 4–0 victory.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-20) In the quarter-final, Manchester City's opponents were Championship club [Barnsley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnsley_F.C. "Barnsley F.C.") at home. Tevez scored the first goal for Manchester City in the eleventh minute after Silva's [volley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volley_(association_football) "Volley (association football)") rebounded off the goalpost. [Aleksandar Kolarov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandar_Kolarov "Aleksandar Kolarov") and Tevez then scored in quick succession to make it 3–0 at half-time. Five minutes after the interval, Tevez completed his [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick#Association_football "Hat-trick"), scoring from [Samir Nasri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Nasri "Samir Nasri")'s pass. Midway through the second half, Silva scored after his initial shot was kept out by Barnsley goalkeeper [Luke Steele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Steele_(footballer) "Luke Steele (footballer)") to make it 5–0, which was the final score.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-21)

In the semi-final, Manchester City faced defending FA Cup champions [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") for the first time in the competition since 1971, the match being held at Wembley, a [neutral venue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutral_venue "Neutral venue").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-22) Ten minutes before half-time, Manchester City took the lead. Agüero's shot bounced off Chelsea's defender [César Azpilicueta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Azpilicueta "César Azpilicueta") and the ball fell to Nasri who scored. [Vincent Kompany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Kompany "Vincent Kompany") then shot off-target shortly before half-time, and two minutes after the interval Barry's cross found Agüero, who headed the ball into the Chelsea goal off the post while goalkeeper [Petr Čech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_%C4%8Cech "Petr Čech") remained motionless. [Demba Ba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demba_Ba "Demba Ba") then scored past Pantilimon to reduce the deficit for Chelsea but the match ended 2–1 and Manchester City progressed to the final.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-23)

Premier League side Wigan Athletic's FA Cup campaign also began in the third round, in which they faced [League One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_League_One "EFL League One") side [AFC Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") at the DW Stadium. [Roberto Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mart%C3%ADnez "Roberto Martínez") made nine changes to the team that had played in the league four days earlier.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-24)[Eunan O'Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunan_O'Kane "Eunan O'Kane") scored for the visiting side towards the end of the first half with a strike from distance. Wigan Athletic hit the Bournemouth crossbar twice in the second half before they won a penalty after [Simon Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Francis_(footballer) "Simon Francis (footballer)") fouled [Maynor Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maynor_Figueroa "Maynor Figueroa") in the area in the 70th minute. [Shwan Jalal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shwan_Jalal "Shwan Jalal") saved [Jordi Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordi_G%C3%B3mez "Jordi Gómez")'s penalty kick but Gómez scored from the rebound to make it 1–1, and ensured the tie would need to be settled in a [replay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_(sports) "Replay (sports)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-25) At [Dean Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Court "Dean Court") ten days later, the match was settled by a single goal: in the first half, Bournemouth's [Harry Arter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Arter "Harry Arter") conceded possession of the ball to [Mauro Boselli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Boselli "Mauro Boselli") whose shot from around 20 yards (18 m) flew into the top corner of the goal, securing a 1–0 win for Wigan Athletic.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-26) They were drawn against [non-league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") team [Macclesfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macclesfield_Town_F.C. "Macclesfield Town F.C.") in the fourth round. To avoid postponement, snow had to be cleared from the pitch at [Moss Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moss_Rose "Moss Rose") on the morning of the game. Six minutes into the match, [Thierry Audel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Audel "Thierry Audel") fouled [Callum McManaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callum_McManaman "Callum McManaman") in the Macclesfield [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area") and Gómez scored the resulting penalty to give Wigan Athletic the lead. The home side had several opportunities to score, including a header from Audel from 6 yards (5.5 m) which went straight to Wigan Athletic's debutant goalkeeper [Joel Robles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Robles "Joel Robles"). Macclesfield's appeals for a penalty late in the match were turned down by the referee and Wigan Athletic won 1–0. Victory gave them their second appearance in the fifth round of the FA Cup since the founding of the club.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-27)

In the fifth round, Wigan Athletic were drawn away against Championship team [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C."). McManaman gave the visiting side the lead in the 31st minute, shooting into the top corner of the goal after a pass from [James McArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_McArthur "James McArthur"). Five minutes before half-time, Koné doubled his side's lead after Gómez had passed from a McManaman cross before McArthur made it 3–0 when he scored in the 56th minute. [Lee Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Novak "Lee Novak") scored with a header from a [Calum Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Woods "Calum Woods") cross to reduce Huddersfield Town's deficit but with a minute of the match remaining, Koné scored his second to secure a 4–1 win for Wigan Athletic.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-28) Their quarter-final opponents were Premier League side [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") whom they faced at [Goodison Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodison_Park "Goodison Park"). Wigan Athletic scored three goals within four minutes in the first half: just after half an hour, Wigan Athletic's Figueroa opened the scoring when he headed in a corner. McManaman then doubled the lead when a mistake by [Phil Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Neville "Phil Neville") allowed him to take the ball past Everton's goalkeeper [Ján Mucha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1n_Mucha "Ján Mucha") and shoot. Gómez then struck a long-range shot into the Everton goal to make it 3–0, the final score. The win ensured Wigan Athletic would play in the first FA Cup semi-final appearance in the club's history.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-29)

Wigan Athletic's fifth appearance at Wembley Stadium saw them face Championship side [Millwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") in the semi-final. In the first half, Koné's cross found [Shaun Maloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Maloney "Shaun Maloney") who volleyed the ball past [David Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Forde_(footballer) "David Forde (footballer)") in the Millwall goal to give Wigan Athletic the lead. With twelve minutes of the match remaining, Wigan Athletic broke out of defence and Gómez's pass found McManaman who took the ball round Forde to double his side's lead. Wigan Athletic won the match 2–0 and progressed to the first FA Cup final in the club's history.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-30)

### Pre-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Pre-match")]

[![Image 6: Roberto Mancini](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Roberto_Mancini_-_Lech_-_Manchester_005_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Roberto_Mancini_-_Lech_-_Manchester_005_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Roberto_Mancini_-_Lech_-_Manchester_005_(cropped).jpg)

Manchester City's manager Roberto Mancini's position was a matter of speculation before the final.

[![Image 7: A football stadium with scores of perfomers and smoke machines on the feild](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Opening_ceremony_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg/250px-Opening_ceremony_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Opening_ceremony_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg)

Musical and pyrotechnic performance before the match

Before the match, it was reported in _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ that manager [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini")'s job was under threat after he failed to lead Manchester City to a defence of their league title. It was suggested that the [Málaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1laga_CF "Málaga CF") manager [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini") was to be Mancini's successor.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-31) The [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") for the match was [Andre Marriner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Marriner "Andre Marriner") who had officiated at Wembley Stadium twice previously, at the [2010 FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FA_Community_Shield "2010 FA Community Shield") and the [2010 Football League Championship play-off final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Football_League_Championship_play-off_final "2010 Football League Championship play-off final"). He was [assisted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_referee_(association_football) "Assistant referee (association football)") by Stephen Child and Simon Long, [Anthony Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Taylor_(referee) "Anthony Taylor (referee)") was the [fourth official](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_official "Fourth official") and Gary Beswick acted as the [reserve assistant referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_assistant_referee "Reserve assistant referee").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-referee-32)

Manchester City were considered strong favourites to win the match by the British media.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-teleprev-34) Wigan Athletic wore the club's black away [kit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_(association_football) "Kit (association football)") for the final, used the away team dressing room and were allocated the East End of the stadium. Manchester City fans occupied the West End and the team played in their home kit after winning the coin toss to decide who would wear which kit.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-35) Ticket prices for the final started at £45 and were available at £65, £85 and £115, with a £10 discount for concessions.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-36) Manchester City received an initial allocation of 25,000 tickets, later increased to 31,779, and Wigan Athletic requested 21,000 tickets, later increased to a 25,000 allocation.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-38)

Despite expectations in the media that Pantilimon would retain his position as the Manchester City goalkeeper for the final, he was dropped to the substitute's bench in place of [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-teleprev-34)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-39) Before the match, Mancini said "I decided this because I wanted this for this game but it doesn't change anything... We know Costel is a good keeper."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40) Manchester City had no injury problems, Touré being included in the team after suffering from a muscle problem.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-yaya-42) Manchester City made eight changes to the starting line-up from their previous match, a Premier League game against [West Bromwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."); only Hart, Nasri and Tevez keeping their place.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-43)[Antolín Alcaraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antol%C3%ADn_Alcaraz "Antolín Alcaraz") returned to the Wigan Athletic starting lineup after recovering from a [torn hamstring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulled_hamstring "Pulled hamstring") in place of [Gary Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Caldwell "Gary Caldwell"), and Figueroa was ruled out with a groin injury.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-yaya-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-wiganprev-45)[Ben Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Watson_(footballer,_born_July_1985) "Ben Watson (footballer, born July 1985)") dropped to the substitute's bench and was replaced by Gómez.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-wiganprev-45) Wigan Athletic adopted a 3–4–1–2 formation,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-:1-46) and Manchester City played as a [4–2–3–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%932%E2%80%933%E2%80%931 "Formation (association football)").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-timesrep-47)

The kick-off time for the final was 5:15 p.m. as opposed to the traditional 3 p.m. This was controversial, particularly with regard to both sets of supporters facing difficulties in guaranteeing train transport back to the North West of England after the match.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48) The secretary of the Manchester City Supporters Club stated that "Not only does it show that [the FA] don't care but it shows that they don't know", and a spokesperson for the Wigan Athletic Supporters Club noted that "The FA don't think about stuff like young children of four or six years old potentially not getting home till 2 a.m. if they are travelling by coach."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-49) It was also the subject of a cross-party [early day motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_day_motion "Early day motion") in the [House of Commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom "House of Commons of the United Kingdom").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-50)

Wigan Athletic owner [Dave Whelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Whelan "Dave Whelan") led out his team before kick-off along with manager Martínez.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-51) The traditional pre-match anthem, "[Abide with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abide_with_Me "Abide with Me")", was performed by musical quartet Amore alongside the [Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Royal Philharmonic Orchestra"). The [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Save_the_Queen "God Save the Queen") was also performed by Amore with the [Band of the Grenadier Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_of_the_Grenadier_Guards "Band of the Grenadier Guards").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-52) Paralympic footballer [Dave Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Clarke_(Paralympic_footballer) "David Clarke (Paralympic footballer)") and [David Bernstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bernstein_(executive) "David Bernstein (executive)"), chairman of the FA, were introduced to the teams prior to [kick-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-off_(association_football) "Kick-off (association football)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40) In the United Kingdom, the match was televised by [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") and [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Sport_ESPN "BT Sport ESPN").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-referee-32)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: First half")]

Wigan Athletic kicked off the match around 5:15 p.m. in front of a crowd of 86,254.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-53) Two minutes into the game, Zabaleta made a run down the right wing and crossed the ball, which took a deflection before falling to Silva whose volley was blocked by McArthur. Agüero was then fouled by Alcaraz on the edge of the Wigan Athletic penalty area but Tevez's subsequent free kick was blocked with the ball finding Touré whose shot was pushed away by Robles. In the ninth minute, Wigan Athletic's McManaman made a run down the right-hand side of the pitch after a pass from Koné. He cut inside and struck the ball from around 8 yards (7 m), but his shot went wide of the Manchester City post. Wigan Athletic then enjoyed a spell of pressure before Silva's 18th-minute shot for Manchester City was blocked. Midway through the half, Maloney's shot from around 30 yards (27 m) was off-target before [Matija Nastasić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matija_Nastasi%C4%87 "Matija Nastasić") failed to score with a long-range strike for Manchester City. In the 29th minute, Silva passed the ball into the Wigan Athletic penalty area and found Tevez, who stretched to shoot, but Robles made a save with his boot. Tevez's shot from the corner of the Wigan Athletic penalty area was too high before Gomez's strike from 25 yards (23 m) was blocked by Kompany. With nine minutes of the half remaining, Alcaraz ran through the middle of the pitch and passed to McManaman who went round Nastasić, before his shot was blocked by Zabaleta. Nasri's cross was then headed off-target by Silva. In the 41st minute, Zabaleta's shot was blocked but the ball fell to Barry whose curling strike was saved by Robles. Just before half-time, Robles saved Nasri's 20-yard (18 m) shot and the half ended 0–0.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Second half")]

[![Image 8: A packed football stadium with overcast sky in the 63rd minute](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg/250px-Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Play_during_the_FA_Cup_Final_2013.jpg)

Play during the second half of the match

Neither side made any changes to their playing personnel during the interval and Manchester City kicked off the second half. Two minutes in, McCarthy's shot was wide before Agüero's attempt to score was defended by [Emmerson Boyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmerson_Boyce "Emmerson Boyce"). A corner from Barry was then headed onto the roof of the Wigan Athletic net by Kompany. In the 54th minute, Manchester City made the first [substitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") of the game with Milner coming on to replace Nasri. On the hour mark, Zabaleta became the first player of the match to be shown the [yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_card#Yellow_card "Penalty card") after he committed a [professional foul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_foul "Professional foul") on McManaman who had made a break for Wigan Athletic. In the 64th minute, Gomez's shot from 25 yards (23 m) went over the Manchester City crossbar before Kompany tackled McManaman after the Wigan Athletic player had [dribbled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dribbling "Dribbling") past both Silva and [Gaël Clichy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ga%C3%ABl_Clichy "Gaël Clichy"). Five minutes later, [Jack Rodwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Rodwell "Jack Rodwell") was brought on in place of Tevez in Manchester City's second change of the game. In the 72nd minute, [Roger Espinoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Espinoza "Roger Espinoza") fouled Milner who took the resulting free kick himself, from which Rodwell's header was straight at Robles. Nastasić was then booked for a foul on McManaman before Maloney's cross struck the Manchester City crossbar. In the 81st minute, Wigan Athletic made their first substitution, with Ben Watson coming on to replace Gomez. Three minutes later, Kompany received a poor pass from Clichy in the centre circle which Koné intercepted. He passed to McManaman who was fouled by Zabaleta around 30 yards (27 m) from the Manchester City goal. As a result, Zabaleta was [sent off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sent_off "Sent off") after receiving a second booking, and became the third player to be dismissed in an FA Cup final. Barry was then shown the yellow card for bringing down Maloney. In the final minute of the match, Wigan Athletic won a corner which was played in by Maloney. Watson beat Rodwell to the ball at the near post and headed it inside the far post of the goal to give Wigan Athletic the lead. Three minutes into stoppage time, Robles was booked for time-wasting and Manchester City brought on [Edin Džeko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edin_D%C5%BEeko "Edin Džeko") for Barry. A minute later, the final whistle was blown and Wigan Athletic had won the match 1–0, securing the FA Cup for the first time in their history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-guardasit-40)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 79](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/David_Sharpe%2C_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png/250px-David_Sharpe%2C_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Sharpe,_Paul_Sharpe_and_David_Whelan_holding_FA_cup.png)

Members of the Wigan Athletic board holding the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup") trophy following their team's victory

The cup was jointly lifted by playing captain Boyce and club captain Caldwell.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-57) Wigan Athletic's McManaman was named [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match "Player of the match").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-man_of_the_match-55) On 20 May, Wigan Athletic had an open-top bus tour of the town to celebrate the FA Cup victory.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-58) Zabaleta became the third player to be sent off in an FA Cup final, after [Kevin Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Moran_(footballer) "Kevin Moran (footballer)") (in the [1985 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_FA_Cup_final "1985 FA Cup final")) and [José Antonio Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Reyes "José Antonio Reyes") (in [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FA_Cup_final "2005 FA Cup final")).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-61) As FA Cup winners, Wigan Athletic received £1.8 million from the FA Cup Prize Fund, and Manchester City earned £900,000.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-62)

[_Sporting Life_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Life_(British_newspaper) "Sporting Life (British newspaper)") described the win as the "biggest FA Cup final shock" since [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimbledon_F.C. "Wimbledon F.C.")'s defeat of [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in the [1988 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_FA_Cup_final "1988 FA Cup final").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-63) Other commentators went further with [Fox Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Sports "Fox Sports"), [BBC Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sport "BBC Sport") and _[FourFourTwo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FourFourTwo "FourFourTwo")_ all saying it was one of the biggest shocks in the competition's history, and [bookmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmaker "Bookmaker")[William Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hill_(bookmaker) "William Hill (bookmaker)") agreeing.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-inside-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-67) In a statistical analysis performed by _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_, the 2013 final was the tenth-biggest "surprise" result in the history of the FA Cup.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-68) European newspapers also commented on the shock result, _[La Gazzetta dello Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Gazzetta\_dello\_Sport "La Gazzetta dello Sport")_, _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Welt "Die Welt")_ and _[Le Figaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Figaro "Le Figaro")_ all noting the historical significance of the event.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-71)

Wigan Athletic lost their next Premier League match, a 4–1 defeat against Arsenal at the [Emirates Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirates_Stadium "Emirates Stadium"), and were consequently [relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_and_relegation "Promotion and relegation") to the Championship. In doing so, they became the first club ever to have won the FA Cup and be relegated from the top tier of English football in the same season.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-72) Mancini was dismissed days after the final with the club owners citing that he had "failed to achieve any of the club's targets, with the exception of qualification for next season's Champions League".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-mansack-73) His assistant, [Brian Kidd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Kidd "Brian Kidd"), took temporary charge of the club and they ended the season with a 2–0 victory at [Reading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_F.C. "Reading F.C.") followed by a 3–2 home defeat by [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") to finish second in the Premier League.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-75)

Because Manchester City and their semi-final opponent Chelsea had already qualified for the following season's [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") by virtue of their league positions, Wigan Athletic had already gained a place in the group stage of the [2013–14 Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League "2013–14 UEFA Europa League") competition by winning their semi-final match.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-76) They failed to progress to the knockout stage, finishing bottom of [Group D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage#Group_D "2013–14 UEFA Europa League group stage").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-77)

Pellegrini was appointed as the full-time replacement for Mancini in June 2013.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-78) Defender [Joleon Lescott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joleon_Lescott "Joleon Lescott") later reflected that "it was a little bit weird on the morning of the final. We were eating breakfast together and the TVs were on with Sky Sports News reporting that Mancini was going to get sacked".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-inside-64) In early June, Wigan's manager Martínez left the club and joined [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), being replaced at his former club by [Owen Coyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Coyle "Owen Coyle").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-80) The final drew a peak television audience of 9.4 million.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48) Despite the criticism of the early evening kick-off time, the BBC confirmed that subsequent finals would be started at a similar time as part of their new deal to broadcast the final from 2014. However, the broadcaster agreed to schedule the match as the last game of the domestic season.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-times-48)

The clubs would meet in both domestic cups the following season at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium"); City defeated Wigan 5–0 in the [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Football_League_Cup "2013–14 Football League Cup") third round en route to the [title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Football_League_Cup_final "2014 Football League Cup final"), before Wigan defeated City again in the sixth round of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_FA_Cup "2013–14 FA Cup"), winning 2–1,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-81) but failed to retain the trophy after they lost in a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") against eventual winners Arsenal in the semi-final.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-82) They met for another FA Cup tie in the [2017–18 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_FA_Cup "2017–18 FA Cup") where Wigan, then in [League One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_League_One "EFL League One") (the [third tier of English football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system")), won the fifth round tie 1–0 at the [DW Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brick_Community_Stadium "Brick Community Stadium"),[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-83) which was described by BBC Sport as "one of the biggest FA Cup giant-killings".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-84)
